verdictVsMk8: Blind side-by-side, this loses badly and for a diagnosable reason: the karts are not lit like objects, they are lit like decals. Every kart in every frame is pure diffuse toon + a weak fresnel rim, with no specular event anywhere — MK8's karts sell mass because a hard highlight slides across glossy paint while the tires stay matte and the trim flashes chrome, and none of those three material classes are separable here. Worse, two things read as outright bugs: the authored GLB bodies (6 of 7 kart options, including the default Hero Kart) have no rotating wheels at all because `replaceBody` deletes the procedural wheel groups and then looks for Kenney node names that do not exist in those files, and the blob shadow is parented to the transformed outer group so it hops, rolls and squashes with the kart instead of staying on the road. The silhouette work is actually decent (chunky proportions, good roster variety in comeback-city-p0_45) but the shading, contact and driver integration are all one generation behind MK8.

findings.title: Authored GLB karts have ZERO rotating wheels — the default Hero Kart drives at 289 km/h on frozen tires
findings.evidence: src/game/ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:772-787 `replaceBody` disposes every child of `bodyGroup` (which is where the four procedural wheel Groups were added, line 597-616), does `wheels.length = 0`, then repopulates `wheels[]` only from `KENNEY_WHEEL_NODES` ('wheel-fl'…'wheel-br', line 1407). `attachTripoKartBody` (line 1525-1553) calls `replaceBody(rig)` with a single fused Tripo/Meshy mesh that has no such nodes — its own comment at 1524 admits 'no wheel nodes, so wheels are static'. Every entry in `KART_NOSE_YAW` (line 226-233: hero, icesled, iceracer, miamicruiser, iceblock, btckart) takes that path, i.e. 6 of the 7 `KART_OPTIONS` including the gate default `hero`. The frame loop at 6135-6138 (`engine.playerModel.wheels.forEach`) therefore iterates an empty array. Visible in penguin-village-p0_78 (Ice Sled, wheels are painted-on slabs) and comeback-city-p0_67 (Ice Racer at 289 km/h).
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 wheel rotation is the primary speed cue on the player kart — it is the one thing that never stops moving in the lower third of frame. A kart whose wheels are welded reads as a sliding prop, which is exactly the 'flat toy' failure this pillar is judged on. MK8 additionally blurs the rim spokes above ~120cc so the wheel reads as a disc of motion, never as a static texture.
findings.fix: In `createGroundedKartModel` (src/game/ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:489), move the four wheel Groups OUT of `bodyGroup` and into a sibling `wheelRig` Group added to `model` (same treatment `boostFlame`/`idleFlames` already get at line 578-583 so they survive the swap). Change `replaceBody` (772) to NOT clear `wheels[]` unconditionally: keep the procedural wheels as the default, and only swap to GLB nodes when `KENNEY_WHEEL_NODES` actually resolve (`const found = KENNEY_WHEEL_NODES.map(n => rig.getObjectByName(n)).filter(Boolean); if (found.length === 4) { wheelRig.visible = false; wheels.length = 0; wheels.push(...found) }`). Then in `attachTripoKartBody` (1525), after `rig.position.y -= fitted.min.y`, re-seat the procedural wheel rig to the fused body's footprint: `wheelRig.position.set(0,0,0); wheelRig.scale.setScalar((fitted.max.x - fitted.min.x) / 9.2)` and place the four wheels at ±0.42×bodyWidth, z = ±0.34×bodyLength, y = tireRadius. Add a per-kart `wheelOffsets` override in `KART_OPTIONS` for the two karts (iceblock, icesled) whose fused bodies already sculpt wheel wells.

findings.title: Blob shadow is parented to the transformed group — it hops, rolls, pitches and squashes with the kart instead of staying on the road
findings.evidence: src/game/ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:723-736 adds `shadow` (a `CircleGeometry`, `MeshBasicMaterial` #03060c) to the OUTER `group`. `updateVehiclePose` (5362-5374) then writes to that same group: `group.position.y += 0.05 + (pose?.hop || 0)` (5364), `group.rotation.z = -(slideYaw*0.3 + steer*0.1)` (5370), `group.rotation.x = …pitch` (5371), `group.scale.y = pose.squash` (5373). So every hop (drift hop, ramp air, shortcut arc), every drift roll and every landing squash drags the shadow off the ground plane and tilts it out of the road. The code comment at 5384-5385 claims 'the outer group, whose blob shadow must stay glued to the road' — the intent is documented and the implementation contradicts it. The contact ellipse is visible detaching under the Ice Racer in comeback-city-p0_9 and sitting as a hard-edged dark polygon in penguin-village-p0_56.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8's kart shadow is the entire grounding contract: it stays flat on the surface, shrinks and lightens as the kart leaves the ground, and snaps back on landing. That decoupling is what makes an MK8 hop read as a jump rather than a scale animation. Here the shadow is rigidly welded to the kart, so airtime has no visual cost and the kart never looks like it is touching anything.
findings.fix: Split the contact set off the transformed group. In `createGroundedKartModel` create `const contactGroup = new THREE.Group()` and add `shadow` + `contactGlow` + the underglow sprite to it; return `contactGroup` alongside `group`, and add it to `world` as a SIBLING of `group` (not a child). In the frame loop, after `updateVehiclePose`, drive it from the surface sample only: `contactGroup.position.copy(sample.point); contactGroup.position.y = sample.point.y + 0.07; contactGroup.rotation.set(-Math.PI/2, 0, 0)` (align to the track normal via `sample.normal` if the sampler exposes one), `contactGroup.rotation.z` from the kart yaw only. Then fade with airtime: `const airT = clamp((pose.hop || 0) / 6, 0, 1); shadow.material.opacity = 0.34 * (1 - airT * 0.75); shadow.scale.setScalar(1 - airT * 0.35)`. Same treatment in the rival branch (6205-6215).

findings.title: No specular response on any kart — glossy paint, matte rubber and metallic trim are visually identical
findings.evidence: Every kart surface is either `MeshToonMaterial` (src/game/ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:1295-1302 `createToonMaterial`, used for body/black/tire/hub/trim/seat at 511-516; and `attachTripoKartBody` 1527-1534, `attachAuthoredKartBody` 1558, `mountDriverAvatar` 1424-1430) or `MeshStandardMaterial` with `metalness: 0.02, roughness: 0.68` (src/game/city3dAssets.js:60-67 / src/game/race/render/createKartModel.js:9-16). `MeshToonMaterial` has no specular term at all, and `grep -n 'envMap|PMREMGenerator|environment'` across the whole race runtime returns zero hits — so `metalness` is meaningless too. The only lighting variation the karts get is the 4-band diffuse ramp (900-919) plus the fresnel rim (toonRimShader.js:21-23). Result: in comeback-city-p0_06 the red hero kart body, its black tires and its white trim all read as the same plastic; in penguin-village-p0_78 the Ice Sled is a flat pale-blue slab with no form.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8's single most identifiable kart cue is the hard specular streak that sweeps along the cowl and the wheel rims as the kart yaws under the sun — glossy body, dead-matte tire, hot chrome exhaust. That contrast between three material classes is what makes MK8 karts read as physical objects at 200cc. This game has exactly one material class.
findings.fix: Add a second injection to /Users/andrewferguson/Downloads/comeback-tracker/src/game/race/render/toonRimShader.js next to `applyToonRim`: `applyToonSpecular(material, { gloss, tint, steps })`, composed through the existing `addShaderInjection` registry (do NOT assign `onBeforeCompile` directly). Fragment pars: `uniform vec3 uSpecColor; uniform float uSpecGloss; uniform float uSpecStrength;`. Fragment chunk at the same `#include <opaque_fragment>` anchor, using symbols already in scope from `lights_fragment_begin`: `vec3 specH = normalize(geometryViewDir + normalize(vec3(-64.0, 98.0, -54.0)));` (the `sun` direction from createRaceScene.js:108) `float specNdH = saturate(dot(geometryNormal, specH)); float specTerm = pow(specNdH, uSpecGloss); specTerm = smoothstep(0.42, 0.52, specTerm);` (the smoothstep is what makes it a stepped cel highlight rather than a PBR blob) `outgoingLight += uSpecColor * uSpecStrength * specTerm;`. Apply three presets in `createGroundedKartModel` and in `attachTripoKartBody`/`attachAuthoredKartBody`: PAINT `{gloss: 28, strength: 0.55, tint: palette.rimLightColor}` on body/cowl, TRIM/CHROME `{gloss: 90, strength: 1.1, tint: '#ffffff'}` on hubs, exhaust pipes and the roll cage, and RUBBER = no injection at all (tires stay pure matte, which is the contrast). Zero bytes, one extra uniform block, no new draw calls.

findings.title: Authored kart bodies lost their tail lights, brake lights and rear light bar in the body swap
findings.evidence: The rear light bar `addPart(box(4.2, 0.42, 0.26, createBasicMaterial('#ff4a3d', { emissive:'#ff4a3d', emissiveIntensity: 1.0 })), 0, 2.95, -5.2)` and the front headlight strip (line 545-547) are added via `addPart`, which pushes into `bodyGroup` (519-524). `replaceBody` (772-779) disposes and clears `bodyGroup` wholesale, so every authored kart — the entire shipped roster — loses them. Only `idleFlames` survived (they were deliberately added to `model`, line 578-583, per the comment at 576-577). Confirm in comeback-city-p0_06 and penguin-village-p0_15: the player kart's rear face is a dark silhouette with no emissive anchor whatsoever, against a dark blue road, in a game whose camera is permanently behind the kart.
findings.whyMk8Wins: Every MK8 kart carries hot emissive tail lamps and exhaust tips that stay legible at the darkest point of Neon Lights / Big Blue. They are the reason the rear three-quarter view — which is 100% of gameplay framing — never goes to mush. Here the player's own kart is the darkest object on screen in comeback-city-p0_06.
findings.fix: Build a `lightRig` Group in `createGroundedKartModel`, added to `model` (NOT `bodyGroup`) so it survives `replaceBody`, containing: a rear bar `BoxGeometry(4.2, 0.34, 0.22)` with `MeshBasicMaterial({ color:'#ff4a3d', toneMapped:false })`, two round lamps `CircleGeometry(0.55, 12)` at x ±2.1, and two forward-facing headlight quads in the accent color. In `attachTripoKartBody` (1525) / `attachAuthoredKartBody` (1556), after the `fitted` box is computed, re-seat the rig from the measured body: `lightRig.position.set(0, (fitted.max.y - fitted.min.y) * 0.42, fitted.min.z + 0.15)` for the rear set and `fitted.max.z - 0.15` for the front. Drive brightness in the frame loop next to the existing `idleFlames` block (6139-6144): `const braking = race.speed < prevSpeed - 8; rearMat.color.setHex(braking ? 0xff2a18 : 0xff4a3d); rearMat.opacity = braking ? 1.0 : 0.6`. Emissive-only `MeshBasicMaterial` with `toneMapped:false` puts them above the bloom `luminanceThreshold: 1.0` (line 4001) so they bloom for free.

findings.title: Wheel spin rate aliases into a backwards crawl at race speed
findings.evidence: src/game/ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:6135-6138 `wheel.rotation.x -= dt * race.speed * 0.12`. At the speeds the manifest actually records (tmp/aaa-visual/baseline/capture-manifest.json: 285, 287, 289 on comeback-city) and dt = 1/60, that is 289 × 0.12 / 60 = 0.578 rad = 33.1° per frame. The procedural tire is a `LatheGeometry` with 10 radial segments (line 592) = 36° rotational symmetry, and the hub is `CylinderGeometry(..., 9)` = 40°. 33° per frame against a 36° period reads as −3°/frame: the wheel appears to rotate slowly BACKWARDS. The same constant drives rivals at 6209-6211. The rate is also not derived from tire radius, so it is arbitrary at every speed.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 never lets a wheel alias: above a speed threshold the tire swaps to a radially-blurred material so it reads as a solid spinning disc, and the visible rotation rate is decoupled from the true angular velocity. The result is that MK8 wheels always look fast; here they look broken or stalled.
findings.fix: Two changes in the frame loop (6135-6138 and 6209-6211). (1) Derive from radius and clamp to a perceptual ceiling below the Nyquist limit of the geometry: `const TIRE_R = 2.5; const MAX_VIS_RATE = (Math.PI * 2 / 10) * 0.45 * 60; // ~0.28 rad/frame` then `wheel.rotation.x -= dt * Math.min(race.speed / TIRE_R, MAX_VIS_RATE)`. (2) Above `race.speed > 140`, blend the tire toward a spin-blur read at zero cost: keep a second pre-made material on `tire.userData.blurMat` — same toon material but with a 64×64 canvas `map` of concentric grey rings generated once (the same `makeQuestionTexture`/canvas pattern already used at line ~810), `map.wrapS = RepeatWrapping`, and simply swap `tire.material` on threshold crossing. Bump the lathe segment count 10 → 14 (line 592) at the same time; the geometry is shared across all four wheels so it costs ~48 extra triangles per kart total.

findings.title: Drivers are standing rigs dropped onto an arbitrary mount height — no seated pose, no hands on the wheel, no legs
findings.evidence: `mountDriverAvatar` (src/game/ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:1420-1447) takes whatever pose the GLB was authored in, normalizes it to `height` (5.7–6.4 from `KART_CHARACTERS.driverHeight`, line 185-196), and seats it with `rig.position.y -= fitted.min.y` — i.e. the rig's FEET land on the mount plane. `attachTripoKartBody` then puts that plane at `kartModel.driverMount.position.set(0, (fitted.max.y - fitted.min.y) * 0.58, -1.9)` (1552) — a hardcoded 58% of body height with no relation to where the GLB's seat actually is. In comeback-city-p0_67 the CRRT Bunny reads as a standing figure balanced on the cowl, its lower body simply absent; in penguin-village-p0_9 the rival driver's torso floats clear of the seat; in comeback-city-p0_06 the driver is a black blob hovering above the chassis with a visible gap.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 characters are physically bound to the kart: hands gripping the wheel, elbows in, torso pinned into the bucket, and they visibly counter-steer and brace. That binding is what sells the kart+driver as one object rather than two props sharing a transform. Here they share a transform and nothing else.
findings.fix: Three steps, all zero-byte. (1) Replace the `0.58` guess with a measured seat anchor: add a `seatY` field per kart in `KART_OPTIONS` (fraction of body height) OR probe the fused mesh — raycast straight down from `fitted.max.y` at (0, −0.15 × length) and use the first hit's y as the mount plane. (2) Change `mountDriverAvatar` to seat rather than stand: after the fit, apply a static seated pose by splitting the rig at its hip height — `rig.position.y -= fitted.min.y + size.y * 0.34` so the hips (not the feet) land on the seat, and clip the legs with a per-material `clippingPlanes: [new THREE.Plane(new THREE.Vector3(0,1,0), -hipWorldY)]` plus `renderer.localClippingEnabled = true`. (3) Add hands: two `SphereGeometry(0.28, 8, 6)` meshes in the suit material parented to `driverMount`, positioned at the steering-wheel torus location (line 557: y 4.35, z 0.95), and rotate them with `race.steer * 0.5` in `updateKartBodyMotion` (5386-5410) — the same function that already owns the lean. Two spheres per kart is the cheapest possible 'attached to the vehicle' cue and it is the one MK8 leans on hardest.

findings.title: No per-wheel suspension, no body roll, no acceleration pitch — the chassis is rigid
findings.evidence: `updateKartBodyMotion` (src/game/ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:5386-5410) is the entire kart animation budget and it does exactly two things: `driverMount.rotation.z = motion.lean` (the DRIVER leans, not the kart) and `bodyRig.position.y = bob` — a single global sine on the whole model. The kart body itself never rolls, never pitches under throttle or braking, and the four wheels only ever get `rotation.x` (spin) and, on the fronts, `rotation.y` (steer) at 6136-6137. There is no per-wheel Y travel anywhere in the file. In comeback-city-p0_9 the kart is mid-corner at 264 km/h and the chassis sits perfectly level on all four corners.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 karts visibly squat under acceleration, dive under braking, and load the outside wheels through a corner with real suspension travel — the outside-front tire compresses into the arch while the inside-rear extends. That weight transfer is 80% of why an MK8 kart feels heavy. A rigid chassis reads as a toy pushed along a table, which is exactly the frame-p0_9 impression.
findings.fix: Extend `updateKartBodyMotion` (5386). Track `motion.roll`, `motion.pitch`, `motion.prevSpeed`. Roll: `const rollTarget = -(steer + (drift ? driftDirection * 0.6 : 0)) * 0.10 * speedRatio; motion.roll = lerp(motion.roll, rollTarget, 1 - Math.pow(0.0008, dt)); kartModel.bodyRig.rotation.z = motion.roll;` — note this must go on `bodyRig` (the inner rig), NOT the outer group, otherwise it drags the blob shadow (see the shadow finding). Pitch: `const accel = (speed - motion.prevSpeed) / Math.max(dt, 0.001); const pitchTarget = clamp(-accel * 0.0016, -0.07, 0.09); motion.pitch = lerp(motion.pitch, pitchTarget, 1 - Math.pow(0.004, dt)); kartModel.bodyRig.rotation.x = motion.pitch;`. Per-wheel travel: since the kart now owns four procedural wheel Groups again (see finding 1), give each `wheel.userData.side = Math.sign(x)` and write `wheel.position.y = wheel.userData.restY - motion.roll * wheel.userData.side * 1.6 - motion.pitch * (wheel.userData.front ? 1.4 : -1.4)` so the wheels stay planted while the body leans over them. That inverse relationship — body rolls, wheels don't — is the whole trick.

findings.title: Contact shadow and underglow are hard-edged flat circles with no falloff
findings.evidence: src/game/ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:723-735 — the shadow is `CircleGeometry(6.2–7.0 × scale, 22–24)` with `MeshBasicMaterial({ color:'#03060c', opacity: 0.24–0.34 })`: a uniform-alpha disc, so the edge is a hard 22-gon boundary. `addGlowSprite` (470-482) is the same construction — `CircleGeometry(8 × scale, 24)`, `MeshBasicMaterial({ color, opacity: 0.22 })`, no map, no additive blending, no falloff. Both are visible as painted decals: the dark polygon under the Ice Sled in penguin-village-p0_78, and the flat cyan puddle under the kart in comeback-city-p0_33.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8's contact shadow has a soft radial gradient that is near-black directly under the chassis and fades to nothing at the tire line, plus a tighter, darker patch at each contact patch. That gradient IS the grounding read. A uniform disc with a visible rim announces itself as a sprite and flattens the kart onto the road plane.
findings.fix: Generate one shared 128×128 canvas texture at module scope (same pattern as `makeQuestionTexture`, line ~810): `const g = ctx.createRadialGradient(64,64,4,64,64,64); g.addColorStop(0,'rgba(255,255,255,1)'); g.addColorStop(0.45,'rgba(255,255,255,0.62)'); g.addColorStop(1,'rgba(255,255,255,0)')`. Use it as `alphaMap` on the shadow material (keep color '#03060c', set `transparent: true, depthWrite: false`) and as `map` on the underglow with `blending: THREE.AdditiveBlending`. One 128px canvas texture, shared across all four karts, zero bundle bytes. While you are there: scale the underglow with speed in the frame loop (`glow.scale.setScalar(0.85 + speedRatio * 0.4); glow.material.opacity = 0.16 + speedRatio * 0.18`) and stretch it rearward under boost (`glow.scale.z = 1 + boostT * 0.9`) so it reads as thrust rather than a static ring. Also add two small dark contact patches per axle (`CircleGeometry(1.1, 10)`, same alphaMap, opacity 0.4) parented to the new contact group at the wheel x/z positions — MK8's per-tire contact darkening is a big part of why its karts touch the road.

findings.title: Per-kart paint identity is dead — `characterEntry.color` is ignored for every authored kart
findings.evidence: `attachTripoKartBody` (src/game/ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:1525-1553) replaces the whole body with `MeshToonMaterial({ gradientMap, map: node.material?.map })` — the baked texture only. The `color` field on every `KART_CHARACTERS` entry (line 185-196: '#e8261d', '#8e1a43', '#2378ff', '#7e35f4', '#f28b2e', '#a86b32') and the `createGroundedKartModel({ color })` argument (4341, 4498) reach nothing but the deleted procedural body. Only `attachAuthoredKartBody` (1556) still recolors, via `makeKartPaletteTexture` (1375), and that is the fallback Kenney path. Net effect in comeback-city-p0_45: four racers on screen and the only per-racer color signal is the flat underglow disc — the karts themselves carry whatever paint their GLB was baked with.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 lets you read the whole field by paint at a glance and reinforces it with per-racer trail and item-hit colors. Racer identification at speed is a gameplay affordance, not just decoration. Here two rivals in comeback-city-p0_45 read as generically dark and you cannot tell who is who without the mini-map.
findings.fix: Add a hue-shift term to the same toon-rim injection registry in /Users/andrewferguson/Downloads/comeback-tracker/src/game/race/render/toonRimShader.js — `applyPaintTint(material, { tint, mask })`. Fragment pars `uniform vec3 uPaintTint; uniform float uPaintAmount;`, chunk anchored at `#include <opaque_fragment>` before the rim chunk: `float paintMask = smoothstep(0.28, 0.62, max(max(diffuseColor.r, diffuseColor.g), diffuseColor.b) - min(min(diffuseColor.r, diffuseColor.g), diffuseColor.b));` (saturated regions of the baked map = the paint, greys/blacks = tires and trim, so the mask self-selects) then `outgoingLight = mix(outgoingLight, outgoingLight * uPaintTint * 1.6, uPaintAmount * paintMask);`. Call it from `attachTripoKartBody` with `{ tint: characterEntry.color, amount: 0.55 }` — pass `characterEntry` through from the call site at 5186. Zero bytes, reuses the existing `addShaderInjection` composition so it stacks with rim and specular.

findings.title: Toon ramp blows out on Penguin Village — light-colored karts lose all form
findings.evidence: The gradient map (src/game/ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:905-919) is 4 bands at 90/150/215/255. Lights are `HemisphereLight('#fff8cf','#2085a4', 3.15)` and `DirectionalLight('#fff2b9', 3.55)` plus a `1.45` rim (src/game/race/render/createRaceScene.js:104-114) — over 8.0 combined intensity. Every surface whose N·L clears ~0.35 lands in band 3 or 4 and clamps. On a pale body against snow the result is total form loss: penguin-village-p0_78, the Ice Sled in front of the player is a single flat pale-blue shape with no readable top/side break, and penguin-village-p0_9 shows the same on the rival's grey body. Comeback City survives only because its palette is saturated and its road is dark.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8's cel ramp is authored so the terminator lands mid-form on the body panel — you can always read the cowl separating from the side pod, even on white karts on Sherbet Land. A ramp that saturates on the top three bands throws away the entire silhouette-within-silhouette read that makes MK8 karts look sculpted.
findings.fix: Two knobs, both zero-byte. (1) Push the ramp's break points down and widen the dark end: change the DataTexture at 905-919 from `[90,150,215,255]` to a 5-texel `[62, 108, 156, 214, 255]` and set `texture.magFilter = THREE.NearestFilter` (already set) — the extra dark step is what gives pale bodies their form back. (2) Add a cheap curvature-AO term to the hero-kart materials via a third `addShaderInjection` in toonRimShader.js: `float toonAo = smoothstep(-0.35, 0.85, geometryNormal.y); outgoingLight *= mix(0.72, 1.0, toonAo);` — downward-facing surfaces (wheel wells, undertray, seat interior, the shadowed side of the cowl) darken, which reintroduces vertical form independent of light direction. Judge both against penguin-village-p0_78 specifically; that frame is the worst case.

findings.title: Comeback City ships the hero rim at half Penguin Village's strength, and the kart's non-GLB parts get no rim at all
findings.evidence: src/game/race/tracks/comebackCity.js:53 `heroRim: { power: 3.2, strength: 0.22 }` vs src/game/race/tracks/penguinVillage.js:143 `heroRim: { power: 2.2, strength: 0.45 }` — the DARK track gets the weaker rim. Separately, `applyHeroRim` is only ever called on GLB-loaded nodes (ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:1424, 1529, 1558, 5226, 5251, 5286); `createToonMaterial` accepts a `rim: true` flag (1299-1301) but `createGroundedKartModel` never passes it for any of its six materials (511-516), and the wheels, hubs, exhaust pipes and roll cage are all built from those. So on a Tripo kart only the fused body is rimmed and the procedural parts around it are not. Result in comeback-city-p0_06: the player kart is the darkest object on screen, its outline dissolving into the navy road at the very start of the race.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 keeps a bright edge on the player kart in every lighting condition — Neon Lights and Big Blue both push a strong environment rim so the kart never loses its outline against a dark road. Silhouette legibility is non-negotiable because the player's eye tracks the kart, not the road.
findings.fix: (1) Raise Comeback City to `heroRim: { power: 2.4, strength: 0.40, tint: '#4fd8ff' }` in src/game/race/tracks/comebackCity.js:53 — the neon-dusk palette can carry it and the dark road demands it. (2) Pass `rim: true` on the body, trim, hub and seat materials in `createGroundedKartModel` (511-516) — leave `tireMat` rim-free so rubber stays matte (that contrast is a feature). (3) Make the rim speed-reactive so it does double duty as a velocity cue: in the frame loop, `TOON_RIM_SHARED_TINT` is already a shared uniform object (toonRimShader.js:33) — add a parallel shared `TOON_RIM_STRENGTH_SCALE` uniform and drive it `1.0 + speedRatio * 0.5 + (boosting ? 0.6 : 0)`. That is one float write per frame for the whole hero set.

findings.title: Exhaust is a static emissive cone with a sine scale — no heat shimmer, no throttle response, no backfire
findings.evidence: src/game/ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:575-584 builds two `ConeGeometry(0.4, 1.6, 6)` flames in a flat `#FF8C00` `createBasicMaterial` with `emissiveIntensity: 1.0`, and the only animation is 6139-6144: `flame.visible = race.speed > 16` and `flame.scale.setScalar(0.65 + heat*0.65 + sin(raceTime*26 + i*2.1)*0.16)` — a uniform breathing scale on an opaque orange cone. It never changes color with load, never flickers off-and-on, and there is no soft/additive falloff, so it reads as an orange traffic cone bolted to the bumper (visible bottom-left of comeback-city-p0_45).
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8's exhaust pops and stutters — the flame is short and blue-white at the root, orange at the tip, cuts out on lift-off and cracks back on throttle. It is a small element but it is one of the few things telling you the kart has an engine.
findings.fix: Same file, same block. (1) Two-part flame: keep the outer cone but drop it to `MeshBasicMaterial({ color:'#FF8C00', transparent:true, opacity:0.55, blending: THREE.AdditiveBlending, depthWrite:false, toneMapped:false })` and add an inner `ConeGeometry(0.18, 0.9, 6)` in '#9fe8ff' at full opacity — the hot-core/cool-tip gradient is what stops it reading as plastic. (2) Throttle response: hold `motion.prevSpeed` (already needed for the pitch fix) and gate on acceleration, not speed — `const onThrottle = speed > motion.prevSpeed - 2; flame.visible = speed > 16 && (onThrottle || Math.random() < 0.35)` gives free stutter. (3) Backfire on drift release: in the `releaseFlash` branch of `updateKartBodyMotion` (5392-5394), scale the flames to 2.4× for the flash duration and tint them to the banked tier color from `DRIFT_FEEL.sparkColors` — it ties the exhaust to the drift system that already exists.

verdictVsMk8: Worse, and not by a subtle margin. In a blind side-by-side the single loudest read of these frames is the boost speed-line mesh, which lands as a fan of opaque grey lollipop-sticks pasted over the sky, the skyline and the player kart itself (comeback-city-p0_78, penguin-village-p0_15) — MK8's equivalent is a tapered, edge-hugging, outward-streaming field that never intrudes on the readable centre of frame and never occludes the kart. Underneath that, the VFX vocabulary answers only 2 of the 15 gameplay cues the game already derives (raceParticles.js:246-266 vs kartAudio.js:36-56): there is no item-use effect, no impact, no landing puff, no ambient wheel dust, no lap or finish celebration, and no camera shake anywhere in the shipped runtime. The plumbing is genuinely good — pooled, budgeted, cue-driven, tier-coloured — so almost every gap here is a shader-and-parameters problem, not an architecture problem. Score reflects a solid chassis carrying a flagship effect that currently reads as a rendering bug.

findings.title: Boost speed-lines occupy a mid-frame band and rigidly pinwheel — they read as floating grey sticks, not motion
findings.evidence: comeback-city-p0_78.png (a streak runs diagonally across the player kart's nose and roof), comeback-city-p0_24.png / p0_45.png (streaks lie across the sun disc, skyline and the centre of the road), penguin-village-p0_15.png (streaks over the snowman and the ice shelf). Code: src/game/race/render/raceParticles.js:154-201 builds 14 fixed wedges in the camera's XY plane at z=-1.6, inner radius 0.86, outer radius 1.5, constant half-width 0.009-0.013, no texture and no per-vertex alpha; lines 369-376 animate them only via `speedLines.rotation.z += dt*2.4` plus a per-frame `opacity = 0.18 + Math.random()*0.12`, with `depthTest:false` and `renderOrder:60`.
findings.whyMk8Wins: Three concrete failures. (1) SCREEN PLACEMENT: the radii are fixed world units on a plane at z=-1.6, but the shipped camera runs fov 70-77 (ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:6326-6329). At fov 74 / 16:9 the frustum half-height at that plane is 1.21 and half-width 2.14, so inner 0.86 = 40% of half-width and outer 1.5 = 70% of half-width. Horizontally the streaks live in a 40%-70% band and NEVER reach the frame edge, while vertically they overshoot off-screen. That is exactly inverted from MK8, whose speed lines start near the frame border and run off it, leaving the centre 60% of the image clean. (2) NO LIFECYCLE: the geometry is static and the whole ring spins about Z — motion perpendicular to the streak axis. A streak only sells speed when it moves ALONG its own axis. Spinning it sideways reads as a rotating fan of sticks, which is precisely what the frames show. (3) NO TAPER: a constant-width, constant-alpha quad with no map has hard rectangular ends; MK8 streaks fade to zero alpha at both ends so they have no visible termination. Add `depthTest:false` and they punch through the kart, which no MK8 effect ever does.

findings.title: Speed-lines are visible in 18 of 18 baseline frames — the boost effect has no envelope and therefore no contrast
findings.evidence: All nine comeback-city and all nine penguin-village baseline PNGs show the streak field, at HUD speeds ranging from 73 to 289 (tmp/aaa-visual/baseline/capture-manifest.json). Code: src/game/race/render/raceParticles.js:370 `const boostVisible = context.boosting && !context.reducedMotion;` with `context.boosting = race.boostTimer > 0 || driftState.miniTurboTimer > 0` (ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:6238). Visibility is a hard boolean with no attack, no decay, and no speed term; opacity is re-randomised every frame (raceParticles.js:374), so it flickers at framerate rather than animating.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8's speed distortion is an EVENT: it punches in over ~4 frames, holds, and bleeds out over ~15 frames, and it only appears when you are genuinely above cruise speed. Because boost pads, coins and mini-turbos fire almost continuously on these two tracks, this implementation is on essentially all the time — so it stops being feedback and becomes furniture. A player cannot tell from the screen whether they are boosting. The per-frame `Math.random()` opacity also produces a 60Hz strobe rather than a coherent stream, which is why the sticks read as dirt on the lens.

findings.title: The VFX vocabulary answers 2 of the 15 gameplay cues the game already derives
findings.evidence: src/game/race/kartAudio.js:36-56 `cuesForTransition` emits: countdown-1/2/3, go, lap, finish, item-pickup, item-use, coin, coin-loss, spin-out, drift-start, tier-1/2/3, mini-turbo-1/2/3, boost, land. src/game/race/render/raceParticles.js:246-266 `onCue` handles exactly two: 'coin' and 'spin-out'. Everything else is visually silent. Confirmed in frames: comeback-city-p0_9.png shows two karts in door-to-door contact with zero impact VFX; penguin-village-p0_9.png shows the ICE SHIELD item deployed as a bare wireframe geodesic cage with no deploy flash, no fresnel, no orbiting particles; item boxes just blink out of existence (raceVfx.js:259-263 `visible: cooldown <= 0`) with no shatter.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 gives every single gameplay event a distinct, instantly-legible visual signature: the item box explodes into coloured shards, the shell launch has a muzzle puff plus a ground shockwave ring, a hit produces a star burst + screen shake + a spinning smoke ring, a landing kicks a ground puff sized by fall height, crossing the finish line fires confetti and fireworks. Here the player learns most of the game state from the HUD numbers, not from the world. That mismatch — a world that never reacts — is the single largest quality gap in this pillar and the one that most reads as 'prototype' next to MK8.
findings.fix:
Extend the `onCue` router in raceParticles.js. All of these reuse the EXISTING pooled burstMesh (one InstancedMesh, instanceColor already wired) — grow the pool from 32/16 to 96/40 (raceParticles.js:141) which is +64 instance matrices ≈ 5 KB VRAM and ZERO new draw calls. Add cases:
- `item-pickup`: 8 particles, colour = the item's icon accent, speed 3.0, ttl 0.35, upBias 5.0, spawn at kart +2.8y — plus scale the item-box shatter (see below).
- `item-use`: 12 particles ejected in a forward cone (bias velocity along `context.yaw`), colour #FFF4C2, speed 9, ttl 0.3, upBias 1.2 — a muzzle puff.
- `spin-out`: keep, but add a screen-space shockwave ring — reuse `driftTierPopRing` geometry (ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:711-718) with colour #FF5A5A, scaled 0.4→3.2 over 0.35s. +0 DC (mesh exists).
- `land`: 10 particles in a flat ring (upBias 0.8, speed 6, ttl 0.4), colour from the surface table in finding #5, count scaled by `race.airState.peakHeight`.
- `tier-1/2/3`: 6 particles at the rear wheels in DRIFT_FEEL.sparkColors[tier], speed 7, ttl 0.28 — a real spark pop on top of the existing pop ring.
- `mini-turbo-1/2/3`: 14 particles fired BACKWARD along -yaw at speed 16, ttl 0.4, colour = tier colour; plus set `punch = 1.4` on the speed-line envelope.
- `lap` / `finish`: see finding #11.
- Item-box shatter: in the boostPad/itemBox frame block, when `box.cooldown` flips positive, fire 14 burst particles at the box position with colour #7FE7FF and `gravity` — requires passing a position override into `spawnBurst` (see finding #10).
Total added draw calls: ZERO (all through the existing burst pool + existing ring meshes).

findings.title: Skid-mark ring buffer wraps after ~0.17 s of drifting — marks pop out of existence three kart-lengths behind the kart
findings.evidence: src/game/race/render/raceParticles.js:27-30 `SKID_QUADS = 64`, `SKID_MIN_STEP = 1.25`, `SKID_FADE_SECONDS = 6`, `SKID_HALF_WIDTH = 0.34`. `laySkidSegment` (lines 268-305) emits one quad PER REAR WHEEL every 1.25 world units, so the 64-quad ring is shared 32/32. 32 quads x 1.25 units = 40 world units of trail per wheel. MAX_SPEED is 228 (ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:173), so the ring wraps in 40/228 = 0.175 s. The 6-second alpha fade at line 348 can therefore never actually run — quads are recycled ~34x faster than they fade. Visible in comeback-city-p0_9.png: the two dark tyre lines behind the player kart terminate abruptly about three kart-lengths back, mid-road, with a hard edge and no taper.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 lays a long, continuous, softly-tapered rubber trail that persists through the whole corner and fades gradually, so a drift leaves a legible arc you can read your own line off. Here the trail is a stub that is constantly being erased at its tail with a hard cut — which looks like a rendering artifact, not like rubber. Also, `SKID_HALF_WIDTH = 0.34` gives a 0.68-unit-wide strip under a kart whose rear wheels sit at x = ±4.6 (raceParticles.js:272) — the mark is a pinstripe, far narrower than the tyre that supposedly made it.
findings.fix:
In src/game/race/render/raceParticles.js:
- `SKID_QUADS` 64 → 256 (buffers grow to 256*4*3 floats position = 12 KB and 256*4*4 = 16 KB colour — negligible; indices must move from Uint16Array to Uint16Array still fine at 1024 verts).
- `SKID_MIN_STEP` 1.25 → 2.4 (halves emission; 128 quads/wheel x 2.4 = 307 units = 1.35 s of trail at full speed, roughly a full corner).
- `SKID_FADE_SECONDS` 6 → 4.0 so the fade is actually reached before recycling.
- `SKID_HALF_WIDTH` 0.34 → 0.78 to match the rear tyre footprint.
- Add a HEAD/TAIL taper so the ends never hard-cut: when writing a quad, scale its alpha by `min(1, ageIndex/3)` at the freshest end and by the existing age fade at the old end; and lerp the two outer vertices toward the centreline by 35% on the oldest 4 quads so the trail narrows to a point.
- Mobile: keep 128 quads (`mobile ? 128 : 256`).
Still exactly ONE draw call — this is a buffer-size and constants change only.

findings.title: Boost flame is two opaque solid cones — no additive core, no alpha falloff, no animated noise
findings.evidence: src/game/race/render/createKartModel.js:149-159 — `new THREE.ConeGeometry(0.82, 4.6, 7)` with `createBasicMaterial('#ffd34f', { emissive:'#ffd34f', emissiveIntensity:0.9 })`: an opaque, un-blended, 7-sided solid. The only animation is a uniform `scale.setScalar()` and an emissive colour swap at ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:6046-6052. Lines 160-190 add two opaque `BoxGeometry(0.52, 0.28, 8.8)` streak bars and a `TorusGeometry` halo, all `depthTest:false`.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8's boost plume is a layered additive element: a white-hot core, a coloured mid-shell, a soft outer haze, all with an animated noise mask so the flame shape breathes and the silhouette never reads as a rigid solid. A hard-edged opaque yellow cone with visible facets reads as a plastic party hat bolted to the bumper, and it gets no help from the bloom pass because it is a solid mid-luminance surface rather than a bright additive core. The `depthTest:false` streak bars also draw through geometry, so at close quarters (comeback-city-p0_9.png) a rival's boost bars would punch through the player kart.

findings.title: No ambient or surface-specific particles: dust only exists while drifting, so the karts never touch the ground
findings.evidence: src/game/race/render/raceParticles.js:312 `const spraying = context.drifting && !context.airborne;` gates BOTH the spray pool and the skid marks. There is no emission for straight-line driving, for going off-road (surfacePhysics.js has an off-road state that produces no VFX), for landing, for water, or for driving on snow. Visible in comeback-city-p0_45.png / p0_78.png and penguin-village-p0_56.png: karts at HUD speed 283-289 sit on the road with absolutely nothing coming off the tyres. penguin-village-p0_78 shows water/ice shelf adjacent to the road with no interaction at all.
findings.whyMk8Wins: In MK8 every kart is always shedding something — a faint tyre dust plume on tarmac, a heavier brown plume off-road, white spray on snow, a rooster tail through shallow water, plus rhythmic exhaust puffs. That constant low-level particulate is what glues the vehicle to the surface and is a huge part of why MK8 reads as fast; without it a kart at 289 looks like it is sliding on glass. It is also the primary way MK8 communicates 'you are off the racing line' without HUD text.
findings.fix:
Reuse the SAME spray InstancedMesh — no new draw call. In raceParticles.js:
1. Add a surface table: `const SURFACE = { asphalt:{tint:'#6E7488', rate:9, size:0.55}, snow:{tint:'#EAF6FF', rate:16, size:0.8}, grass:{tint:'#7FA05A', rate:22, size:0.85}, ice:{tint:'#CFEFFF', rate:6, size:0.5}, water:{tint:'#9FE0FF', rate:26, size:0.95} }`.
2. Change the emission gate to: `const groundRate = context.airborne ? 0 : (context.drifting ? (24 + tier*11) : SURFACE[context.surface].rate * clamp((speed - 0.30*maxSpeed)/(0.55*maxSpeed), 0, 1) * (context.offroad ? 3.0 : 1.0));`
3. Add per-particle colour: switch the spray pool to `instanceColor` (already supported by makeBillboardPool's InstancedMesh — call `setColorAt`) so drift spray keeps the tier colour while ambient dust takes the surface tint, instead of the current single `sprayMesh.material.color` swap at raceParticles.js:323-324.
4. Switch the ambient-dust particles to `THREE.NormalBlending` via a second material is NOT possible on one mesh — instead keep additive but drop the ambient tint luminance to ~0.35 so it does not blow out on Penguin Village snow.
5. Grow the pool 48/24 → 110/48 to carry both systems.
6. Pass `surface`, `offroad`, `speed` into the particleContext at ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:6236-6249 (surfacePhysics already resolves these each frame).
Draw-call cost: 0. Byte cost: 0.

findings.title: No camera shake anywhere in the shipped runtime — the shake code lives in a dead module
findings.evidence: src/game/race/camera/chaseCamera.js:328-332 implements `race.cameraShakeTimer` positional shake, but chaseCamera.js is only imported by src/game/race/raceCameraRuntime.js, which is only imported by src/game/ArcadeRace3D.jsx — explicitly listed as DEAD legacy. The shipped camera is the inline block at src/game/ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:6285-6333: it lerps position, calls `lookAt`, and lerps fov, with no jitter term. `grep -n cameraShakeTimer src/game/ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx` returns nothing. Spin-outs are set at nine separate sites (lines 5458, 5558, 5718, 5757, 5773, 5786, 5856, 5882, 5892) and none of them touch the camera.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 punctuates every impact with a short, high-frequency camera shake plus a brief hitch — it is the difference between 'my kart spun' and 'I got HIT'. Without it a spin-out here is a silent rotation with a small grey poof. Shake is also the cheapest possible AAA-feel win: zero draw calls, zero bytes, ~15 lines.

findings.title: Drift spray is too sparse and too dim to read at race speed, and additive white on Penguin Village snow self-erases
findings.evidence: src/game/race/render/raceParticles.js:314 `const rate = (24 + context.tier * 11)` — max 57 particles/sec at tier 3; TTL 0.30-0.52 s (line 221) means the steady-state live count is only ~23 sprites, each 0.62 world units (line 89) against a kart whose rear wheels sit ±4.6 units apart. Blending is hard-coded `THREE.AdditiveBlending` for the whole pool (line 61), and Penguin Village's road surround is near-white snow that is already at the bloom threshold (bloom `luminanceThreshold: 1.0`, ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3993) after the ACES tonemap.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8's tier-3 drift spray is a dense, opaque, continuously-emitting jet with a visible volume — you can see the shape of the spray cone from the chase camera. 23 half-metre translucent dots is a sprinkle. Worse, additive blending can only ADD light: over Penguin Village snow that is already near clipping, an additive white sprite contributes almost nothing after tonemapping, so the arctic track — the one where snow spray should be the signature effect — is the track where the spray is least visible.
findings.fix:
In raceParticles.js:
1. Raise emission: `const rate = (52 + context.tier * 26) * (reducedMotion ? 0.5 : 1)` (max 130/s) and lengthen TTL to `0.42 + Math.random()*0.30`, giving ~48 live sprites.
2. Raise the pool to 110 desktop / 48 mobile (still 1 draw call).
3. Split blending by track: pass `blending: isIce ? THREE.NormalBlending : THREE.AdditiveBlending` into `makeBillboardPool` for the spray mesh (line 89). On ice/snow, NormalBlending with a slightly darker-than-white tint (#DCEEFF at 0.8 alpha) actually reads against the bright ground; on Comeback City asphalt keep additive so the neon tier colours glow.
4. Give the sprites shape variance: currently every particle is the same 32px radial dot at the same rotation (line 336 composes with the camera quaternion only). Add a random per-particle roll and a non-uniform scale that stretches along the velocity direction: `scratchScale.set(0.35 + fade*0.7, (0.35 + fade*0.7) * (1.0 + speedOfParticle*0.02), 1)` and pre-multiply the camera quaternion by a Z-roll quaternion seeded from the pool index.
5. Bump the soft-dot texture from 32x32 to 64x64 (getSoftDotTexture, line 45-59) and add a second, harder-cored stop (`grad.addColorStop(0.18, 'rgba(255,255,255,0.92)')`) so the sprite has a bright core instead of a uniform smudge. Canvas-generated: zero bytes.

findings.title: Mini-turbo stages are communicated by hue alone — no shape, density or screen-space escalation
findings.evidence: The tier ladder is implemented entirely as colour swaps plus small scalar bumps: driftFeel.js:23 `sparkColors: ['#F5F8FF','#00E5FF','#FFD34F','#C879FF']`; ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:6070-6094 sets `spark.material.color` and a `scale.setScalar(0.7 + sparkTier*0.3)`; raceParticles.js:314 raises spray rate by 11/tier; raceParticles.js:373 flips the speed-line colour only at `miniTurboTier >= 3`. Tier 1 and tier 2 produce an identical screen-space read.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 escalates mini-turbo across four independent channels simultaneously: colour, spark COUNT, spark SIZE and shape (blue pinpricks → orange forks → purple starbursts), an audio pitch ladder, and a visible camera/FOV response. You know your charge tier from peripheral vision alone while watching the road. Here the only reliable signal is a hue you have to look down at the rear wheels to read, and the biggest channel (the speed-line field) is binary at tier 3.
findings.fix:
Four cheap additions, all inside existing meshes:
1. Spark COUNT: the drift spark group is built with a fixed 4 sparks per side (createKartModel.js, the `for (let index = 0; index < 4; index += 1)` loop). Build 8 per side and gate visibility by tier: `spark.visible = sparkIndex % 8 < (2 + sparkTier * 2)`. +0 draw calls (same group, same material).
2. Spark SHAPE: give tier 3 a forked read by scaling the sparks non-uniformly — `spark.scale.set(0.6 + t*0.2, 0.7 + t*0.55, 0.6 + t*0.2)` so higher tiers elongate vertically instead of just getting bigger.
3. Speed-line tint per tier (already in finding #1's fix): drive `uTint` from `DRIFT_FEEL.sparkColors[miniTurboTier]` continuously, not just at tier 3, and scale `uLanes` 26 → 34 → 44 with tier so the field visibly densifies.
4. FOV ladder: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:6326-6329 currently adds a flat `miniTurboActive ? 3.5 : 0`. Change to `(miniTurboActive ? 2.0 + driftState.miniTurboTier * 2.2 : 0)` (tier 1 = +4.2, tier 3 = +8.6) and speed the lerp up on the way IN only: `const k = targetFov > camera.fov ? 1 - Math.pow(0.00002, dt) : 1 - Math.pow(0.02, dt);` — fast punch, slow settle, which is the MK8 rhythm.

findings.title: One-shot bursts always spawn at the kart centre regardless of where the event happened
findings.evidence: src/game/race/render/raceParticles.js:231 — `item.position.set(context.kartPosition.x, context.groundY + 2.4, context.kartPosition.z)` is hard-coded for EVERY burst. A coin collected at a lateral lane offset, a shell impact on a rival, a broken item box, a wall scrape — all would sparkle at the player kart's origin, 2.4 units above the ground, floating inside the driver.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 anchors every burst to the thing that caused it: the coin pings at the coin, the box shatters where the box was, the impact star ring appears at the contact point. Spawning at the kart origin means the effect cannot ever confirm WHAT you hit or WHERE, which is exactly the information a racer needs mid-corner. It also means bursts on rivals are impossible to represent at all.

findings.title: No lap or finish celebration — the two biggest moments in the race are visually silent
findings.evidence: src/game/race/kartAudio.js:43-44 emits `lap` and `finish` cues, and raceParticles.js:246-266 ignores both. `grep -i 'confetti|celebrat' src/game/ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx` returns nothing. The finish is handled purely as a camera change (ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:6303-6306: pull back to 30 units, height 13) plus HUD text.
findings.whyMk8Wins: Crossing the line in MK8 fires confetti cannons, a firework volley over the finish gate, a camera swing and a lap-flash wipe. It is the payoff for the whole run. Here the moment the player has been racing toward produces nothing but a number change — which makes the entire race feel unresolved even when the driving felt good.
findings.fix:
Two additions, both cheap and both procedural:
1. LAP cue: a one-frame screen flash + a chevron sweep. Reuse the speed-line screen quad from finding #1 by adding a `uFlash` uniform — on 'lap', set `uFlash = 1` and decay it over 0.22 s, adding `gl_FragColor.rgb += uTint * uFlash * 0.35 * smoothstep(0.0, 1.0, vUv.x)` as a left-to-right wipe. ZERO new draw calls.
2. FINISH cue: a confetti volley through the existing burst pool. Add a `confetti` burst mode to `spawnBurst`: 48 particles (24 on mobile), spawned in an arc 18 units wide above the finish gate, `speed 14`, `upBias 18`, `ttl 2.6`, gravity already applied at raceParticles.js:361, per-particle `instanceColor` cycled through the track palette (#FF4FA3 / #FFD34F / #00E5FF / #C879FF for Comeback City; #EAF6FF / #7FE7FF / #FFD34F for Penguin Village). Requires the pool growth from finding #3 (96 desktop / 40 mobile) — with the pool at 96 a 48-particle volley is comfortable. Add a flutter term so confetti does not fall like dust: `item.velocity.x += Math.sin(item.life*11 + index)*22*dt` in the burst update loop, and give the sprites a Z-roll (see finding #8 item 4). ZERO new draw calls, ZERO new bytes.
3. Optionally reuse the existing `driftTierPopRing` mesh for a shockwave ring at the gate on 'finish' (already in the scene, +0 DC).

verdictVsMk8: In a blind side-by-side this loses badly, and it loses at the top of the frame before a player even looks at the track. The sky does not close: the far backdrop cylinder's rim sits at ~22.6° elevation (y_top = 330 at radius 780, camera y ≈ 5) and above it the raw `scene.background` gradient is exposed at rgb(10,15,40), so every single one of the 18 baseline frames has a hard elliptical arc of near-black stamped across the upper third — measured at x=600 in comeback-city-p0_33 the frame goes (4,7,42) → (162,48,47) in 24 pixels. On top of that the far plate is wrapped `repeats: 5` with MirroredRepeatWrapping, and the plate has a sun disc baked into it, so comeback-city-p0_67 shows TWO SUNS in one 66° FOV. MK8 never shows you a skybox edge — Sunshine Airport and Toad Harbor use a fully closed dome with a layered cloud deck and one authored sun, and every distant object is value-compressed toward the horizon colour so the world reads as air rather than as painted cardboard standing in a void. Here the fog colour on Comeback City is #272252, a dark purple, sitting under a 255,106,30 orange horizon, so distance gets DARKER — aerial perspective is running backwards.

findings.title: The sky dome does not close — a hard black arc cuts the top of every frame
findings.evidence: Visible in all 18 baseline frames; worst in comeback-city-p0_33/-p0_45 and penguin-village-p0_45/-p0_78. Cause: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3957 `addBackdropRing(..., { height: 380, radius: 780, y: 140 })` — an open-ended CylinderGeometry whose top rim sits at y=330, i.e. atan(324/780)=22.6° elevation, well inside the 33° half-FOV of the 66° camera (line 3870). Above that rim the bare `scene.background` gradient shows: DUSK_SKY_STOPS[0] = '#0a0f28' = rgb(10,15,40) (line 867), measured at (1590,2) as (0,0,8) after vignette in p0_45/p0_67/p0_78/p0_9. The plate's own 35% alpha ramp (cc-far.webp alpha = 0 at row 0, 146 at row 214, 255 at row 375) is crushed by perspective foreshortening into ~24 screen pixels: at x=600 in comeback-city-p0_33 the column reads (4,7,42) at y=212 and (162,48,47) at y=236. So instead of a fade you get a seam.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 skyboxes are closed domes — you can point the camera straight up on Sunshine Airport or Mount Wario and there is authored sky all the way to zenith. A visible geometric skybox rim is a shipping bug no Nintendo track has. It is also the first thing a player's eye lands on because it is a high-contrast curved edge in an otherwise smooth region.
findings.fix: Replace the screen-space background + open cylinder top with a real dome. New file src/game/race/render/createSkyDome.js: `SphereGeometry(1, 32, 20)`, ShaderMaterial {side: THREE.BackSide, depthWrite:false, depthTest:false, fog:false}, mesh.frustumCulled=false, mesh.renderOrder=-1000. Vertex shader pins it to the far plane so radius and camera-follow are moot: `varying vec3 vDir; void main(){ vDir = position; gl_Position = (projectionMatrix * modelViewMatrix * vec4(position,1.0)).xyww; }` (set mesh.matrixAutoUpdate=false, identity matrix, and copy only camera rotation implicitly via modelViewMatrix). Fragment samples the EXISTING makeSkyTexture canvas as a 1D LUT so this costs zero new bytes: `vec3 d=normalize(vDir); float v = 1.0 - pow(clamp(d.y/0.85,0.0,1.0), 0.65); gl_FragColor = vec4(texture2D(uSky, vec2(0.5,v)).rgb, 1.0);` The 0.65 exponent biases resolution into the lower 20° where the plate lives. Then set `scene.background = null` at ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3863 and add the dome. Second half of the fix: raise the far ring so its rim is inside the fade zone rather than at 22.6° — change line 3957 to `{ height: 900, order: -20, radius: 780, repeats: 5, y: 330 }` (rim at y=780 → 45° elevation) and widen the plate's alpha ramp to 60% of its height when you regenerate it, so the plate top dissolves into the dome over ~15° instead of 2.7°.

findings.title: Two suns in one shot — the sun disc is baked into a plate that tiles 5x, mirrored
findings.evidence: comeback-city-p0_67.png shows two identical yellow sun discs about 35° apart inside a 66° FOV (centre-left at ~x=690 and centre-right at ~x=960). comeback-city-p0_06 shows a third at the far right edge. Cause: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3940-3941 `texture.wrapS = THREE.MirroredRepeatWrapping; texture.repeat.x = repeats;` with `repeats: 5` on the far band (line 3957) and `repeats: 7` on the near silhouette (line 3958). cc-far.webp is 2560x1072 with a sun painted into it, so the sun is instanced 5x around the horizon and mirrored, producing symmetric sun PAIRS. The same mirroring makes the skyline silhouette bilaterally symmetric about 10 axes — visible as repeated tower clusters in comeback-city-p0_33 and -p0_45.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 has exactly one sun per track and it is an authored world-space element, not a repeating wallpaper motif. Two suns is not a stylistic choice a player forgives; it reads as a texture-wrap bug, which it is.
findings.fix: Two changes. (1) Paint the sun disc out of cc-far.webp (and any glow bloom around it) so the plate is a pure horizontal gradient band + skyline silhouette that is legitimately tileable; re-export at the same 2560x1072 — the file will get SMALLER, so this is byte-negative. (2) Move the sun into the new dome shader from finding 1 as a world-space element: uniforms `uSunDir` (vec3, normalize the DirectionalLight direction from line 3883 so the sun disc and the key light agree — currently sun.position is (-150,52,-70), i.e. azimuth 245°, elevation 18°) and `uSunColor` (#ffb85a for CC, #ffd9a8 for PV). Fragment: `float sd = max(dot(d, uSunDir), 0.0); col += uSunColor * (smoothstep(0.9985, 0.9994, sd) * 2.2 + pow(sd, 14.0) * 0.30 + pow(sd, 3.0) * 0.08);` The three terms are disc, tight halo, and broad sky-glow lobe — the last one is what makes MK8's sunset skies feel lit rather than painted. Also swap MirroredRepeatWrapping to THREE.RepeatWrapping once the plate is genuinely tileable, killing the mirror symmetry in the skyline.

findings.title: The horizon is world-fixed geometry the player drives through — skyline size swings ~2.6x per lap
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3954 `scene.add(ring)` — both rings are parented to the scene at the world origin and are never repositioned (no ring reposition exists anywhere in the frame loop; grep for 'ring' in the file returns only the mini-turbo/tier-pop torus meshes). The CC centreline spans x -285..346, z -239..257 (src/game/courseV2.js, 81 nodes), so the player is up to ~350 units off origin. Against a 780-unit ring that makes the far skyline 430 units away at one end of the lap and 1130 at the other. In comeback-city-p0_9 a single tower fills the entire left edge of frame floor-to-ceiling; in comeback-city-p0_33 the whole skyline is a thin strip under 25% of frame height. Same plate, same camera height, 2.6x apparent scale. It is also visible in the seam from finding 1: at x=1200 in p0_33 the alpha ramp spans ~90px while at x=600 it spans 24px, because that side of the ring is much closer.
findings.whyMk8Wins: Every MK8 skybox layer is camera-locked (translation-invariant). Toad Harbor's bay and Sunshine Airport's ocean never change size as you drive — they read as genuinely distant. A horizon that grows and shrinks as you corner reads as a painted cylinder standing in the level, which is exactly what it is here, and it destroys the sense of scale of the whole track.
findings.fix: In ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx around line 3936, create `const backdropAnchorFar = new THREE.Group(); const backdropAnchorNear = new THREE.Group(); scene.add(backdropAnchorFar, backdropAnchorNear);` and add each ring to the matching anchor instead of `scene`. In the frame loop (~line 6340, right after the chase camera update) add: `backdropAnchorFar.position.set(camera.position.x, 0, camera.position.z); backdropAnchorNear.position.set(camera.position.x * 0.72, 0, camera.position.z * 0.72);` Full lock on the far band = infinite horizon; 0.72 on the near silhouette row = a deliberate, controlled parallax so the two layers still separate in depth (this is precisely MK8's multi-layer skybox trick). Cost is two Vector3 writes per frame. Once locked you can also drop the far ring radius from 780 to ~600 and shrink its height proportionally, which improves the texel density of the plate for free.

findings.title: Aerial perspective runs backwards on Comeback City — fog is dark purple under an orange sky
findings.evidence: comebackCity.js palette (lines 43-59) declares only `bridge` and `heroRim` — there is no `fog` key, so ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3869 falls through to `new THREE.Fog('#272252', 240, 820)` = rgb(39,34,82). The horizon it is supposed to blend into is rgb(255,106,30) (cc-far.webp row 375, sampled). Result: distant ground goes darker and colder while the sky behind it goes brighter and hotter. Measured in comeback-city-p0_33 at x=1500: ground is (45,60,55) at y=480 (near the horizon) and (39,58,54) at y=560 — effectively no gradient at all across several hundred world units — and it terminates against the backdrop with no transition whatsoever.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 always hazes toward the sky colour at the corresponding elevation. On Sunshine Airport distant tarmac lifts and warms into the sky; on Mount Wario distant snow lifts into pale blue. That value-compression is the single strongest depth cue in the whole image, and it is completely absent here — which is why the Comeback City ground plane reads as a flat sheet of dead olive rather than as land receding into a sunset.
findings.fix: Add a `fog` key to the Comeback City palette in src/game/race/tracks/comebackCity.js: `fog: { color: '#c9541f', near: 300, far: 1000 }`. That colour is the horizon orange pulled ~25% toward the ground base so the road does not wash out at mid distance; `near: 300` keeps the drivable ~250 units in front of the kart completely fog-free so gameplay readability is untouched. Then bump the fog.far ceiling comment at ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3866-3867 — the 840 limit is stale since camera.far is 1800 when the backdrop is on (line 3934). Second half: the fog colour must vary with view elevation, not be a constant, or the sky-facing and ground-facing halves disagree. Cheapest correct version is a fog-colour override in the toon material's onBeforeCompile (src/game/race/render/toonRimShader.js already hooks materials): replace `vFogDepth`-driven `mix(gl_FragColor.rgb, fogColor, fogFactor)` with `mix(gl_FragColor.rgb, mix(uFogGround, uFogSky, clamp(normalize(vViewDir).y*2.0+0.5,0.0,1.0)), fogFactor)` where uFogGround = '#7a3a2c' and uFogSky = '#ff6a1e' for CC. Roughly 6 extra ALU ops per pixel, no new draw calls.

findings.title: The sky is a screen-space quad — it never rotates, pitches or parallaxes with the camera
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3863 `scene.background = makeSkyTexture(palette.sky)`. makeSkyTexture (lines 873-885) returns a plain 64x512 CanvasTexture with the default UVMapping. In Three r184's WebGLBackground, a non-cube, non-equirect Texture is drawn on a fullscreen plane in screen space — it is nailed to the framebuffer, stretched to viewport aspect, and completely independent of camera orientation. So the only part of the frame that responds to the camera is the ring geometry; the ~top third of the image is a static gradient. On the Comeback City bridge launch, where the camera pitches hard, the zenith does not move at all.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 skyboxes are true world-oriented domes. The moment you launch off a ramp or the camera whips through a hairpin, the sky and clouds swing with you — that swing is a big part of why MK8's jumps feel like jumps. A screen-locked gradient makes every vertical camera move feel weightless.
findings.fix: This is subsumed by the dome in finding 1, but call it out explicitly so it is not skipped: after adding the dome, set `scene.background = null` and DELETE the makeSkyTexture call at line 3863 (keep the function — reuse its canvas as the dome's 1D elevation LUT, `texture.wrapS = ClampToEdgeWrapping; texture.wrapT = ClampToEdgeWrapping; texture.minFilter = LinearFilter; texture.generateMipmaps = false`). Verify by capturing a bridge-launch frame with the camera pitched >20° up and confirming the zenith colour moves down the frame.

findings.title: Zero clouds in either sky — the upper 40% of frame is empty gradient
findings.evidence: There is no cloud geometry, cloud shader or cloud texture anywhere in the shipped kart runtime; grep for 'cloud' in ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx returns only blizzard-cloud.glb (an ITEM prop, line 42/1342/1516). In comeback-city-p0_45 everything above y≈250 is a single unbroken orange-to-black ramp for 250 vertical pixels. Penguin Village fares slightly better only because the ice-shelf plate has soft mist forms painted into it (penguin-village-p0_78), but those sit below 20° elevation — above that, nothing.
findings.whyMk8Wins: Sunshine Airport, Toad Harbor and Cloudtop Cruise all run at least two cloud layers with different scroll rates, and the clouds are what carry the eye and sell the time of day. An empty gradient sky is the visual signature of a hobby project. It is also the cheapest place in the entire frame to add perceived production value.
findings.fix: Add a procedural cloud layer to the dome fragment shader (finding 1) — zero new asset bytes. Generate a 256x256 tileable value-noise fbm ONCE at scene build into a CanvasTexture (3 octaves, lacunarity 2.0, gain 0.5; ~4ms one-time on the main thread, or reuse the existing makeNoiseTexture helper at line ~830). Sample it with the classic infinite-plane projection so clouds converge at the horizon: `vec2 cuv = d.xz / max(d.y, 0.055) * 0.020; float c = texture2D(uCloud, cuv * 1.0 + uTime * 0.0018).r * 0.62 + texture2D(uCloud, cuv * 2.7 - uTime * 0.0031).r * 0.38; c = smoothstep(0.52, 0.78, c) * smoothstep(0.05, 0.28, d.y);` then `col = mix(col, uCloudColor, c * uCloudStrength);`. CC: uCloudColor '#ff9a5e', uCloudStrength 0.55, plus a second additive pass tinted '#ffd9a0' where the cloud faces the sun (`c * pow(max(dot(d,uSunDir),0.0), 4.0) * 0.5`) for lit undersides. PV: uCloudColor '#cfe2ee', uCloudStrength 0.75 and a lower smoothstep floor (0.40, 0.72) so the storm front reads as heavy overcast rather than scattered cumulus. Two texture fetches on a full-screen dome pass — budget ~0.3ms at 0.85 render scale on desktop; gate it off on mobile via the existing raceViewport.mobile flag if the phone profile can't take it.

findings.title: The ground plane ends at 560 units and dies against the backdrop on a razor line
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:1683-1690 — `new THREE.PlaneGeometry(1120, 1060, 18, 18)` at y=-0.06, i.e. half-extent 560 from world origin. The near backdrop ring is at radius 590 and the far at 780 (lines 3957-3958), so the ground physically stops INSIDE both rings. With the player up to 350 units off origin, the ground edge is as close as 210 units — well inside the camera's useful range. In comeback-city-p0_33 the olive ground meets the skyline base on a perfectly straight horizontal edge with a 1-pixel value break: (39,58,54) at y=560 against the plate below. Same failure in penguin-village-p0_06 where the snow plane terminates on a hard line under the icebergs.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 tracks never show you the edge of the world — the ground is either extended far past the visible skybox or fully occluded by mid-ground geometry, and where it does meet the horizon it is fogged into the sky colour so there is no line at all. A visible ground-plane terminator is a level-of-detail failure a player reads as 'the map ran out'.
findings.fix: In ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:1684 change to `new THREE.PlaneGeometry(2600, 2600, 24, 24)` so the ground passes well under both backdrop rings (780 radius) with margin for the 350-unit track offset. The grass texture already uses RepeatWrapping via makeNoiseTexture, so just scale `palette.ground.repeat` from 16 to 38 to keep the same texel density. With the fog fix from finding 4 (near 300, far 1000) the extra ground fades to the horizon colour before it reaches the ring, so the terminator disappears entirely. Cost: 1152 tris instead of 648, one draw call either way, zero bytes. Also worth belt-and-braces: give the ground plane's outer ring of vertices a vertex-colour alpha ramp (or a second oversized skirt mesh at y=-0.08 in the fog colour) so it is impossible for a camera-height or fog-tuning change to re-expose the edge.

findings.title: The sky gradient stops are authored against nothing — a 10:1 luminance jump at the plate seam
findings.evidence: DUSK_SKY_STOPS (ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:866-872) tops out at '#0a0f28' = rgb(10,15,40) and Comeback City has no `sky` palette key so it uses that default verbatim. The backdrop plate it is supposed to receive is bright orange right up to where its alpha ramp starts: sampled cc-far.webp row 375 = rgb(254,106,30) at alpha 255, row 214 = rgb(255,105,32) at alpha 146, row 0 = rgb(245,93,48) at alpha 0. So the alpha ramp is cross-fading a 255-luma orange into a 15-luma navy — that is a ~10:1 luminance ratio across the blend, which is why the transition reads as a muddy brown smear rather than a fade (measured (76,20,45) and (124,32,46) mid-ramp in p0_33 at x=600). Penguin Village has the same problem in the other direction: palette.sky[0] = '#061220' = rgb(6,18,32) against pv-far.webp row 375 = rgb(134,167,180).
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8's skyboxes are single continuous paintings — there is no seam because there are no two independently authored layers that have to agree. Where MK8 does composite layers, the values are matched within a stop or two, so the composite reads as one atmosphere. Here the two halves of the sky were clearly authored in isolation.
findings.fix: Re-author the gradient stops so the colour at the plate's top-of-fade elevation matches the plate. For Comeback City, after the dome lands (finding 1) the plate occupies roughly 0-22° elevation and the fade band 15-22°, so the LUT must read ~rgb(250,100,35) at v corresponding to 22° and ramp to a deep dusk blue only well above that. Concrete replacement for DUSK_SKY_STOPS: `[[0,'#0d1233'],[0.34,'#2a2358'],[0.58,'#6b3468'],[0.76,'#b84f4a'],[0.88,'#f0722a'],[1,'#ff8c3a']]` — note the top (v=1, horizon end of the LUT) is now the plate's orange, and the previously-black zenith is lifted to #0d1233 so the vignette doesn't crush it to (0,0,8). For Penguin Village, edit the `sky` array in src/game/race/tracks/penguinVillage.js to `[[0,'#0b1c30'],[0.40,'#1a3b54'],[0.64,'#33607a'],[0.82,'#6d9db2'],[1,'#a8c8d8']]` so its top matches pv-far's rgb(134,167,180)-to-rgb(224,248,247) band. Validate numerically, not by eye: sample the dome LUT at the plate's top elevation and assert deltaE < 8 against cc-far/pv-far row 375.

findings.title: Penguin Village fog is cold grey-blue under a warm cream horizon glow
findings.evidence: src/game/race/tracks/penguinVillage.js palette: `fog: { color: '#4a6478', near: 150, far: 680 }` = rgb(74,100,120), a desaturated cold blue. But pv-far.webp's horizon band is warm: row 536 = rgb(164,188,178), row 1071 = rgb(224,248,247), and the frames show a distinctly gold/cream glow along the ice shelf (penguin-village-p0_45 and -p0_78 both show warm yellow rims on the iceberg silhouettes). Measured in penguin-village-p0_45 at x=200: (184,217,228) at y=440 and (205,219,224) at y=520 — the near ground is BRIGHTER than the distant ground, which is aerial perspective in reverse for an overcast arctic scene.
findings.whyMk8Wins: Mount Wario and Sherbet Land keep the fog tint locked to the sky's own horizon hue, so snow at distance lifts toward the sky and the whole valley reads as one volume of air. Here the mid-ground snow is cooler and darker than the near snow while the sky behind it is warm — the two atmospheres are fighting.
findings.fix: Change penguinVillage.js palette to `fog: { color: '#9fb8c4', near: 210, far: 900 }`. Raising the colour from rgb(74,100,120) to rgb(159,184,196) makes distant snow lift toward the plate instead of dropping below it; pushing near from 150 to 210 stops the haze from creeping onto the drivable ribbon (at 150 the road 150 units ahead is already 0% but the first rival ahead of you is already picking up haze). Also raise far from 680 to 900 now that camera.far is 1800 with the backdrop on — 680 was set under the stale `fog.far <= 840` comment at ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3866. Watch the bloom interaction: the palette comment warns snow sits near the bloom threshold, so after this change re-capture penguin-village-p0_45 and confirm the mid-ground does not cross luminanceThreshold 1.0 (line 4002) into white-out; if it does, drop hemi.intensity from 3 to 2.8 rather than re-darkening the fog.

findings.title: No time-of-day anchor in world space — nothing tells you where the light is coming from
findings.evidence: The DirectionalLight key is at (-150, 52, -70) (ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3883) = azimuth ~245°, elevation ~18°. The sun discs the player actually sees come from the tiled plate (finding 2) and therefore appear in five different directions, none of which is 245°. So the shading direction on the karts and the apparent sun position in the sky are uncorrelated. There is also no crepuscular/horizon-glow lobe: comeback-city-p0_9 shows a sun disc at x≈760 with no surrounding sky brightening at all — the pixel 200px to its left is the same orange as the pixel 200px to its right.
findings.whyMk8Wins: On Sunshine Airport the sun's position, the warm rim on every kart, the long shadows and the glow lobe in the sky all agree, so the scene reads as a specific moment of a specific day. That coherence is most of what people mean when they say MK8 'looks expensive'. Here the lighting is arbitrary relative to the sky.
findings.fix: After moving the sun into the dome shader (finding 2), drive both from one source of truth. Add to raceSceneTheme.js per-track: `sunAzimuth` (CC 248°, PV 195°) and `sunElevation` (CC 7°, PV 12° — lower than the current 18° reads more like sunset). In createScene, compute `const sd = new THREE.Vector3().setFromSphericalCoords(1, THREE.MathUtils.degToRad(90 - elev), THREE.MathUtils.degToRad(azim));` then set `sun.position.copy(sd).multiplyScalar(200)` AND `skyMaterial.uniforms.uSunDir.value.copy(sd)`. Add the broad glow lobe in the fragment (the `pow(sd, 3.0) * 0.08` term from finding 2) so the sky brightens over ~50° around the sun — that lobe is what makes a sunset sky read as lit air rather than a gradient. Also anchor the existing bloom to it: the sun disc term should exceed BloomEffect's luminanceThreshold of 1.0 (line 4002), so emit the disc at 2.2x uSunColor as specified, which gives you a free authored sun bloom instead of the current flat yellow circle.

findings.title: Backdrop plates have no anisotropy and mip-blur at grazing angles
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3938-3941 sets colorSpace, wrapS and repeat.x on the loaded texture but never touches anisotropy, minFilter or generateMipmaps. A 2560px plate wrapped 5x onto a 64-segment cylinder at radius 780 is heavily minified and viewed at grazing angles at the frame edges, so the GPU picks a coarse mip and the skyline goes soft. Visible in comeback-city-p0_33 where the towers at the left and right thirds are noticeably mushier than those near the frame centre, and in penguin-village-p0_78 where the left-side ice shelf loses its gold crack detail entirely.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8's distant skyline elements stay crisp across the whole frame — the silhouette edges are what carry the read at that distance, and softening them makes the horizon feel like a low-res JPEG. This is free to fix.
findings.fix: In addBackdropRing's loader callback (ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3938) add `texture.anisotropy = renderer.capabilities.getMaxAnisotropy();` (typically 16 on desktop, 4-8 on mobile — cap at 8 when raceViewport.mobile to protect the phone budget) and `texture.minFilter = THREE.LinearMipmapLinearFilter;`. Also raise the cylinder's radial segments from 64 to 96 in line 3943 so the UV interpolation across each segment does not shear the skyline — at radius 780 a 64-segment ring has 76-unit facets, which is enough to visibly kink vertical building edges. Cost: 64 extra tris on a depth-write-off, single-draw-call mesh.

findings.title: Vignette crushes the exposed sky to pure black, amplifying the seam
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:4008 `new VignetteEffect({ offset: 0.32, darkness: 0.45 })`. Measured top-right corner (1590,2) reads (0,0,8) in comeback-city-p0_45/-p0_67/-p0_78/-p0_9 — the DUSK_SKY_STOPS top of rgb(10,15,40) is driven to essentially zero. That turns the region above the backdrop rim into dead black, which maximises the contrast of the arc from finding 1 and makes the upper corners of the frame read as letterboxing.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 uses no meaningful vignette; its frame corners carry as much sky information as the centre. A vignette that reaches 0 is only acceptable when there is texture underneath it to protect — over an empty gradient it just deletes a quarter of the image.
findings.fix: Once the dome and clouds land (findings 1 and 6) there is content in the corners worth protecting, so keep the vignette but back it off: `new VignetteEffect({ offset: 0.42, darkness: 0.30 })`. offset 0.32 -> 0.42 pushes the darkening start outward past where the cloud deck lives; darkness 0.45 -> 0.30 keeps the corner at roughly 70% instead of 55%, which preserves the lifted zenith #0d1233 from finding 8 as a visible blue rather than black. Re-verify against the owner's 2026-07-06 post-lab sign-off with a fresh A/B capture at p0_45 on both tracks before shipping, since the vignette was an explicit owner pick.

pillar: Environment art, set dressing and world density
verdictVsMk8: Blind side-by-side, both tracks read clearly worse than any MK8DX course, and for a structural reason rather than an art-quality one: the world has exactly two depth layers — a thin 40-unit ribbon of trackside props and a painted billboard ring 590 units out — with an unbroken 500-unit band of flat, untextured ground between them. Comeback City's palette and the Miami asset set are genuinely strong and the neon-dusk key reads as stylized-AAA, but the frames are empty at mid-distance, there is not one crowd, grandstand, banner wall or moving set piece anywhere, and the backdrop ring has visible tiling bugs (two suns simultaneously in comeback-city-p0_67, mirrored duplicate towers) plus a hard curved seam where the sky goes dead-black. Penguin Village is materially worse: it is white-on-white at every value, the backdrop is scale-blown to 4x on half the lap because the ring is centred on world origin while the track is not, and its props are lower-contrast than its ground. MK8 wins because every one of its courses fills the 50-200m band with authored silhouette geometry, puts an animated crowd at the start/finish, and gives you one big slow-moving landmark to track over a lap — this build has none of the three.

findings.title: Backdrop ring tiles the baked sun and landmark towers — two suns visible at once
findings.evidence: tmp/aaa-visual/baseline/comeback-city-p0_67.png shows TWO identical yellow sun discs in frame simultaneously (screen x≈690 and x≈960); comeback-city-p0_9.png shows the sun plus a mirrored partial twin at frame left. comeback-city-p0_24.png shows two bilaterally-mirrored spiky tower pairs. Cause: src/game/ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3940-3941 sets texture.wrapS = THREE.MirroredRepeatWrapping and texture.repeat.x = repeats, with repeats=5 for the far strip (line 3957) and 7 for the near strip (line 3958). The sun and the hero towers are baked INTO those strips, so a unique landmark is repeated 5 and 7 times around the ring and the 66° FOV (line 3870) regularly frames two of them.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 treats a sun/moon and every hero backdrop landmark as a singleton — Toad Harbour has one sunset, Sunshine Airport has one control tower. A duplicated sun is read instantly by any player as a rendering bug, and mirrored tiling makes every far building look like a Rorschach blot instead of architecture.
findings.fix: In src/game/ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3936 extend addBackdropRing with a `unique` option. When unique: build the ring as a partial cylinder — `new THREE.CylinderGeometry(radius, radius, height, 24, 1, true, sunYaw - 0.55, 1.1)` — and set `texture.wrapS = THREE.ClampToEdgeWrapping; texture.repeat.x = 1`. Pick sunYaw to match the authored key light (sun.position -150,52,-70 at line 3886 → Math.atan2(-150,-70) ≈ -2.0 rad). Split the far layer into two calls: the unique sun/glow wedge, and the tileable city band with the sun masked out (asset-pipeline edit to cc-far.webp / pv-far.webp, no byte increase — these are 49 KiB and 35 KiB). Also switch the tiled bands from MirroredRepeatWrapping to THREE.RepeatWrapping so towers stop appearing in mirror pairs; the strips are already authored to tile. If the pipeline edit cannot land immediately, ship the sun procedurally instead: reuse makeGlowTexture() (line 886) on a 220-unit Sprite at radius 900, sunYaw bearing, y 90 — zero bytes.

findings.title: Backdrop rings are pinned to world origin, so backdrop scale swings 10x over a lap
