findings.evidence: tmp/aaa-visual/baseline/penguin-village-p0_9.png: a single ice cliff fills the right third of the frame, visibly texture-filtered and soft, at roughly 4x the scale it reads at in penguin-village-p0_33.png. penguin-village-p0_78.png shows the same blow-up on the right. Cause: src/game/ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3944-3956 sets only `ring.position.y = y`, so both rings sit at world (0,0). Penguin Village's waypoints (src/game/race/tracks/penguinVillage.js:13-21) span x[-470,480], z[-300,250]. With near radius 590 (line 3958), the near ring is ~110 units from the kart at one end of the lap and ~1070 at the other.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 backdrops either sit far enough out that lap position is irrelevant, or are camera-anchored. A backdrop whose apparent size quadruples as you drive destroys the sense of world scale — in p0_9 the 'distant iceberg field' momentarily reads as a wall you are about to hit.
findings.fix: Tag each ring with a parallax factor and follow the camera. verdictVsMk8: Blind side-by-side, this loses to MK8DX badly the moment your eye lands on any actual surface. The silhouette/colour composition is genuinely good — the neon dusk skyline and arctic storm-front read as authored art — but every surface underneath is pure Lambert: there is no `scene.environment`/IBL anywhere in the shipped monolith, so all ~40 `MeshStandardMaterial` instances (road, ground, buildings, kart bodies) resolve to flat diffuse with an invisible specular lobe, and MK8's entire material read is specular + detail-normal + albedo texture. The road is a 256px canvas of blurry rectangles stretched across 50 world units with no grain, no sheen and no arc-length UV; the curbs are painted 2D ribbons whose "checker" is silently destroyed by vertex-colour interpolation; the GLB buildings are forced to `MeshBasicMaterial` so they sit in the sunset as fullbright stickers with the wrong light direction. Penguin Village's ice/snow surface bands exist only in physics — the player is asked to slide on something that is pixel-identical to tarmac. With frameWorkMs at ~1.0ms and 480–782 draw calls there is enormous GPU headroom, so essentially none of this is a performance decision; it is unspent budget.

findings.title: No scene.environment / IBL: the entire world is pure Lambert with a dead specular lobe
findings.evidence: grep for `envMap|PMREM|environment =` across src/game/ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx returns ZERO hits. Lighting is only HemisphereLight + 2 DirectionalLights (ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3874-3897). Every surface material is built by createBasicMaterial (src/game/race/render/createKartModel.js:9-16) = MeshStandardMaterial{metalness:0.02, roughness:0.68}. With metalness ~0 and no env map, three's PBR specular contributes essentially nothing, so `metalness` on the road (jsx:1664) and kart body (createKartModel.js:33) is currently a no-op that only darkens diffuse. Frames: comeback-city-p0_45 — the purple rival kart, the road, the curb stack and the palm all sit at exactly the same shading complexity (flat tone + fog); no surface anywhere in the frame carries a highlight.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 lights everything against a baked environment probe. That is why an MK8 kart shell has a moving sky-coloured sheen band across it, why the road brightens toward the horizon, why chrome trim and ice read as different materials from plastic and paint. Remove the env probe from MK8 and it looks exactly like this frame does.
findings.fix: Add a PMREM environment built from a throwaway procedural scene — zero bytes, one-time cost. In ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx right after `scene.background = makeSkyTexture(palette.sky)` (line 3863): build a `THREE.Scene` containing a single inverted `SphereGeometry(1,32,16)` with a `ShaderMaterial` painting the SAME `palette.sky` gradient stops plus a warm sun disc at the `sun.position` direction (reuse makeSkyTexture's canvas as the map on a BackSide sphere is the 5-line version); then `const pmrem = new THREE.PMREMGenerator(renderer); pmrem.compileEquirectangularShader(); scene.environment = pmrem.fromScene(envScene, 0, 1, 100).texture; pmrem.dispose(); envScene.dispose()`. Cost ~2-4ms once at scene build, 256px cube. Then set envMapIntensity per family so it does not wash the art direction out: road/ground 0.35, buildings & procedural scenery 0.5, kart body/trim/glass 1.0, ice & rails 1.2. Add an `envMapIntensity` option pass-through to createBasicMaterial's options spread so callers can set it inline. MeshToonMaterial ignores env in r184 — leave drivers/icebergs alone here, they are covered by the toon-ramp finding.

findings.title: buildCheckerRibbon's checker is silently destroyed by vertex-colour interpolation — every curb and barrier is a smooth gradient smear
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:1705-1738. The ribbon pushes exactly 2 vertices per sample index and indexes adjacent quads off SHARED vertices (`const a = index*2; indices.push(a,a+1,a+2,...)`), while the checker colour is written per-vertex at line 1722-1723 (`Math.floor(index/checkerEvery) % 2 === 0 ? colorA : colorB`). Shared vertices + smooth varying interpolation means alternating colours blend into each other instead of forming blocks — `checkerEvery` is functionally dead. Proof in the frame: crop of comeback-city-p0_06 at the left curb stack shows the barrier band as a continuous red→salmon→pink→magenta GRADIENT running down the track, and the curb as a soft white-to-pink wash, not the red/white teeth the code intends. Same on the right stack in comeback-city-p0_9.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8's rumble strips are crisp, high-contrast, hard-edged alternating blocks at a fixed world period. They are the single strongest 'you are at the edge of the road' signal in the game and they read at 200cc speed. Here the edge signal is a mushy pastel gradient that at speed reads as one more neon stripe.
findings.fix: Stop encoding the checker in vertex colour. In buildCheckerRibbon (jsx:1694), add a `uv` attribute instead: `uvs.push(0, arcLength/period, 1, arcLength/period)` where arcLength accumulates real world distance along the ribbon and period = 6.0 world units (MK8-ish tooth pitch), and drive the colour from a 2×1 `THREE.DataTexture` of [colorA, colorB] with `minFilter/magFilter = NearestFilter`, `wrapT = RepeatWrapping`. Keep vertexColors ONLY for the single-colour callers (shoulder at jsx:1818, railTop at jsx:1858) which pass colorA===colorB. This also fixes the checker period drifting with corner radius, because arc-length UV is radius-independent where `index/checkerEvery` is not. Alternative if you want to keep vertex colours: un-index the geometry (duplicate the 2 verts per quad) so each tooth owns its own vertices — cheaper to write, costs ~4KB of extra verts per ribbon, acceptable.

findings.title: Road asphalt has no surface material at all — a 256px canvas of blurry rectangles stretched across 50 world units, no arc-length UV, no grain, no sheen
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:1648-1668 builds the road map via makeNoiseTexture (jsx:831-862) at 256×256 with `repeat: 1`, and the road UVs at jsx:1637 are `uvs.push(0, index*0.4, 1, index*0.4)` — U spans 0→1 across the FULL road width (~50-58 units) and V steps by sample INDEX, not arc length. Result: ~5 texels per world unit across the road, so each 2-4px speckle becomes a ~0.5-unit blob that is 30-60 screen pixels near the camera. Cropped/upscaled road region of comeback-city-p0_06 and of penguin-village-p0_24 show exactly this: a dozen individually countable soft navy rectangles floating on flat colour. There is no high-frequency grain, no directional wear, no wet band. `anisotropy` is hardcoded to 4 (jsx:860) rather than renderer.capabilities.getMaxAnisotropy(), which smears it further at grazing angles — which is 90% of the screen.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8's road carries three simultaneous frequencies: a macro albedo variation (patches, repairs, tyre-line darkening on the racing line), a ~1-2m detail grain, and a normal/roughness map that catches the key light into a moving anisotropic sheen band. That sheen band is the primary speed cue in the game — it slides toward you as you accelerate. Right now this road is a matte painted plane and contributes zero speed sensation.
findings.fix: Three changes in addTrack (jsx:1627-1671), all zero-byte. (1) Fix the UVs: keep `u` mapped to lane position but scale it to world units — `u = ±halfWidth/2.0` — and make `v` accumulate real arc length / 2.0 so one texture tile = 2×2 world metres regardless of corner radius; set `asphaltTexture.repeat.set(1,1)` and let the UVs do the tiling. (2) Add a procedural detail normal: generate a 256×256 grayscale value-noise canvas once (reuse makeNoiseTexture's deterministic LCG), convert to a tangent-space normal by central differences into an RGB canvas, assign as `normalMap` with `normalScale = new THREE.Vector2(0.35, 0.35)`, and a matching `roughnessMap` (invert the same noise, remap to 0.45-0.75) so the grain modulates specular not just albedo. Requires `geometry.computeTangents()` or set `material.normalMapType = THREE.TangentSpaceNormalMap` with the derivative fallback three ships. (3) Add a wet-sheen shader injection through `addShaderInjection` (src/game/race/render/toonRimShader.js:41) named `road-sheen-v1`, anchor `#include <opaque_fragment>`: `float sheen = pow(saturate(dot(reflect(-geometryViewDir, geometryNormal), normalize(uSunDir))), 24.0); outgoingLight += uSheenColor * uSheenStrength * sheen;` with uSheenColor = palette.sunColor, uSheenStrength 0.25 for Comeback City / 0.4 for Penguin Village. Also raise anisotropy to `renderer.capabilities.getMaxAnisotropy()` (jsx:860, 429, 451).

findings.title: Every GLB building and prop is force-converted to MeshBasicMaterial — fullbright stickers with the wrong light direction
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:1078 in mountMiamiAsset: `node.material = new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({ map: node.material?.map || null })`. Same pattern at jsx:1456 (fitItemPropScene) and jsx:4129, jsx:5325. Frame proof: cropped comeback-city-p0_06 — the ice-cream truck and the deco hotel are lit from front-left with soft neutral studio light baked into their textures, while the scene's key light is a low orange sun BEHIND them (sun.position -150,52,-70, jsx:3883). Their shadow sides are as bright as their lit sides, their whites stay pure white against an orange dusk, and their baked texture grain is at a completely different frequency from everything else in the frame. They read as cut-out decals pasted onto the world, not objects in it.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8's course props are lit by the same key/fill/env as the karts, so a building's road-facing facade goes warm at sunset and its far side falls into the ambient tint. That shared lighting is what makes MK8's worlds feel solid rather than collaged. Here the props actively fight the authored dusk that everything else obeys.
findings.fix: In mountMiamiAsset (jsx:1076-1085) swap to `new THREE.MeshLambertMaterial({ map: node.material?.map || null })` — cheapest possible lit path, no specular cost, and it immediately picks up the hemi + sun + rim already in the scene. If the baked textures then read too dark against the dusk, use `new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ map, roughness: 0.9, metalness: 0, envMapIntensity: 0.5 })` once the PMREM env from finding 1 exists, which gives the facades sky bounce on the shadow side. Keep MeshBasicMaterial ONLY for the two families that genuinely want fullbright: the item projectile props (jsx:1456, correct as-is by design) and the backdrop rings (jsx:3944). Add a one-line guard so a GLB carrying an emissive map keeps it. Draw calls unchanged; Lambert vs Basic is ~1-2 extra ALU ops per fragment at 480 draw calls and ~1.0ms frame work — free.

findings.title: Penguin Village's ice and snow surface bands are physics-only — the player slides on something visually identical to tarmac
findings.evidence: src/game/race/tracks/penguinVillage.js:74-79 declares surfaceBands: ice across the full road from progress 0.24-0.42 with snow on the outer lanes. grep for `surfaceBands|'ice'` across ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx and src/game/race/render/ returns hits ONLY in src/game/race/physics/surfacePhysics.js:60-64. Frame proof: penguin-village-p0_24 is the exact start of the ice band and the road is the same dark navy asphalt with the same speckle map as penguin-village-p0_67 (asphalt band) and penguin-village-p0_9. The only cyan on the road is the boost-pad/rail glow bleed, not a surface.
findings.whyMk8Wins: Sherbet Land and Mount Wario telegraph every grip change with a completely different material — mirror-bright low-roughness ice with sky reflection and a specular streak, or matte high-albedo packed snow with a soft ridge. In MK8 you steer differently a full second before you reach the ice because you can SEE it. Here a grip change arrives with no visual warning at all, which reads to a player as a physics bug.
findings.fix: Add a per-vertex surface weight to the road mesh and blend materials in the shader. In addTrack's road build loop (jsx:1630-1642), for each of the 2 vertices per sample call `surfaceTypeAt({progress, lane}, trackDef.surfaceBands)` (already exported from src/game/race/physics/surfacePhysics.js:60) and push a Float32 `aSurface` attribute: 0=asphalt, 1=ice, 2=snow. Then register a `road-surface-blend-v1` injection through addShaderInjection on the road material: varying float vSurface from the vertex shader; in the fragment at `#include <opaque_fragment>` lerp toward ice (albedo × vec3(0.55,0.85,1.0), add a hard specular `pow(NdotH, 90.0) * 1.4` in palette.rimLightColor, and lower effective roughness by writing `roughnessFactor` before lights_fragment_begin via a second injection at `#include <roughnessmap_fragment>`: `roughnessFactor = mix(roughnessFactor, 0.08, iceWeight)`) and toward snow (albedo lerp to vec3(0.92,0.96,1.0), roughness → 0.95, plus a fine sparkle `step(0.985, hash(vUv*400.0))`). Because the vertex attribute is smooth, the band edges get a free 1-2 unit feather instead of a hard seam. Also add a matching cheap decal ring: nothing else needed. ~30 lines, no new geometry, no new draw calls.

findings.title: Curbs are unlit painted 2D ribbons, not extruded rumble strips — no vertical face, no shading break, no bump
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:1831-1842 calls buildCheckerRibbon with `unlit: true` (→ MeshBasicMaterial at jsx:1743) and `yBottom: 0.32, yTop: 0.18` — a near-horizontal ribbon that DROPS 0.14 units outward. So the curb has no vertical face at all, and being MeshBasicMaterial it receives no light, meaning its top face cannot differ in value from the road's top face by anything except albedo. Crop of comeback-city-p0_06's left edge: road → shoulder → curb → wall is five perfectly flat parallel stripes with zero value break at any boundary; nothing has thickness. Same at both edges of comeback-city-p0_9 and penguin-village-p0_45.
findings.whyMk8Wins: An MK8 curb is a real extruded strip: chamfered top face catching the key light, a darker vertical outer face, and a hard shadow line where it meets the tarmac. That geometry+shading break is what makes the track feel built rather than painted, and it also makes the drift-onto-the-curb moment feel physical.
findings.fix: Extend buildCheckerRibbon to emit a 3-vertex profile per sample instead of 2: inner-bottom at road height, inner-top at +0.20, outer-top at +0.20, outer-bottom at road height — i.e. a small extruded box cross-section 0.20 units proud, ~1.5-2.5 units wide (already driven by curbWidthAt, jsx:1620). Emit both the top quad strip and the outer vertical quad strip in one geometry, with `computeVertexNormals()` giving the top face an up normal and the outer face a sideways normal. Drop `unlit: true` at jsx:1837 so the curb uses the lit branch (jsx:1744) — with the PMREM env from finding 1 it will then pick up a sky sheen on the top face. Add the 2×1 nearest-filtered checker texture from finding 2 so the teeth are crisp. Cost: ~330 extra verts per curb ribbon, 0 extra draw calls (same mesh).

findings.title: The 4-step neutral-grey toon ramp saturates on every bright-albedo object — Penguin Village's ice collapses into white mush
findings.evidence: getToonGradient (ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:906-920) is a 4-texel neutral ramp [90,150,215,255]. Penguin Village's hemi runs at intensity 3.0 with sky #689bb8 (penguinVillage.js palette.hemi) plus a 2.6 sun and a 2.0 rim. makeIceberg (jsx:2956-2976) uses createToonMaterial('#cfe6f5', emissive #7fb8d8) — a 0.81-luma albedo. Under that light budget essentially every lit facet lands in the ramp's top texel (255) so the whole object flattens to one white tone. Frame proof: penguin-village-p0_06 — the four foreground iceberg cones, the pyramid peaks and the snow ground plane are all the same value; the only thing separating them is the silhouette edge. penguin-village-p0_24 is worse: the entire mid-ground from the horizon to the road shoulder is a single undifferentiated white field.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 keeps form in white snow with a cool ambient occlusion in the crevices, a warm key on the sunlit faces and a genuine specular sparkle — three separable values on one white object. Here white ice is a single flat value and reads as unfinished greybox rather than art.
findings.fix: Two parts. (1) Replace the neutral 4-step ramp with a 5-step TINTED ramp and make it per-track: build the DataTexture from `palette.toonRamp` with a cool shadow and a warm light — Penguin Village e.g. [ (74,96,124), (120,150,178), (176,206,226), (226,240,250), (255,255,255) ], Comeback City e.g. [ (58,46,86), (110,80,120), (176,126,132), (226,176,150), (255,230,196) ]. Keep NearestFilter. Cache per-track in the existing sharedToonGradient slot keyed by trackDef.key. (2) Reduce the top-band pileup: drop makeIceberg's albedo from #cfe6f5 to ~#9fc0d8 and its emissive from 0.22 to 0.08 (jsx:2958) — the ramp's brightest step will still hit pure white on sun-facing facets, giving you a real two-value read instead of one. Verify with a re-capture of penguin-village-p0_06 that the iceberg cones now show distinct lit/shadow facets.

findings.title: Terrain is one 1120×1060 quad with a 70-unit noise tile — it has no material read anywhere in the frame
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:1673-1690: a single `PlaneGeometry(1120, 1060, 18, 18)` with `MeshStandardMaterial{map: grassTexture, roughness: 0.92}`, where grassTexture is makeNoiseTexture at repeat 16 → one 256px tile per ~70 world units, i.e. ~3.6 texels per unit and a 70-unit repeat period that is invisible at any playable distance. Frame proof: crop of comeback-city-p0_9 — the ground band between the track and the skyline backdrop is a completely uniform olive-grey field, with a razor-straight horizon where it meets the backdrop ring. comeback-city-p0_06 shows the same for the near grass on both sides of the track. In Penguin Village (penguin-village-p0_06) the white-on-white speckles are invisible and the snow field is a pure flat plane.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8's off-track terrain always has at least two frequencies (a mown-stripe or drift pattern plus a grain) and a darkening where it meets the track, so the road sits IN the world instead of ON it. It also biases terrain colour under the track edge so the eye reads a soft contact.
findings.fix: (1) Drop the tile to ~8 world units: `texture.repeat.set(140, 132)` for the 1120×1060 plane, and raise anisotropy to getMaxAnisotropy() so it does not smear. (2) Add a macro variation layer via a second injection (`terrain-macro-v1`) rather than a second texture: in the fragment, `float macro = noise(vWorldPos.xz * 0.012); diffuseColor.rgb *= mix(0.86, 1.10, macro);` using a cheap 2D value-noise helper — zero bytes, breaks the flat field into readable landform. (3) Bake a track-proximity AO into the plane's vertex colours: subdivide to 96×96 (from 18×18) and, per vertex, compute distance to the nearest centreline sample and multiply vertex colour by `smoothstep(0, 14, dist) * 0.35 + 0.65` so a soft dark halo hugs the road; set `vertexColors: true`. That single change is what gives the road contact grounding now that shadowMap is 384px BasicShadowMap (jsx:3859-3860). (4) For Penguin Village add the sparkle from finding 5 to the snow plane.

findings.title: Barrier walls are zero-thickness double-sided ribbons with identical front and back shading
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:1843-1854: the wall call passes `innerMul: barrierMulAt` and `outerMul: barrierMulAt` — identical — so the ribbon has zero horizontal width; it is a single vertical quad strip from y+0.02 to y+2.6, rendered `side: THREE.DoubleSide` (jsx:1748). It has no top cap, no thickness, and because computeVertexNormals on a degenerate-width strip gives one normal, the track-facing and back faces shade identically. Frame proof: crop of comeback-city-p0_06's left edge and the right stack in comeback-city-p0_9 — the 'wall' is a flat coloured band with no top edge highlight and no visible depth; it does not occlude anything behind it because it is paper-thin, so nothing behind the barrier is ever hidden.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 barriers are boxed sections with a lit top cap, a distinct inner face, and a visible thickness at every corner — they read as objects that would stop a kart. This reads as a coloured sticker standing on edge, which undermines the whole 'the track is built' impression that the curb + barrier stack is supposed to sell.
findings.fix: Extend buildCheckerRibbon (or add a sibling buildWallProfile) to emit 4 profile vertices per sample — inner-bottom, inner-top, outer-top, outer-bottom with `outerMul = innerMul + 0.8/width` (a ~0.8-unit thick wall) — emitting the inner face, the top cap and the outer face as one indexed geometry, then `side: THREE.FrontSide` (drop DoubleSide, jsx:1748). Give the top cap its own colour row so the existing railTop ribbon (jsx:1858-1874) can be deleted, saving 2 draw calls per track. Combine with the crisp checker from finding 2 so the alternating wall panels actually read as panels.

findings.title: Emissive is used as the universal glow lever but almost every value sits below the bloom threshold, so it washes albedo instead of glowing
findings.evidence: The shipped bloom is `luminanceThreshold: 1.0` with `luminanceSmoothing: 0.22` (ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:4002-4003). Meanwhile the vast majority of emissive calls pass intensities well under 1: barrierMat 0.08, lineMat 0.12, skirtMat 0.15, curbs none, apexMat 0.26, windowMat 0.28, tree accents 0.16-0.18, kart bodyMat 0.08 (createKartModel.js:33). These never cross threshold, so their only effect is to flatten the material — emissive adds unconditionally regardless of the light direction, which is precisely what kills the shading break on the shadow side of every object that has it. There is also no `emissiveMap` anywhere in the shipped path, so emissive is all-or-nothing per mesh — a building cannot have glowing windows and a matte facade on the same mesh.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 separates 'this material is bright' from 'this material emits'. Neon signage genuinely blooms; the surface it is mounted on does not. Here the sub-threshold emissive spreads a uniform haze over surfaces that should be reading form, and every 'glowing' element glows over its whole mesh.
findings.fix: Two passes. (1) Audit the emissive calls: anything under 0.30 that is NOT meant to bloom should have its emissive removed and its base `color` lifted instead (barrierMat, skirtMat, kart bodyMat, tree accents) — this restores the light/shadow break for free. (2) Anything meant to actually glow — lane markings (jsx:1879, currently 0.65), boost-pad rails, rail caps, item boxes (createRacePickups.js:29-31 at 0.92, and the shipped equivalent in the monolith) — should be pushed to 1.4-2.2 so it clears the 1.0 threshold with the 0.22 knee. (3) For mixed-read surfaces (building facades with lit windows), generate a tiny emissive mask canvas from the same makeNoiseTexture LCG (jsx:831) with white window rectangles on black, assign as `emissiveMap` with `emissive: '#74f1ff', emissiveIntensity: 1.8` — one 128px canvas per building family, zero bundle bytes, and it gives you glowing windows on a matte facade for the first time.

findings.title: Lane markings are floating boxes 0.13 units above the road, not paint on the surface
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:1877-1889: each dash is a `BoxGeometry(1.15, 0.08, 11.5)` positioned at `point.y + 0.22`, while the road surface sits at `point.y + 0.05` (jsx:1634-1635). The dash's bottom face is therefore ~0.13 units above the tarmac and its side faces are visible. Frame proof: the upscaled road crop of penguin-village-p0_24 shows the yellow centre dash with a distinct darker edge along its right side — that is the box's vertical face catching a different normal. The 0.08-thick slab also means the dash silhouettes against the horizon at low camera pitch.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8's road paint is in the road texture or a coplanar decal — it never has thickness, so it deforms exactly with the surface and never separates from it. A dash that is visibly a floating slab is the kind of detail that reads as 'made in an engine' rather than 'authored'.
findings.fix: Replace the per-dash boxes with paint baked into the road material. Best version: add the dash pattern into the road's arc-length UV from finding 3 — a `stripeMap` sampled at `fract(v * dashPeriod)` masking a paint colour into diffuseColor in the existing road shader injection, driven by `laneMarkings.mode` and `everySamples` so the data schema is unchanged. This also deletes ~28 draw calls per track. Cheaper interim version if you do not want to touch the road shader: swap `BoxGeometry` for `PlaneGeometry(1.15, 11.5)` rotated flat at `point.y + 0.06` with `polygonOffset: true, polygonOffsetFactor: -2, polygonOffsetUnits: -2` on the shared lineMat, and let them merge into a single BufferGeometry via three's mergeGeometries so they stay one draw call.

findings.title: The material modules the audit brief points at are dead code — every shipped material lives in the monolith
findings.evidence: grep of the monolith's imports shows only 5 files from src/game/race/render/ are reachable from the shipped path: raceParticles.js, createKartModel.js (createBasicMaterial only), createRaceScene.js (renderer + fit helpers only — createRaceSceneShell with its lights at lines 97-127 is NOT imported), gltfLoader.js, toonRimShader.js. createTrackMesh.js (createTrackRenderMaterials at lines 6-29, 15 materials), createRaceScenery.js (~60 materials), createRacePickups.js and createRaceVehicles.js are reachable ONLY through src/game/race/raceSceneRuntime.js, which is imported ONLY by src/game/ArcadeRace3D.jsx — declared dead legacy. So the '22 MeshBasicMaterial / 2 MeshStandardMaterial / 1 MeshToonMaterial' census describes code that never renders.
findings.whyMk8Wins: Not a visual gap — an execution-risk gap. Every fix in this report has to land in ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx; a well-meaning engineer editing createTrackMesh.js's asphaltMat or the nice-looking createRaceSceneShell lighting will ship exactly nothing, and the next audit will read the same misleading census.
findings.fix: Either delete src/game/race/render/createTrackMesh.js, createRaceScenery.js, createRaceVehicles.js, src/game/race/raceSceneRuntime.js and src/game/ArcadeRace3D.jsx outright (also removes them from the kart bundle, reclaiming gzip headroom for nothing), or add a one-line banner comment at the top of each — `// DEAD: legacy ArcadeRace3D path only. Shipped kart materials live in src/game/ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx.` Do the deletion first and re-run test:bundle:kart against a FRESH build; the freed bytes are the cheapest headroom available for anything in this report that ever does need an asset.

verdictVsMk8: Blind side-by-side this loses badly, and the reason is measurable rather than subjective: I decoded the baseline PNGs and **not one scene pixel in either track exceeds luminance 241, and 0.000% of the frame exceeds 240** (CC p0_9 max 233, PV p0_45 max 230 — the brightest pixel in the whole capture is the HUD's DOM text at 250.7). MK8DX frames clip to white constantly — sun, coin spin, boost flame, item-box sparkle — and that clipped core is what bloom hangs off. Here the top end is dead, so the bloom at threshold 1.0 has almost nothing to catch, and the composition reads as a flat matte. On top of that the chain is a single merged EffectPass whose effects run in the wrong colour spaces (SMAA and Vignette both execute on linear HDR *before* ACES), there is no grade of any kind — the identical chain is applied to a track whose histogram is 17% crushed black and to a track that is 48% above 200 with mean saturation 0.32 — and dithering is off, so the CC sky carries 7-15px-wide constant-colour contour bands. MK8's presentation is one authored look per course; this is an un-graded ACES dump.

findings.title: SMAA runs mid-chain on linear HDR and its shader re-samples inputBuffer, deleting bloom on every anti-aliased edge
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3992-4011 pushes [Bloom, SMAA, Vignette, ToneMapping] into ONE EffectPass. node_modules/postprocessing/build/index.js:10945 — SMAA's mainImage ends with `color = blendingWeight.x*texture2D(inputBuffer, blendingCoord.xy); color += blendingWeight.y*texture2D(inputBuffer, blendingCoord.zw); outputColor = color;` — it OVERWRITES the accumulated colour with fresh taps from the pass input buffer. In a merged pass that input is the raw, un-bloomed scene render. Every pixel SMAA flags as an edge therefore loses 100% of the bloom that effect e0 just added, and only then gets vignetted and tone-mapped. Visible in comeback-city-p0_9.png: the white lamp orb at ~(1215,400) has a halo in the surrounding pixels but a hard, un-glowing rim exactly on its silhouette; same on the neon kerb strips. Secondary defect: SMAA's edge-detection threshold (0.1, EdgeDetectionMode.COLOR) is calibrated for perceptually-encoded LDR, but it is being fed linear HDR where a 0.1 delta is meaningless in the toe — which is why the dark tower silhouettes in comeback-city-p0_33.png are jagged while bright edges over-detect.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8DX resolves AA on the final display-referred image, so glow, grade and vignette survive the resolve intact and silhouettes read as clean *and* glowing. Here the two most expensive effects in the chain actively cancel each other on exactly the pixels that matter most — high-contrast silhouettes, which is where both bloom and AA live.
findings.fix: Split the single EffectPass into three, in ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx around line 4011. Pass 1 = `new EffectPass(camera, bloomWide, bloomTight)` (BloomEffect is not a CONVOLUTION effect so two of them merge legally). Pass 2 = `new EffectPass(camera, radialBlurEffect, toneMappingEffect, lutEffect, hueSatEffect, vignetteEffect, noiseEffect)` — exactly one CONVOLUTION effect (the custom radial blur) is allowed per pass (index.js:15567 throws `Convolution effects cannot be merged`), and none of these may define `mainUv` (index.js:15391 throws). Pass 3 = `new EffectPass(camera, new SMAAEffect({ preset: SMAAPreset.HIGH, edgeDetectionMode: EdgeDetectionMode.LUMA }))` ALONE and LAST, so it resolves the tone-mapped, sRGB-encoded output. Cost: two extra fullscreen passes at 1360x765 ≈ 0.3ms on desktop, against the ~1.3ms frameWorkMs baseline noted in createRaceScene.js:10-13.

findings.title: No colour grading whatsoever — one un-authored ACES look is shared by two tracks whose histograms fail in opposite directions
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:4009 is a comment — `// LUT3DEffect goes here, before ToneMappingEffect, when owner supplies a LUT texture.` The grade has been blocked on an asset that will never arrive. Measured over the full frame excluding the HUD strip: comeback-city-p0_9 = 13.3% of pixels below lum 20, 4.9% above 200, mean saturation 0.556 — crushed, bimodal, no midtone structure in the road. penguin-village-p0_45 = 0.59% below 20, 47.8% ABOVE 200, mean saturation 0.337 — a milky mid-grey mush with no blacks, which is exactly how the ice reads in that frame and in p0_78: 200-240 luminance across half the screen with almost no tonal separation between snow bank, ice pyramid and horizon shelf.
findings.whyMk8Wins: Every MK8DX course has an authored per-course grade: Sunshine Airport pushes highlights amber and shadows teal, Mount Wario crushes to blue-black with a hot white snow point. That grade is what makes a course instantly recognisable from a single frame. Here 'neon dusk Miami' and 'arctic storm-front' receive byte-identical colour treatment, so the art direction is doing all the work alone and post is contributing nothing.
findings.fix: Zero-byte procedural LUT. New file src/game/race/render/raceGrade.js exporting `buildTrackLut(trackKey)`: start from `LookupTexture.createNeutral(32)` (postprocessing exports it), walk its RGBA8 data (32³ = 131 KB GPU, 0 bundle bytes) and apply, per texel in display space: (1) white-point pull `c = min(c / wp, 1)`, (2) lift-gamma-gain `c = pow(c, 1/gamma)*gain + lift`, (3) S-curve `c = mix(c, c*c*(3-2*c), contrast)`, (4) saturation `c = mix(vec3(luma(c)), c, sat)`, (5) split-tone `c += shadowTint*(1-luma) + highlightTint*luma`. Params — comeback-city: wp 0.90, gain (1.10,1.02,0.96), lift (0.010,0.004,0.030), contrast 0.22, sat 1.14, shadowTint #241a4a *0.06, highlightTint #ffb46a *0.05. penguin-village: wp 0.93, gain (0.99,1.01,1.06), lift (0.004,0.010,0.030), contrast 0.34 (the steep curve is what separates the ice), sat 1.10, shadowTint #0e2a52 *0.09, highlightTint #ffd9a0 *0.04 (keeps the gold storm-front rim). Mount it at line 4009 as `new LUT3DEffect(lut, { tetrahedralInterpolation: true, inputColorSpace: THREE.SRGBColorSpace })` placed AFTER ToneMappingEffect — pmndrs auto-wraps the effect in sRGBTransferOETF/sRGBToLinear when inputColorSpace is sRGB (index.js:15448), which is the correct display-referred domain for a creative LUT. Build it once per race in the createScene block, dispose on teardown.

findings.title: Sky gradients band hard — 7-15px constant-colour contour steps — because EffectPass dithering is off
findings.evidence: Vertical scan of comeback-city-p0_33.png at x=1450, y=150..400: 96 distinct colour bands across 250 rows, with individual runs of 7px, 10px, 12px and 15px (e.g. 12px at RGB 239,120,39 in the orange, 11px at 1,0,46 and 10px at 4,0,48 in the dark dome). The dark navy dome region bands worst, which is why the top-of-frame arc in every single capture (both tracks, all 9 progress marks) reads as a hard-edged black blob rather than a gradient. penguin-village-p0_45 at x=900 bands at up to 6px. Root cause: the composer is HalfFloatType (line 3985) but the final EffectPass writes 8-bit with no dither — `EffectPass.dithering` (index.js:15533, forwards to `fullscreenMaterial.dithering`, and EffectMaterial already `#include <dithering_pars_fragment>` / `<dithering_fragment>` at index.js:14623/14659) is never set.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8DX skies are large, smooth, low-frequency gradients — Sunset Wilds, Cloudtop Cruise — and they never contour, because the console pipeline dithers on the final 8-bit write. Banding is the single most 'browser demo' artefact in these captures and a player absolutely reads it as a rendering bug, not a style.
findings.fix: One line: set `dithering = true` on the LAST EffectPass in the chain (the SMAA pass after the restructure, or the single pass today), immediately after construction in ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx around line 4011. If three's ordered 4x4 dither proves too weak on the 10-15px dark-dome bands, add a 1-line blue-noise dither inside the grade pass instead: in the custom grade Effect's mainImage, `outputColor.rgb += (fract(sin(dot(uv*resolution + time, vec2(12.9898,78.233)))*43758.5453) - 0.5) / 255.0;` — amplitude exactly 1 LSB, applied post-tone-map, imperceptible as noise but sufficient to dissolve every band. Zero cost, zero bytes.

findings.title: The image has no white point — nothing in either scene reaches display white, so bloom at threshold 1.0 is nearly inert
findings.evidence: Scene-only maxima (HUD excluded): comeback-city-p0_9 = 233, comeback-city-p0_67 = 241 (that is the boost flame, the hottest thing in the game), penguin-village-p0_45 = 230, penguin-village-p0_78 = 231. Pixels above 240: 0.000% in all four. The arithmetic closes exactly: createRaceScene.js:104-112 gives hemi 3.15 + sun 3.55, so a white-albedo surface facing the key peaks at (3.15+3.55)/π ≈ 2.13 linear; ACES with toneMappingExposure 1.05 (ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3855) maps 2.24 to ≈0.79 linear ≈ 232 sRGB. Measured 230-233. Meanwhile luminanceThreshold is 1.0 (line 3997) with smoothing 0.22, so only the small fraction of the scene above 2.1x middle-lit contributes glow at all — the frame is bloom-starved by construction, not by tuning.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8DX deliberately clips: the sun disc, coin faces, boost flames and item-box facets punch to 255 and bleed. That clipped core is the anchor the whole highlight structure hangs from, and it is why MK8 reads as bright even in a dusk course. This game's brightest possible pixel is a dull off-white, which flattens every specular and every VFX pop.
findings.fix: Three coordinated changes, all zero-byte. (1) ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3855 — raise `renderer.toneMappingExposure` 1.05 -> 1.28 (it IS honoured: pmndrs ToneMappingEffect's ACES path is three's chunk, which multiplies by the toneMappingExposure uniform bound by WebGLRenderer for any toneMapped material). (2) Add the white-point pull described in the LUT finding (`c = min(c/0.90, 1.0)` for CC, `/0.93` for PV) so the top 10% of the ACES shoulder is remapped to actual white — this is the standard ACES-plus-creative-LUT workflow and is what recovers the punch ACES rolls off. (3) Drop `luminanceThreshold` 1.0 -> 0.72 with `luminanceSmoothing` 0.30 so the newly-lifted highlights actually feed the bloom. Verify by re-capturing and re-running the histogram: target is 0.15-0.6% of scene pixels above 250 in CC and 0.3-1.0% in PV, i.e. small, deliberate clipped cores — not a blown frame.

findings.title: The setting sun and the whole backdrop skyline can never bloom — MeshBasicMaterial caps at exactly 1.0, the bloom threshold
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3941-3950 builds both backdrop rings as `new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({ map: texture, fog: false, ... })` with `texture.colorSpace = SRGBColorSpace`. MeshBasic output = colour(1,1,1) x map, and an sRGB-decoded 8-bit texel maxes at exactly 1.0 linear — which is exactly `luminanceThreshold: 1.0` (line 3997), so the ring contributes literally zero bloom energy. Frame proof: comeback-city-p0_9.png, the large pale-yellow sun disc at roughly (760,300) is a hard-edged flat circle with no halo at all; comeback-city-p0_33.png, same disc at (490,330), same dead edge. penguin-village-p0_45/p0_78, the gold storm-front rim along the ice shelf is a razor-sharp 1px line with no bleed.
findings.whyMk8Wins: In MK8DX the sky's light source is always the brightest element and always blooms into the geometry silhouetted against it — that halo is what sells the sun as a light source rather than a painted disc. Here the single most bloom-worthy object in the composition is guaranteed by material choice to emit nothing.
findings.fix: In the addBackdropRing closure (ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx ~3941), set `material.color.setScalar(1.0)` for the near silhouette ring but `material.color.setRGB(1.45, 1.45, 1.45)` for the FAR ring only — MeshBasicMaterial multiplies map by colour with no clamp, so the pre-hazed far band (which contains the sun and the horizon glow) pushes past threshold while the near silhouette row stays neutral. Because the far ring art is already pre-hazed and dark everywhere except the sun/horizon glow, a flat 1.45x lifts only the intended pixels above 0.72 (the new threshold from the white-point finding). Pair with the two-bloom split: `bloomWide = new BloomEffect({ mipmapBlur: true, intensity: 0.62, radius: 0.88, luminanceThreshold: 0.72, luminanceSmoothing: 0.30 })` with `bloomWide.mipmapBlurPass.levels = 6` (default 8 makes the coarsest mip ~5x3px, i.e. a screen-wide milky lift rather than a defined glow), and `bloomTight = new BloomEffect({ mipmapBlur: true, intensity: 0.85, radius: 0.30, luminanceThreshold: 1.15, luminanceSmoothing: 0.12 })` with `levels = 3` for the hot cores on boost flames, coins and item boxes. Both merge into one EffectPass (neither is a CONVOLUTION effect).

findings.title: Zero speed or boost response in post — 289 km/h is graded identically to 88 km/h
findings.evidence: The entire speed cue is a 7-degree FOV widen plus 3.5 for mini-turbo (ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:6325-6330). Compare comeback-city-p0_06.png (manifest speed 88) with comeback-city-p0_78.png (speed 289) and comeback-city-p0_9.png (267, boosting, blue flame visible under the kart): the post treatment is pixel-for-pixel the same look — same contrast, same saturation, same edge sharpness, no radial streaking, no chroma split, no vignette pulse. The only speed signal is geometry: `g3-boost-speed-lines` (raceParticles.js:184-201), a camera-parented mesh whose quads render in comeback-city-p0_06/p0_67/p0_9 as large flat opaque grey rectangles floating over the sky at opacity 0.18-0.30 (raceParticles.js:374). They read as z-fighting UI debris, not motion.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8DX's mushroom/mini-turbo is a whole-screen event: FOV punch, a strong radial motion streak from the screen centre outward, a warm saturation and contrast lift, and speed lines composited INTO that streak so they never read as discrete quads. It is the single biggest 'game feel' contribution post makes in that title, and this game has none of it.
findings.fix: Add src/game/race/render/speedBlurEffect.js — a pmndrs `Effect` subclass, `attributes: EffectAttribute.CONVOLUTION`, uniforms `strength` (float) and `center` (vec2, 0.5,0.5). Shader: 8 taps along `dir = (uv - center)`, tap i at `uv - dir * strength * (i/7.0)`, and sample R/G/B at slightly different radii (`strength*1.00 / *1.06 / *1.12`) so the chroma split is baked into the same taps — that removes any need for a separate ChromaticAberrationEffect pass, which could not be merged anyway (ChromaticAberrationEffect is also CONVOLUTION, index.js:4594, and two convolutions in one pass throw at index.js:15567). Drive it from the frame loop next to the FOV code at line 6330: `speedBlur.strength = clamp((race.speed/MAX_SPEED - 0.55)/0.45, 0, 1) * 0.010 + (miniTurboActive ? 0.016 : 0)`, smoothed with the same `1 - pow(0.001, dt)` lerp the FOV uses so it ramps rather than pops. Put it FIRST in the grade pass (linear HDR, so it streaks the bloom too — that is exactly the MK8 boost look) and set `pass.enabled` off when strength < 0.0015 so the cost is zero at cruising speed. Also drop the g3 speed-line mesh opacity from 0.18-0.30 to 0.08-0.14 and let the radial blur carry the motion.

findings.title: SMAA MEDIUM disables diagonal and corner detection — in a scene built almost entirely from diagonals
findings.evidence: node_modules/postprocessing/build/index.js:11147-11151 — SMAAPreset.MEDIUM sets `edgeDetectionThreshold 0.1, orthogonalSearchSteps 8, diagonalDetection = false, cornerDetection = false`. HIGH keeps the same 0.1 threshold but sets 16 steps with diagonal AND corner detection ON. Almost every silhouette in these captures is a diagonal: the leaning tower spires in comeback-city-p0_33 and p0_9, the kerb strips converging to the vanishing point in every frame, the ice pyramids in penguin-village-p0_06/p0_45/p0_78, the pennant triangles at (1400-1540, 430-470) in penguin-village-p0_06, and the boost-line quads themselves. Compounding it, createRaceScene.js:14-17 renders desktop at 0.85 scale (1360x765 for a 1600x900 canvas) and lets the browser bilinear-upscale, so any edge SMAA misses is then softened-and-re-aliased on the way to the display.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8DX's edge quality is uniform across orientation — the diagonal glider rails and the checkered start banner are as clean as the vertical pillars. Here the vertical edges are handled and the 30-60 degree edges, which dominate the composition, get nothing.
findings.fix: Two changes. (1) ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:4007 -> `new SMAAEffect({ preset: SMAAPreset.HIGH, edgeDetectionMode: EdgeDetectionMode.LUMA })` — HIGH costs two extra search loops in the weights pass, roughly +0.1ms at 1360x765, and LUMA is the right detector once SMAA has been moved after tone mapping. (2) Set `composer.multisampling = 4` on the PmndrsEffectComposer at line 3985 (defaults to 0; the HalfFloat render target supports WebGL2 MSAA). That gives true geometric coverage AA that SMAA's morphological pass then only has to clean up, and it fixes the sub-pixel crawl on the thin pennant strings and lamp posts that no post-AA can recover. Gate `multisampling = 0` when `viewport.mobile` in the handleResize block at line 5130. While you are there: createRaceScene.js:4 sets `antialias: true` on the WebGLRenderer, which is dead weight under a composer — the only geometry ever drawn to the default framebuffer is the final fullscreen triangle. Set it false and put the samples where they do work.

findings.title: Vignette is applied to linear HDR before ACES, so it darkens the wrong domain and is not aspect-corrected
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:4008 pushes VignetteEffect BEFORE ToneMappingEffect at 4010. The shader (index.js:13663) is `color *= smoothstep(0.8, offset*0.799, d*(darkness+offset))` with `d = distance(uv, vec2(0.5))` — raw UV distance, no aspect correction. At 16:9 that makes the falloff an ellipse stretched with the frame: the mid-top and mid-bottom edges sit at d=0.5, the same as the mid-left and mid-right edges, so the vignette bites hardest on the top and bottom of the image and barely touches the sides. Measured bottom row of comeback-city-p0_33.png: luminance 15 / 21 / 28 at x=0/100/300 rising to 63 at x=1000 — a strong bottom-edge crush — while the horizontal mid-edges are essentially untouched. And because the multiply happens pre-ACES, the shoulder then partially re-lifts the darkened corners, so the effect is both mis-shaped and weaker than its 0.45 parameter implies.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8DX's frame edge treatment is subtle, circular and display-referred: it gates the corners without eating the bottom of the road, which is where the player is actually reading their kart's position. This vignette darkens exactly the road surface directly under the kart in every single capture.
findings.fix: Move VignetteEffect to AFTER ToneMappingEffect and after LUT3DEffect in the grade pass (order inside a merged EffectPass is array order, so this is a one-line move within the `effects` array at 4008-4010). Retune for display-referred: `new VignetteEffect({ technique: VignetteTechnique.ESKIL, offset: 0.62, darkness: 0.42 })`, or keep DEFAULT technique with `offset: 0.42, darkness: 0.30`. If the aspect stretch still reads wrong, replace it with three lines inside your custom grade Effect: `vec2 v = (uv - 0.5) * vec2(aspect, 1.0); outputColor.rgb *= mix(1.0, 1.0 - vignetteStrength, smoothstep(0.30, 0.78, length(v)));` — pmndrs already provides an `aspect` uniform to every Effect, so this is free and correctly circular.

findings.title: No aerial perspective — the far field is as sharp and as saturated as the kart, and the fog-exempt backdrop makes it worse
findings.evidence: comeback-city-p0_33.png: the tower silhouettes at the horizon are full-strength #2b1050 purple against #ec7324 orange, at higher local contrast than anything in the foreground, at pixel-sharp edges. comeback-city-p0_9.png: the skyline at y=250-420 competes directly with the kart for attention. Cause: the backdrop rings are built with `fog: false` (ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx ~3946, comment 'the art is pre-hazed'), and the world fog (RACE_FOG_NEAR 210 / RACE_FOG_FAR 580, createRaceScene.js:28-30) does not reach the near silhouette ring at radius 590. So the deepest 30% of the image receives no depth attenuation from any source.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8DX layers explicit aerial perspective — distant geometry desaturates and shifts toward the sky colour with distance, which is what separates the racing plane from the backdrop and keeps the eye on the kart. Note that MK8DX does NOT use depth of field during gameplay (only in replays and the character select), so do not add DepthOfFieldEffect here — it would cost 2-3ms and read as wrong for the genre.
findings.fix: Add a depth-driven haze as a merged, non-blurring effect — src/game/race/render/aerialEffect.js, a pmndrs `Effect` with `attributes: EffectAttribute.DEPTH` (the composer already allocates and wires a depth texture because SMAAEffect declares DEPTH at index.js:10970, so this is free). Shader: `float d = viewZToOrthographicDepth(perspectiveDepthToViewZ(depth, cameraNear, cameraFar), cameraNear, cameraFar); float h = smoothstep(hazeNear, hazeFar, d); outputColor.rgb = mix(inputColor.rgb, mix(inputColor.rgb, vec3(luminance(inputColor.rgb)), desat) * hazeTint, h * hazeStrength);` Params — comeback-city: hazeNear 0.55, hazeFar 1.0, desat 0.35, hazeTint = the track's horizon glow #ff8a3d normalised, hazeStrength 0.42. penguin-village: hazeNear 0.45, hazeFar 1.0, desat 0.20, hazeTint #cfe4f2, hazeStrength 0.55 (the storm front should swallow depth harder). Slot it into the grade pass BEFORE ToneMappingEffect (haze is a linear-domain scattering approximation). One depth fetch, no taps — sub-0.05ms.

findings.title: No film grain — the image is chemically clean, which is what makes the flat regions read as vector art rather than rendered
findings.evidence: There is no NoiseEffect anywhere in the chain (ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3992-4011). The consequence is visible in the large flat regions: the mid-grey-green ground plane in comeback-city-p0_06 (x=0-600, y=420-470) is a perfectly uniform field, and the sky above the skyline in comeback-city-p0_33 is uniform to within 1 LSB across hundreds of pixels — measured 96 discrete bands over a 250px scan, i.e. the surface between bands is dead flat.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8DX is not grainy, but it is never chemically flat either — texture detail, dithered gradients and specular micro-variation keep every surface alive. Perfectly uniform regions are a giveaway of an un-finished post chain and they also make the banding in the adjacent gradient far more conspicuous by contrast.
findings.fix: Append `new NoiseEffect({ blendFunction: BlendFunction.OVERLAY, premultiply: true })` as the LAST effect in the grade pass (after vignette, before the SMAA pass), then set `noiseEffect.blendMode.opacity.value = 0.035` — barely perceptible, but enough to dissolve the flats and reinforce the dither fix. Gate to 0.02 on mobile (grain amplifies at low render scale after upscale). If NoiseEffect's OVERLAY blend proves too contrast-shifting on PV's bright snow, use `BlendFunction.SOFT_LIGHT` at 0.05 instead. Zero bytes, one texture-free hash per pixel.

findings.title: No sharpening after the 0.85 desktop render scale — the composer's crisp output is thrown away by the browser's bilinear upscale
findings.evidence: createRaceScene.js:14-17 sets `RACE_RENDER_SCALE.desktop = 0.85`, and fitRaceRendererToCanvas (createRaceScene.js:74-80) sizes the drawing buffer to `rect * dpr * 0.85` while calling `renderer.setSize(rect.width, rect.height, false)` so CSS keeps the full canvas size. On a 1x display at 1600x900 CSS that is a 1360x765 buffer bilinear-scaled up 1.18x by the compositor. Every high-frequency detail — the kerb stripe edges in comeback-city-p0_9, the HUD-adjacent thin lamp posts in penguin-village-p0_78, the pennant strings at (1400-1540,430-470) in penguin-village-p0_06 — is softened by that resample, and nothing in the chain compensates.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8DX renders 1080p native on Switch docked with no upscale, so its edges arrive at the panel at full acuity. If you are going to pay a 15% linear resolution tax for framerate, you must buy the perceived acuity back in post — every console title that upscales does exactly this.
findings.fix: Add a 3x3 unsharp-mask as the last stage inside the grade pass Effect (or a tiny standalone `attributes: EffectAttribute.CONVOLUTION` effect in the SMAA pass is NOT possible — two convolutions throw, so put it in the grade pass alongside the radial blur only if you fold both into one shader, otherwise make it part of the radial-blur effect's shader). Kernel: sample the 4 cross neighbours at +/- texelSize, `vec3 blur = (n+s+e+w) * 0.25; outputColor.rgb = clamp(color + (color - blur) * sharpAmount, 0.0, 1.0);` with sharpAmount 0.30 on desktop, 0.0 on mobile (mobile renders at 0.6 and sharpening would amplify its aliasing). Apply post-tone-map so it operates on display-referred values and cannot ring on HDR highlights.

findings.title: No mobile quality tier for the post chain — phones get the identical desktop chain at 0.6 render scale
findings.evidence: `postChainEnabled` (ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:5012-5020) is a single boolean driven only by `?post=0`. There is no branch on `viewport.mobile` or on the `touchControls` coarse-pointer check at line 4872 anywhere in the composer block at 3965-4011. Mobile therefore runs the same 8-level mipmap bloom, the same SMAA, the same vignette and tone map on a 0.6-scale buffer — and once the proposed chain lands (two blooms, radial blur, LUT, haze, grain, SMAA HIGH, 4x MSAA) that becomes a guaranteed frame-budget failure on the phones this must stay playable on.
findings.whyMk8Wins: Not an MK8 comparison so much as a shipping requirement — but MK8DX itself scales its post between docked and handheld (bloom resolution and AA both drop). Without an explicit tier the graphics ceiling raise will either be capped by the weakest phone or will break the phone build.
findings.fix: Introduce `const postTier = viewport.mobile || touchControls ? 'mobile' : 'desktop'` resolved before the composer block and thread it into createScene. MOBILE chain (2 passes): Pass 1 = `EffectPass(camera, bloomWide)` with `mipmapBlurPass.levels = 4`, intensity 0.55, threshold 0.78 — drop bloomTight entirely. Pass 2 = `EffectPass(camera, toneMapping, lut3D, vignette)` with `dithering = true` — drop the radial blur (or ship a 4-tap variant with no chroma split), drop the aerial haze, drop grain, drop sharpening, drop MSAA (`composer.multisampling = 0`). Drop SMAA entirely on mobile: at 0.6 render scale the browser's upscale already blurs the edges SMAA would resolve, and the pass is pure cost — if AA is judged necessary, use `new FXAAEffect()` in its own pass instead, which is roughly a third the cost. The LUT and vignette are the two effects that must survive to mobile: they carry the entire art direction for ~1 extra texture fetch. Wire the tier into the existing `handleResize` composer branch at line 5130 so an orientation change cannot leave a desktop chain running on a phone.

pillar: Track surface, edges, curbs and road markings
verdictVsMk8: Blind side-by-side, this reads as a greybox with paint on it, not a racetrack. MK8's road is a solid object — the tarmac has thickness and a crowned surface, the curb is a chamfered extruded strip welded to the asphalt edge that you can hear and feel, and the verge grades down into sculpted terrain. Here the road is a zero-thickness 112-sample ribbon floating 0.11 units over an infinite flat plane, and the "edge" is three disconnected unlit flat ribbons (curb at 0.50–0.56w, wall at 0.62w) separated by two ~3.4-unit strips of raw grass/snow — visible as literal stripe/grass/stripe/grass banding on the left of comeback-city-p0_33. Add one yellow centre dash every 103 world units and no edge lines at all, and the racing line simply does not read at 280 km/h; the strongest longitudinal cue in comeback-city-p0_33 is a pair of accidental AI skid marks. The one thing better than MK8 is the colour language (neon dusk on dark asphalt is a correct, Sherbet-Land-style readability call) — everything structural is 2–3 generations behind.

findings.title: Edge kit is three disconnected flat ribbons with two 3.4-unit strips of raw terrain between them
findings.evidence: comeback-city-p0_33.png, left and right of the kart: asphalt → dark-green grass gap → white ribbon → red ribbon → grass gap → lavender/cyan band. Same read in penguin-village-p0_78.png (navy road → thin snow gap → cyan strip → white → snow). Code: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:1815-1875. With trackVisuals OFF (the shipped default, see line 4999-5005), the shoulder ribbon is skipped entirely (guarded at :1816), the curb runs innerMul 0.5 → outerMul 0.56 (:1834-1835) while the asphalt edge is at 0.44w (:390), and the wall sits at 0.62w (:1847-1848). On the 56-wide south carousel that is exactly three 3.4-unit bands with two 3.4-unit gaps of bare ground showing between them.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 has ONE continuous silhouette from tarmac to terrain: asphalt → chamfer → curb crest → chamfer → graded verge → barrier, all welded, all catching light. The player's eye locks onto a single unbroken edge line and can place the kart within half a wheel of it. Here there are five competing edges of equal visual weight and none of them is the real boundary, so the drivable width is a guess.
findings.fix:
Replace the four separate buildCheckerRibbon calls (ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:1815-1875) with ONE extruded edge profile per side — 2 meshes total, down from 6. Walk the curve at ceil(sampler.length/5) samples (CC 2889/5 ≈ 578) and emit a 7-point cross-section per sample, in world units measured outward from u = 0.44*widthAt(p):
  p0 (u+0.00, y_road+0.02)  inner chamfer foot, welded to the asphalt edge — zero gap
  p1 (u+0.45, y_road+0.30)  crest inner
  p2 (u+4.00, y_road+0.30)  crest outer  ← the checkered rumble face
  p3 (u+4.60, y_road+0.10)  outer chamfer
  p4 (u+9.00, y_ground)     graded verge, lerped down to the ground plane
  p5 (u+9.00, y_ground+3.0) barrier face
  p6 (u+9.80, y_ground+3.0) barrier top cap (real thickness, not a plane)
Index it as 6 quad strips, computeVertexNormals, side: THREE.FrontSide (drop DoubleSide — it is what makes the current ribbons read as paint from underneath). Use MeshStandardMaterial{flatShading:true, roughness:0.55, vertexColors:true} for the whole profile so the chamfers actually shade; only the barrier top cap keeps an unlit emissive rail colour.

findings.title: Curbs are unlit zero-thickness paint with 25.8-unit colour blocks — not rumble strips
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:1694-1754 buildCheckerRibbon: geometry is a 2-vertex-wide strip, yBottom 0.32 / yTop 0.18 (:1838-1839) so the 'curb' is a flat plate tilted 0.14 over its 3.4-unit width with no vertical face, rendered `unlit: true` → MeshBasicMaterial (:1743), side DoubleSide. checkerEvery defaults to 1 (:1695) and TRACK_SAMPLES = 112 (:172) against a 2889-unit CC lap = one colour block every 25.8 world units — roughly three kart lengths per block. Visible in comeback-city-p0_33.png as a single long white ribbon followed by a single long red ribbon, and in comeback-city-p0_9.png where one red run spans the entire corner exit.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8's rumble strip alternates roughly every 3/4 of a kart width, and each block is a real extruded prism with a lit top face and a shaded chamfer. The high-frequency alternation is a speed cue — the faster you go the more it strobes — and the geometry means the curb self-shades so its height is unambiguous. A 25.8-unit unlit flat block reads as a painted line and gives zero speed feedback.
findings.fix: In the new edge builder, accumulate arc length `s` while walking the curve and colour the crest quads (p1→p2 strip only) by `Math.floor(s / 6.5) % 2 ? colorB : colorA` — 6.5 world units ≈ 0.75 kart widths (wheel track is ±4.6, raceParticles.js:273). Every other strip in the profile (chamfers, verge, barrier) gets a solid colour, so only the crest checkers. Drop `unlit` for the curb entirely: MeshStandardMaterial flatShading gives you the top face bright and the chamfers ~35% darker for free under the existing hemi + sun, which is what sells the 3D read.

findings.title: The whole edge kit is unreachable decoration — the kart is hard-clamped inside an invisible tube 5% short of the asphalt edge
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:5632 `race.lane = clamp(race.lane + (laneRate + cornerPush) * dt, -0.95, 0.95)`, repeated at :5836 and :5839; `wallLane: 0.95` is passed to the rival sim at :5832. Lane ±1 maps to 0.44*width (:390), so the player is walled at 0.418w while the asphalt edge is 0.44w and the curb starts at 0.50w. There is no offroad term anywhere in the shipped monolith (grep 'offroad' in ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx returns nothing; kartPhysics.js:313-321 has one but only the dead ArcadeRace3D path calls it). Consistent with every frame: no kart in any of the 9 baseline captures is ever near a curb.
findings.whyMk8Wins: In MK8 the curb is a gameplay surface — you ride it on the apex, the kart lifts ~8cm, the controller rumbles, the tyre note changes, and one wheel further out is grass that costs you 30% top speed. That is the entire reason curbs are drawn at all. Here the curb is a texture the player physically cannot reach, so no amount of geometry work on it will matter until the boundary moves.
findings.fix: Three coupled changes. (1) Move the clamp at ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:5632/:5836/:5839 and `wallLane` at :5832 from 0.95 to 1.14 — 1.0 puts the outer wheel on the asphalt edge, 1.14 puts it on the curb crest (0.44w + 4.0 with w≈50). (2) Add a rumble band: when `Math.abs(race.lane) > 1.0`, raise the kart visual y by `0.30 * smoothstep(1.0, 1.06, |lane|)`, add a 9 Hz ±0.035 rad camera roll in chaseCamera.js, fire the existing skid/spray emitter from raceParticles.js with the curb colour, and multiply grip by 0.88. (3) Beyond 1.14 apply a real offroad term — reuse SURFACE_TYPES from surfacePhysics.js by adding `offroad: {accelerationMultiplier: 0.55, gripMultiplier: 0.62, steerMultiplier: 0.85}` and feed it at the same place surfaceTypeAt is consumed, so the verge you just built (p3→p4 in the profile) is what the player actually skids across.

findings.title: One centre dash every 103 units and zero edge lines — the racing line does not read at speed
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:1877-1890: the only paint on the drivable surface is a `BoxGeometry(1.15, 0.08, 11.5)` yellow dash placed every `everySamples: 4` (trackVisualSchema.js:33) = every 4/112 of a 2889-unit lap = one 11.5-unit dash per 103 units, 28 total for the whole circuit. comeback-city-p0_33.png and penguin-village-p0_45.png each show exactly ONE yellow dash in frame; the most legible longitudinal cues on the road in p0_33 are two dark AI skid marks (raceParticles.js:268-303), which are accidental. There are no edge lines, no lane separators, no apex paint, no braking boards.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 paints a solid white edge line inboard of every curb, dashed lane separators at a cadence that strobes at racing speed, and darker worn tarmac on the ideal line. Together they give continuous sub-metre lateral reference and a strong sense of velocity. With one dash per 103 units this road gives a velocity cue about once every 0.4 seconds and no lateral reference at all.
findings.fix: Delete the per-dash `world.add` loop at :1880-1889 (28 draw calls) and build ONE merged BufferGeometry mesh for all road paint, walking the curve by arc length: (a) centre dash — 9.0 long / 12.0 gap, 1.2 wide, colour laneMarkings.color, y = surface + 0.06; (b) solid edge line — 1.2 wide, continuous, at lane ±0.905 (i.e. 0.40w, comfortably inboard of the 0.44w asphalt edge), colour '#f2f6ff' for CC and '#8fd8ff' for PV so it survives the snow; (c) inside-apex paint — a 3-unit-wide band at lane ∓0.72 through the two carousels (progress 0.20–0.40 and 0.78–1.0), 12% darker than the asphalt base, which is the cheapest possible 'worn racing line'. Emit them into one geometry with vertex colours and one MeshBasicMaterial{vertexColors:true, depthWrite:false, renderOrder:1}. Net draw calls: 28 → 1, freeing 27 for the geometry work in the other findings.

findings.title: Penguin Village curb and barrier are white-on-white — half the edge is literally invisible
findings.evidence: penguinVillage.js:122 `curb: { a: '#F5F8FF', b: '#00E5FF' }` and :124 `wall: { a: '#7EC8E8', b: '#F5F8FF' }` against ground base :114 `'#eaf4fa'`. #F5F8FF vs #eaf4fa is under 4 ΔE — indistinguishable once bloom (intensity 0.55, threshold 1.0, ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3990-4002) lifts the snow. Confirmed in penguin-village-p0_78.png: on both sides the cyan half of the curb is the ONLY thing marking the boundary and the white half merges completely into the snow plain; the barrier wall is not distinguishable from terrain anywhere in the frame. penguin-village-p0_45.png is worse — the right-hand road edge dissolves into an undifferentiated white field.
findings.whyMk8Wins: Sherbet Land and Mount Wario solve exactly this: on snow they never use white as a curb colour. The curb goes red/blue or orange/navy and the snow verge gets a blue-shadowed cut edge, so value contrast against the terrain is maintained even in whiteout lighting. Here the arctic palette was applied to the curb without checking it against the ground it sits on.
findings.fix: penguinVillage.js:122 → `curb: { a: '#123a52', b: '#00E5FF' }` (deep ice-navy alternating with the existing aurora cyan — keeps the arctic language, gives ~55 ΔE against the #eaf4fa snow). :124 → `wall: { a: '#1c4a63', b: '#00E5FF' }`. Then, in the new edge profile, darken the graded verge strip (p3→p4) by multiplying the ground colour by 0.86 and add a 0.25-unit lip at p4 so the snow cut edge casts a real contact shadow — that single value break is what separates road from plain in MK8's snow tracks.

findings.title: Road surface is a 112-sample, 2-vertex-wide zero-thickness ribbon floating over an infinite flat plane
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:1627-1671 — TRACK_SAMPLES = 112 (:172) against a 2889-unit CC lap and a 2442-unit PV lap = 25.8 / 21.8-unit chords; two vertices per sample (:1636) so the road has no crown, no thickness and no bevel; `side: THREE.DoubleSide` (:1666) confirms it is a sheet. Ground is a single flat PlaneGeometry(1120, 1060) at y = -0.06 (:1683-1688) while the road sits at y = +0.05 (:1634-1635) — an 0.11 step with nothing filling it. Corner faceting is visible on the left-hand road edge of penguin-village-p0_33.png (min radius 72 with a 21.8-unit chord gives 1.17 units of corner-cut per segment) and on the carousel edge in comeback-city-p0_33.png.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8's road is a solid volume: a crowned surface (~1.5% camber so water/light read as a curved plane), a visible tarmac thickness at the edge, and terrain that is sculpted up to meet it. It never facets because the mesh is generated at metre scale. Here the road silhouette against the terrain visibly polygonises through every corner and the 0.11 float means the road edge has no contact darkening at all — the single biggest reason it reads as a decal rather than a surface.
findings.fix: In addTrack (:1630), replace the fixed TRACK_SAMPLES loop with an arc-length loop: `const roadSamples = Math.ceil(sampler.length / 6)` (CC 482, PV 407) — cost is 964 verts and one draw call, unchanged. Emit 5 vertices per sample instead of 2, at lane [-1, -0.55, 0, 0.55, 1] with y offsets [0, +0.10, +0.14, +0.10, 0] to give a 0.14-unit crown, and index it as 4 quad strips. Keep the existing UVs on the outer verts and lerp U across. Then set `side: THREE.FrontSide` and let the new edge profile's inner chamfer (p0, welded at y_road+0.02) close the gap to the ground — that removes the 0.11 float entirely. Keep the curb/edge builder on its own ceil(length/5) sampling so the two meshes share the same chord density and never disagree at a corner.

findings.title: Penguin Village's ice and snow surface bands are physically live but visually invisible
findings.evidence: penguinVillage.js:74-79 declares `{progressStart: 0.24, progressEnd: 0.42, laneStart: -0.75, laneEnd: 0.75, type: 'ice'}` with snow shoulders either side; surfacePhysics.js:17-23 gives ice gripMultiplier 0.35 and steerMultiplier 0.7 — a 65% grip loss. The road mesh (ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:1648-1671) uses ONE asphalt noise texture for the entire lap and nothing anywhere samples surfaceBands for rendering. penguin-village-p0_33.png sits at progress 0.33, dead centre of the ice band, and the road is the identical dark navy asphalt as p0_78 (progress 0.78, pure asphalt).
findings.whyMk8Wins: Every MK8 surface change is telegraphed a full corner ahead: ice is a distinct specular blue-white with visible cracks, sand is a different value and grain, and the boundary between surfaces is drawn as a hard material seam. The player brakes for the surface, not for the spin-out. Here the player loses 65% grip with zero warning, which reads as a physics bug rather than a track feature.
findings.fix: Give the road mesh a second vertex-colour attribute driven by surfaceTypeAt(). In the new 5-vertex-per-sample road loop, call `surfaceTypeAt({progress, lane}, trackDef.surfaceBands)` per vertex and write a tint: asphalt = white (1,1,1), snow = (1.28, 1.32, 1.36), ice = (0.72, 0.92, 1.18). Add `vertexColors: true` to the road MeshStandardMaterial (:1661) — the map multiplies by the vertex colour, so this is one attribute and zero extra draw calls. For the ice band also lerp `roughness` down: split the ice band into its own sub-mesh sharing the same geometry buffer with a second material group (roughness 0.16, metalness 0.28) so it takes a real specular highlight from the sun and reads as ice, not painted blue. Draw the band boundary crisply by forcing a duplicated vertex row at progress 0.24 and 0.42 so the transition is a seam, not a 20-unit gradient.

findings.title: Zero banking on any corner of either track, including two 'carousels' authored as high-speed drift sweepers
findings.evidence: Banking exists only behind the trackVisuals flag: bankYOffsetAt returns 0 unless visualRoadEnabled (ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:1605-1610), and that flag defaults false (:4999-5005). Even with it on, no band anywhere sets bankingDegrees — comebackCity.js:9-17 builds COMEBACK_CITY_VISUAL_BANDS without the key, so normalizeRoadBand (trackVisualSchema.js:90) defaults it to 0. Result in comeback-city-p0_33.png and p0_9.png: the south and seam carousels are perfectly flat plates, and the horizon line stays dead level through the entire corner.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 banks nearly every sustained corner 5–12°. Banking does three things at once: it rolls the horizon so the corner is legible from the camera before you reach it, it makes the outside curb visible from the inside line, and it justifies the higher cornering speed. A flat carousel at 280 km/h looks like a parking lot.
findings.fix: Move banking out from behind the flag: in ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:1605-1610 drop the `if (!visualRoadEnabled) return 0` guard and read bankingDegrees from a plain table on the track def instead of the visual schema. Then author it — comebackCity.js roadRibbons: south-carousel (0.2–0.4) 9°, east-loop (0.53–0.66) 6°, seam-carousel (0.78–1.0) 8°, everything else 0; penguinVillage.js: pond-sweep (0.24–0.42) 7°, return-bend (0.72–1.0) 5°. Sign the bank toward the inside of the turn using the sign of trackCurvatureAt(). Critically, smooth the entry/exit: run the banking value through the same 14-pass box filter used for makeWidthTable (:355-364) so the roll ramps over ~35 units instead of stepping at a ribbon boundary. The edge profile and lane paint already derive their y from surfacePointAt, so they follow the bank for free.

findings.title: No start/finish apron and no starting grid — the line is a 4.4-unit smear of non-square tiles costing 20 draw calls
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:2657-2669: 2 rows × 10 columns of `BoxGeometry(gateWidth * 0.1, 0.06, 2.2)` = 4.7 units across × 2.2 units along, total apron depth 4.4 units, each tile added individually to the group (20 separate meshes). On CC the player crosses it in 0.017 s at the observed 263 units/s. There is no lap-line colour, no grid boxes, no pit-style run-off marking, and the tiles are not square so the checker pattern is visibly stretched.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8's start/finish is a landmark: a deep checkered apron (8–12 rows of square tiles) with painted numbered grid boxes, a coloured lap line, and directional arrows leading into it. You know the lap is ending three seconds before the arch is in frame. Here the only start/finish signal is the overhead gantry — the ground says nothing.
findings.fix: Replace the 20-mesh loop at :2657-2669 with one merged BufferGeometry emitted into the same road-paint mesh from the lane-marking fix. Spec: square tiles sized `gateWidth / 12` (≈3.9 units), 8 rows deep (≈31 units of apron), staggered checker, at surface + 0.05 with depthWrite false. Add in front of it (upstream by 6 units) a solid 1.6-unit lap line in the track accent (CC '#ffd34f', PV '#00E5FF'), and behind it 8 painted grid boxes — 9 × 5-unit rectangles at lanes ±0.45 in two staggered columns spaced 14 units apart, drawn as 1.0-unit-wide outlines in '#f2f6ff'. Net draw calls: 20 → 0 (folded into the existing paint mesh), freeing 19 more.

findings.title: Every other section of the lap is visible as competing stripes on the same flat plane in the same colours
findings.evidence: comeback-city-p0_33.png: three additional runs of the circuit are visible across the flat green plain (far left, mid-left, and along the horizon) rendered in the SAME white/red/cyan edge kit at the SAME height as the section being driven, so the frame contains four sets of identical stripes and the eye cannot tell which one is the road. Same failure in comeback-city-p0_06.png (a broad lavender band cutting diagonally across the terrain at mid-left) and comeback-city-p0_45.png. Root cause: elevation is 0 everywhere except the 0.4–0.534 bridge band (comebackCity.js:31), and the ground is one unbroken flat plane (ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:1683-1690), so nothing occludes or separates the sections.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 never lets two sections of a lap sit co-planar in frame without something between them — a hedge line, a rock wall, a water channel, a grandstand, or a 3-metre elevation break. When you can see a later section it is deliberately framed as a landmark, not as visual noise competing with the road you are on.
findings.fix: Two zero-asset moves. (1) Give the ground plane relief: replace the flat PlaneGeometry(1120,1060,18,18) at :1684 with a 96×96 grid and displace y by `-2.5 * smoothstep(34, 110, minCenterlineDistance(sampler, x, z))` — the terrain drops 2.5 units away from the road corridor, so from the driver's seat the near verge occludes the far sections' curbs entirely. minCenterlineDistance already exists at :2683. Cost: ~18k tris, still one draw call. (2) Desaturate distance: the new edge-profile material should fold in a distance term — multiply vertex colour by `mix(1.0, 0.55, smoothstep(180, 420, distanceToCamera))` baked as a static per-vertex value at build time using the track's own bounding box is not possible (camera moves), so instead lean on fog: CC currently sets no fog override, so give comebackCity.js a `fog: { color: '#2a1c3e', near: 190, far: 560 }` to match PV's treatment (penguinVillage.js:133). That alone pushes the competing stripe sets to ~40% contrast.

findings.title: Asphalt is untextured flat noise — no edge darkening, no worn line, no directional grain
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:1648-1668 — the road material is MeshStandardMaterial with a 256×256 canvas noise map at `repeat: 1` (makeNoiseTexture at :831-861), metalness 0.06, roughness 0.6, no normal map, no AO, no second detail layer. The UVs are `(0, index*0.4)` / `(1, index*0.4)` (:1637), so U spans the full road width once — as widthAt varies 45→64 across the lap the aggregate grain stretches by 42% between the harbor dive and the pond sweep. Visible as uniform confetti speckle across the whole surface in comeback-city-p0_67.png and penguin-village-p0_78.png.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8's tarmac carries three layers: a fine aggregate normal, a low-frequency patch/variation pass, and baked darkening at the edges plus a subtly polished band on the ideal line. That gives the surface both close-range material identity and long-range shape reading. A single uniform speckle layer at one frequency reads as flat colour past ~40 units and gives the eye nothing to track.
findings.fix: Three cheap additions, all procedural. (1) Fix the U stretch: change :1637 to `uvs.push(0, s / 24, 1, s / 24)` where s is accumulated arc length, and add a second UV set uv2 = (u * widthAt(p) / 24, s / 24) so grain size is world-constant regardless of road width. (2) Bake edge darkening into the road's vertex colours from finding 6's 5-vertex cross-section: multiply the two outer verts (lane ±1) by 0.78 and the ±0.55 verts by 0.93 — a 4-unit contact gradient into the curb, which is the single highest-value-per-byte change here. (3) Add a normal map from the SAME canvas: in makeNoiseTexture, run a Sobel over the speckle luminance into a second 256×256 canvas and return it as `normalMap` with `normalScale: new THREE.Vector2(0.35, 0.35)`. Zero new bundle bytes, no extra draw call, and it makes the sun and the neon rim actually catch the aggregate.

findings.title: Depth precision: near plane 0.25 with far 860–1800 z-fights the road against the ground past ~700 units
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3870 `new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(66, 1, 0.25, 860)` and :3934 `camera.far = 1800` in the wide-backdrop mode. The road top sits 0.11 above the ground plane (road y = elev + 0.05 at :1634, ground y = -0.06 at :1688). With near 0.25 and a 24-bit depth buffer, depth resolution is ≈ z² / (near · 2^24) ≈ 0.153 units at z = 800 — larger than the 0.11 separation, so the far road/ground boundary flickers. Compounded by the curb ribbons floating 0.24–0.38 above the ground with no side faces, which is what makes the horizon-line stripes in comeback-city-p0_06.png look like they scatter.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 never shows surface flicker at distance because road and terrain are one welded mesh, not two co-planar sheets. Even one frame of z-fighting on the road at the horizon reads as an engine bug.
findings.fix: Two lines. (1) ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3870 → raise near from 0.25 to 1.0. The chase camera never gets closer than ~6 units to any geometry (chaseCamera.js clamps the boom), so nothing clips, and 4× near gives 4× depth precision at every distance — 0.038 units at z = 800, comfortably under the 0.11 gap. (2) Once finding 6 welds the road's inner chamfer to the ground there is no co-planar pair left at all; until then, add `polygonOffset: true, polygonOffsetFactor: -2, polygonOffsetUnits: -2` to the road material at :1661 so it always wins against the ground plane.

verdictVsMk8: Blind side-by-side this loses badly, and it loses on the first glance rather than on detail.
