MK8's HUD is a set of *shapes* you read peripherally — a big framed item slot, a huge ordinal, a lap counter, a coin tally, a minimap — each with its own size, color and corner, so at 200km/h you never look directly at it. Here (every baseline frame) there is exactly one shape: a horizontal strip of eight identical 34px dark rectangles with 12px monospace numerals, at the same weight, in the same color, glued to the top-left over the brightest part of the sky. Position "1ST", the item you're holding, your coin count, and two pure developer counters (boost pads hit, items picked up) are all rendered with equal emphasis, so nothing is readable at a glance and the most important element in a kart racer — the item slot — is literally the smallest thing on screen (`penguin-village-p0_67.png`, the 15px "ON" chip). There is no minimap, no race clock, no lap flash, no position-change animation, no "GO!", and the finish is a 440px pill. The rendering behind it is genuinely close to MK8-adjacent; the HUD is what makes the screenshot read as a prototype.

findings.title: Item slot is the smallest, last, most ignorable element on screen
findings.evidence: penguin-village-p0_67.png / -p0_9.png: the held item is a ~15px icon + "ON" / "ICE SHIELD" text inside the final 34px chip of the strip. src/game/ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:6581-6598 renders it as just another `.three-kart-race__badge`; HeldItemIcon defaults to `size = 15` (line 4777). CSS `.three-kart-race__badge` (comebackCityThreeKartRace.css:56-67) gives it min-height 34px, and on phones the label is `display:none` (line 345-347), leaving a 15px thumbnail. The empty state renders a *grayscaled snowball* (line 6586-6589), which reads as "you are holding a snowball", not "empty".
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8's item slot is a dedicated ~110px framed roulette panel in the top-left, visually separated from every other readout, with an idle empty frame that is unmistakably empty, a spinning roulette while rolling, and a settle pop. It is the one thing a kart player checks constantly, so it is sized like the primary HUD object. Here it is a footnote at the end of a row of numbers.
findings.fix: Promote the item slot out of the chip strip into its own fixed element. New JSX block in ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx (sibling of `.three-kart-race__hud`, before it): `<div className="tkr-item-slot" data-armed={...} data-empty={...}>`, containing `<HeldItemIcon size={72} />` (desktop) / 56 (`@media (max-width:760px)`). CSS: 96x96 desktop (72x72 mobile), `border-radius:18px`, `border:3px solid rgba(255,211,79,.85)`, `background:linear-gradient(160deg,rgba(13,20,30,.86),rgba(13,20,30,.62))`, `box-shadow:0 10px 26px rgba(0,0,0,.45), inset 0 0 22px rgba(255,211,79,.10)`, positioned `top:calc(16px + env(safe-area-inset-top,0px)); left:calc(16px + env(safe-area-inset-left,0px))`. EMPTY state = no icon at all, only a dashed inner frame at 30% opacity (`border:2px dashed rgba(248,251,255,.28)`) — delete the grayscale-snowball placeholder at line 6586-6589. ARMED state adds a 1.6s `@keyframes tkr-slot-breathe` pulsing the box-shadow spread 18px→30px so the eye is drawn to it. Reuse the existing 0.66s `three-kart-item-pop` as a slot-entry transform (scale 1.35→1) instead of a separate mid-screen popup once the slot is large enough to read.

findings.title: Countdown shows "3" for 200ms, is a static grey box, and there is no GO!
findings.evidence: src/game/ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:284 `countdown: 2.2`, decremented at line 5443, rendered at 6600-6602 as `Math.ceil(snapshot.countdown)` inside `.three-kart-race__countdown`. With ceil() on 2.2s, "3" is on screen for 0.2s, "2" for 1.0s, "1" for 1.0s — a visibly broken cadence. Worse, snapshot only refreshes every 0.14s (line 6364), so the first digit can be missed entirely. CSS lines 88-103: a 124px square with a 1px border and zero animation. Nothing renders at countdown === 0.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8's start is a full presentation beat: lights, three evenly-timed digits each with a punch-in scale and a matched audio cue, then a large "GO!" that scales out over ~0.5s while the camera releases. It teaches the rocket-start timing window. Here the player gets an uneven 3-2-1 in a grey square and then simply... starts.
findings.fix:
(1) Set `countdown: 3.0` at line 284 so each digit gets a full second. (2) Track a `goFlash` state: when `race.countdown` crosses 0 in updateFrame, set `race.goFlashTimer = 0.7` and decrement it; publish it in the 6365 snapshot. (3) In JSX render `{snapshot.countdown > 0 ?
{Math.ceil(snapshot.countdown)}
: snapshot.goFlash > 0 ?
GO!
: null}` — the `key` forces React to remount per digit so the animation replays. (4) CSS: drop the box entirely; render numerals at `font:900 clamp(96px,14vw,168px)/1` with `color:#ffd34f`, `-webkit-text-stroke:4px rgba(8,12,20,.9)`, `text-shadow:0 8px 30px rgba(0,0,0,.6), 0 0 44px rgba(255,211,79,.45)`. `@keyframes tkr-count-in { 0%{opacity:0;transform:translate(-50%,-50%) scale(2.2)} 22%{opacity:1;transform:translate(-50%,-50%) scale(.92)} 40%{transform:translate(-50%,-50%) scale(1)} 100%{opacity:.85;transform:translate(-50%,-50%) scale(1)} }` at 1s linear. GO! variant: `color:#5cff9d`, 0.7s `scale(.6)→scale(1.15)` with opacity fading to 0 in the last 30%, plus a 120ms full-screen white `mix-blend-screen` wash at 0.18 opacity.

findings.title: Zero visual hierarchy: eight identical pills in one row is the whole HUD
findings.evidence: Every baseline frame. `comeback-city-p0_78.png` reads left-to-right: `🏆1ST | ⌾283 | ⚑1/3 | ⚡3 | ✨4 | ₿4 | 🔊 | ▪–`. Source: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:6542-6598 — one flex row of `.three-kart-race__badge`; CSS lines 45-67 give every badge the same background, border, 34px height, 12px mono font and yellow icon. Four of the eight chips are a yellow glyph plus a single digit, mutually indistinguishable at speed.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 distributes by importance and by corner: item slot top-left (largest), position ordinal bottom-right at ~3x the size of anything else with a beveled ordinal suffix, lap counter top-right, coins under it, minimap bottom-left. Size, color and *location* all encode meaning, so the HUD is read peripherally with zero eye travel. A single uniform strip forces the player to actually read text mid-corner.
findings.fix:
Replace the single strip in ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:6542-6598 with four corner clusters (keep all existing data bindings and every `data-testid` so smoke tests survive):
• TOP-LEFT: the promoted item slot (see item-slot finding).
• TOP-RIGHT: `.tkr-lap` — eyebrow "LAP" at `font:800 10px/1, letter-spacing:.22em, color:rgba(248,251,255,.55)` above `{lap}` at `font:900 46px/1` with `/{laps}` at 22px and 55% opacity, baseline-aligned. Coins directly beneath: `<HeldItemIcon>`-style 22px ₿ glyph + `font:900 28px/1` count.
• BOTTOM-RIGHT: `.tkr-place` — the position, `font:900 84px/.85` numeral with the ordinal suffix as a superscript `<sup>` at 34px, `color:#ffd34f`, `-webkit-text-stroke:3px rgba(8,12,20,.92)`, `text-shadow:0 6px 20px rgba(0,0,0,.55)`. No pill/background at all — outlined text over the world, MK8-style.
• BOTTOM-LEFT: minimap (separate finding) with the speed readout tucked to its right: numeral `font:900 40px/1` + a 12px "KM/H" unit label (today the speed number at line 6549 has no unit at all).
• Mute button moves to a small 32px ghost icon at top-center-right, `opacity:.5`, out of the hierarchy entirely.
Delete `.three-kart-race__hud` / `.three-kart-race__badge` once nothing references them.

findings.title: No minimap — and a working minimap generator is already in the repo, unused
findings.evidence: No baseline frame contains a minimap. The shipped HUD (ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:6542-6598) has no track map element. Meanwhile `makeRaceMinimap()` exists complete at src/game/race/raceHud.jsx:15-57 (bounds fit, 12% padding, SVG path with branches) and is rendered at raceHud.jsx:282-302 — but raceHud.jsx is only imported by src/game/ArcadeRace3D.jsx:22, which is dead legacy. Both tracks already ship the data: `minimapPath` at src/game/courseV2.js:192/204 and src/game/race/tracks/penguinVillage.js:30.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8's minimap is how you play defensively — it's the only way to know a red shell is inbound, where the pack is, and what the next corner shape is. Without it every rival encounter here is a surprise (see `comeback-city-p0_78.png`: a rival is being passed and the player has no idea whether anyone is behind). It is also the single strongest "this is a real racing game" signal in a screenshot.
findings.fix: Port `makeRaceMinimap` from raceHud.jsx:15-57 into a new `src/game/race/raceMinimap.js`, import it in both ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx and (unchanged) raceHud.jsx. Render `<svg viewBox="0 0 100 100">` in a 148x148 (mobile 104x104) bottom-left panel: route path `stroke:rgba(248,251,255,.34); stroke-width:5; stroke-linejoin:round; fill:none` with a second copy underneath at `stroke:rgba(8,12,20,.55); stroke-width:8` for a contrast halo; branch paths keep `branch.accent` at width 3 dashed. Dots: compute them with the same `mapPoint` closure — export it — and drive them WITHOUT React: keep `<circle>` refs and write `setAttribute('cx'/'cy')` from inside the existing rAF frame loop (around line 6360) using `engine.sampler.pointAt(race.progress)` for the player and `race.rivals[i].progress` for rivals. Player dot r=4 `fill:#ffd34f` with a 1px dark stroke; rivals r=3 `fill:#ff4f7b`. Add a static finish-line tick: a 6-unit perpendicular segment at `mapPoint(course.startProgress)`. Zero new bytes — path data is already in the bundle.

findings.title: Two of eight HUD chips are developer telemetry the player cannot act on
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:6555-6562 renders `snapshot.boostHits` (⚡) and `snapshot.itemPickups` (✨) as first-class chips. In `comeback-city-p0_78.png` they read `⚡3 ✨4` immediately left of `₿4` — three adjacent yellow-glyph-plus-single-digit chips with no way to tell them apart. Neither number affects play: boostHits is a cumulative count of pads driven over, itemPickups is a cumulative count of boxes opened.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 shows exactly four numbers: item, position, lap, coins. Every one of them changes how you drive in the next five seconds. Spending 25% of a fixed HUD budget on debug counters trains the player to ignore the whole strip, which then also costs you the readouts that *do* matter.
findings.fix: Delete both chips from the HUD JSX (lines 6555-6562). Keep `boostHits`/`itemPickups` in the snapshot at 6365-6382 and in `publishTelemetry` — the QA/proof scripts read them from telemetry, not the DOM, and they belong on the post-race results panel as "Boosts 3 · Items 4" stat lines. Reclaim the space for the coin counter (bump it to the 28px treatment described in the hierarchy finding) and for the drift-charge meter, which is currently invisible to the player despite `race.driftTier` existing at line 288: add a 3-segment chevron bar under the speed readout that fills cyan→orange→purple per tier with a 120ms `filter:brightness(1.8)` flash at each tier-up.

findings.title: Nothing on the HUD animates on state change, and it updates at 7Hz
findings.evidence: src/game/ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:6363-6383 — `if (snapshotTimer > 0.14 || race.finished)` gates the entire HUD to ~7 updates/sec. `comeback-city-p0_06.png` (speed 88) vs `-p0_15.png` (speed 228): the number just teleports. The only animation in the whole HUD layer is `three-kart-item-pop` (css:107-126). Overtakes (position 4TH→3RD→1ST across p0_06/p0_33/p0_56) happen with no transition whatsoever, and coin pickups (visible mid-flight in `comeback-city-p0_56.png`) increment a static digit.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 sells every state change: the position numeral punches and flashes on an overtake, the coin counter pops and the +1 arcs off the coin, the item slot roulettes. That feedback is most of the felt 'juice' — without it a pass feels like nothing happened, which is exactly the read here.
findings.fix:
(1) Split the HUD into two update paths. High-frequency values (speed, drift charge, minimap dots) leave React entirely: hold `useRef` handles on the DOM nodes and write `node.textContent` / `style.transform` inside the existing rAF loop near line 6360. Discrete values (position, lap, coins, item) stay in the 0.14s snapshot — but tighten it to 0.08s so a coin pickup never lags its particle burst by 140ms.
(2) Add change-triggered animations via React `key` remount. Position: `<div className="tkr-place" key={snapshot.position}>` + `@keyframes tkr-place-punch { 0%{transform:scale(1.55); filter:brightness(2.4)} 45%{transform:scale(.94)} 100%{transform:scale(1)} }` at 420ms `cubic-bezier(.2,1.5,.4,1)`; add a `data-dir="gain|loss"` attribute (compare against a `usePrevious` ref) so a gain flashes `#5cff9d` and a loss flashes `#ff4f7b` for the first 45% of the keyframe.
(3) Coins: same key-remount trick with a 300ms `scale(1.3)→1` pop, plus a floating `+1` — an absolutely-positioned span that runs `translateY(0)→translateY(-26px)` with opacity 1→0 over 520ms and is removed on `animationend`.

findings.title: No lap flash, no final-lap callout, no race clock, no lap times
findings.evidence: `race.lap += 1` at ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:5644 has zero UI consequence — the lap chip silently ticks from 1/3 to 2/3. There is no elapsed-time display anywhere during the race: `race.raceTime` accumulates at line 5445 and is published in the snapshot (6371) but is only ever rendered *after* the finish (6612). No per-lap split is ever recorded — `onFinish` hardcodes `bestLap: null` (line ~6389). All nine baseline frames show `1/3` with no time readout.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 fires a full-width lap banner on every crossing and a distinct 'FINAL LAP' sting with a music-tempo change — it's the emotional structure of the race. It also keeps a running clock plus lap splits, which is what makes a solo time attack worth repeating. Without any of it, three laps here feel like one undifferentiated blob.
findings.fix:
(1) At line 5644, after the increment, set `race.lapFlash = { lap: race.lap, t: 1.6, final: race.lap >= race.laps }` and push `race.raceTime - race.lastLapAt` onto `race.lapTimes` (init `lapTimes: []`, `lastLapAt: 0` in the state object near line 284); decrement `race.lapFlash.t` each frame and publish it in the 6365 snapshot.
(2) Render a banner: full-width, `top:22%`, `background:linear-gradient(90deg,transparent,rgba(8,12,20,.72) 18%,rgba(8,12,20,.72) 82%,transparent)`, text `font:900 clamp(34px,5vw,64px)/1` reading `LAP 2/3`, or for `final: true` reading `FINAL LAP` in `#ff4f7b` with `-webkit-text-stroke:3px rgba(8,12,20,.9)`. Animate 1.6s: 0-12% slide in from `translateX(-14%)` with opacity 0→1, hold to 72%, then opacity→0 with `translateX(6%)`.
(3) Add the race clock under the lap counter in the top-right cluster: `formatTime(snapshot.raceTime)` (helper already exists at line 166) in `font:800 20px/1` tabular numerals, written via the rAF ref path so it counts smoothly at 60Hz, and show the previous lap's split beneath it at 13px/55% opacity for 4s after each crossing.

findings.title: The finish is a 440px grey pill, not a results presentation
findings.evidence: src/game/ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:6608-6618 — on finish the game renders one `.three-kart-race__results` box containing `Finish · 1ST`, a time, and a Restart button. CSS lines 128-157: `min-width:min(440px,100vw-32px)`, one border, no animation, no entrance. Simultaneously line 5646-5648 sets `race.speed = 0`, so the kart hard-stops the instant the line is crossed.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 stages the finish: the camera releases to a celebration angle, a large placement graphic sweeps in, then the full standings table builds row-by-row with times and points. It's the payoff for three laps. A single pill that appears instantly makes finishing 1st feel identical to finishing 4th.
findings.fix:
(1) Kill the hard stop: at 5646 replace `race.speed = 0` with a `race.finishCoast = 2.2` timer and decay speed by `race.speed *= Math.pow(0.35, dt)` while it runs, so the kart rolls out.
(2) Gate the results panel behind that coast — render nothing for the first 1.2s, then a full-screen `rgba(6,10,18,.72)` backdrop with `backdrop-filter:blur(6px)`.
(3) Panel content, staggered in: a giant ordinal (`font:900 clamp(90px,13vw,150px)`, `#ffd34f`, stroke 4px) sliding up 40px with a 0.45s spring at delay 0; the final time at 34px tabular at delay 0.18s; a standings list of the 4 racers (`race.rivals` already carries `name` and `totalProgressOf` already orders them — rivalRacers.js:134-138) with each row fading in at `delay: 0.32s + index*0.09s`; and the retired dev counters as a stat line (`Boosts · Items · Coins · Best lap` from the new `lapTimes` array) at delay 0.8s.
(4) Restart button becomes a 52px-tall primary button with the existing `#ffd34f` accent and a `Retry / Exit` pair rather than a single ghost chip.

findings.title: HUD typography has no outline or shadow, so it fights the sky it sits on
findings.evidence: comebackCityThreeKartRace.css:56-67 — `font: 800 12px/1 ui-monospace,...` with a flat `rgba(13,20,30,.72)` fill and a 1px hairline border; no `text-shadow`, no stroke. In `comeback-city-p0_06.png` the strip sits directly on the brightest orange band of the sunset, so it reads as a row of dark rectangular holes punched in the art. In `penguin-village-p0_15.png` the same dark strip sits on a near-white snow field — maximum contrast in the opposite direction, so it dominates the frame. Positioning is also arbitrary: `top: calc(72px + safe-area)` (css:52) floats the strip in dead space rather than hugging a corner.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 uses chunky rounded display type with a hard dark outline and a soft drop shadow, so the HUD is legible on snow, on lava and on Rainbow Road without needing a panel behind it — the text itself carries the contrast. That's why MK8 can get away with almost no HUD backgrounds, and why its HUD never looks pasted on.
findings.fix: Move to self-contrasting type and drop most panels. Every HUD numeral gets `-webkit-text-stroke: 3px rgba(8,12,20,.92); paint-order: stroke fill; text-shadow: 0 3px 10px rgba(0,0,0,.5);` (2px stroke under 24px). Replace the mono stack with the app's display face plus `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` so digits don't jitter width as speed changes. Where a panel is still needed (item slot, minimap) use `linear-gradient(160deg, rgba(13,20,30,.82), rgba(13,20,30,.55))` with `border-radius:16px` and a 1px top highlight `inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.14)` instead of the current flat rectangle + hairline. Re-anchor: `top: calc(16px + env(safe-area-inset-top,0px))` for top clusters, `bottom: calc(18px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom,0px))` for bottom ones — corners, not floating mid-air at 72px.

findings.title: aria-live on the whole HUD spams screen readers, and the kart CSS ignores reduced motion
findings.evidence: src/game/ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:6542 puts `aria-live="polite"` on the container that holds the speed readout, which changes ~7 times per second (snapshot gate at line 6364) — a screen reader will queue an unbounded stream of numbers. Separately, `grep -rn 'prefers-reduced-motion' src/` returns hits in src/index.css, WorldScene.jsx and raceMotionRuntime.js but *nothing* in comebackCityThreeKartRace.css, so `three-kart-item-pop` (css:107-126) and every animation proposed above will run at full amplitude for users who asked for less motion — even though the component already receives a `reducedMotion` prop.
findings.whyMk8Wins: Not a MK8 comparison so much as a shipping-quality one: MK8's HUD is fully static-readable and its flashes are bounded. A HUD that narrates every speed tick is worse than no live region at all, and unguarded scale-punch animations are the classic reduced-motion failure.
findings.fix:
(1) Remove `aria-live="polite"` from line 6542. Add a single dedicated `<div className="sr-only" aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true">` that renders ONLY discrete milestones — `Lap 2 of 3`, `Position 1st`, `Item: Ice Shield`, `Finished 1st, 1:24.31` — throttled to fire on value change, never on speed.
(2) Add at the bottom of comebackCityThreeKartRace.css: `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .three-kart-race *, .three-kart-race *::before { animation-duration:.01ms !important; animation-iteration-count:1 !important; transition-duration:.01ms !important; } }` and, for the elements where the animation IS the feedback (position punch, lap banner, GO!), swap to an opacity-only variant gated on `.three-kart-race[data-reduced-motion='true']` — plumb the existing `reducedMotion` prop onto the root div at line 6528 as `data-reduced-motion`, matching what raceHud.jsx:114 already does in the legacy path.

verdictVsMk8: Blind side-by-side this loses badly, and not because of art style — because almost nothing in frame is actually lit. The shipped monolith converts every authored environment GLB to `MeshBasicMaterial` (ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:1078), so the deco hotel, ice-cream truck, palms, igloos, coin pedestal and banners are unlit albedo with `castShadow=false, receiveShadow=false`. Measured on the baseline frames: snow at the coin pedestal's contact line is L=221 vs L=217 in the open (1.6% delta) and Comeback City grass beside the truck's wheels is L=50.6 vs L=50.5 in the open (0.2% delta) — that is mathematically zero grounding across the whole mid-field, where MK8 lands a 25-40% AO/shadow contact under every prop. The one real shadow that exists (player kart only) is a 384² BasicShadowMap over a 128-unit ortho, so it renders as a staircased, ~76%-black puddle detached from the tyres (penguin-village-p0_56), while the rival beside it has no shadow at all and visibly levitates. On top of that the key light sits at 46° elevation while the painted backdrop puts the sun on the horizon, and the backdrop ring tiles 5x so there are literally five suns in the sky at once (comeback-city-p0_67). MK8 would read as one coherent late-afternoon lighting event; this reads as flat-lit toys on a flat plane with one bad decal.

findings.title: Every authored environment prop is MeshBasicMaterial — the entire mid-field is unlit and casts/receives nothing
findings.evidence: src/game/ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:1076-1083 (mountMiamiAsset) replaces every mesh material with `new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({ map })` and sets castShadow=false, receiveShadow=false. That path mounts ALL hero props on both tracks (MIAMI_ASSETS at :994-1001 = condoTower/cornerArcade/decoHotel/lifeguard/palmCluster/retroDiner, plus PV_TRIBUTE_ASSETS merged at :1023). Frame proof: comeback-city-p0_06 — the deco hotel's two orthogonal cream faces measure L=151 (side) vs L=169.9 (front), a 12% delta that is texture, not light; the truck sits on a brown base plate with zero cast shadow on the grass (grass beside the wheels L=50.6 vs L=50.5 in the open). penguin-village-p0_06 — bitcoin coin, ice pedestal, lamp post and both banner poles all sit on snow measuring L=221 at contact vs L=217-220 in the open.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 lights every environment mesh with the same key/sky rig as the karts and bakes AO into the diffuse, so a Toad Harbour awning or a Sunshine Airport palm has a lit face, a shade face, and a soft occlusion pool where it meets the ground. Here the props are effectively 3D stickers: they never darken, never respond to the sunset direction, and never touch the floor. It is the single loudest 'this is not a Nintendo game' signal in the frame.
findings.fix: In `mountMiamiAsset` (ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:1076-1083) swap the material for `applyHeroRim === false` toon: `node.material = new THREE.MeshToonMaterial({ gradientMap: getToonGradient(), map: node.material?.map || null })`, and set `node.castShadow = true; node.receiveShadow = true`. Keep `applyAmbientSway(node.material, sway)` — it is an onBeforeCompile injection and works unchanged on MeshToonMaterial. Because the GLB textures were authored with baked highlights, drop the toon gradient's top band for these props only by passing a 3-band variant (`[110,110,110, 170,170,170, 255,255,255]`) so the lit face does not blow out. Then add a zero-byte contact-AO decal: build ONE shared 128×128 CanvasTexture radial gradient (rgba(0,0,0,0.55) centre -> transparent at r=1.0, gamma ~1.6), and in `mountMiamiAsset` after the `fitted` bounds are computed, push a matrix into a per-track `InstancedMesh(PlaneGeometry(1,1), MeshBasicMaterial({map: aoTex, transparent:true, depthWrite:false, blending: NormalBlending}))` scaled to `fitted` XZ size * 1.35, rotated -PI/2, y = fitted.min.y + 0.04, renderOrder 1. One extra draw call per track, zero new assets.

findings.title: Rival karts cast no shadow at all — they visibly levitate
findings.evidence: src/game/ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:4503-4507: `// Rivals keep only blob shadows ... model.group.traverse((node) => { node.castShadow = false; })`. Frame proof: penguin-village-p0_56 (crop of the 620-1020 x 400-600 region) — the player kart has a hard navy shadow while the grey/blue rival immediately to its right sits on the asphalt with nothing under it; same in penguin-village-p0_9 for the right-hand rival. The fallback blob (`#03060c`, opacity 0.24, ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:723-731) is invisible against Penguin Village's navy asphalt, so the rival reads as floating.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 gives all twelve karts a real projected shadow at all times; it is the primary depth cue that tells you whether a rival is beside you, ahead of you, or airborne off a ramp. Losing it on the AI is a gameplay readability bug, not just a look bug.
findings.fix: Delete the traverse at :4503-4507. Put rivals in a new hero shadow tier (see the tight-fit finding): a single directional light whose ortho box is ±26 units, which already covers the whole kart pack at race spacing. Instrument first: `renderer.info.render.calls` is currently 480 (CC) / 782 (PV) at frameWorkMs 0.94-1.11 (tmp/m2-b4-post-chain/capture-telemetry.json), so adding 5 rival bodies (≈5-10 depth-only draws) to a 1024² map is roughly 0.15ms — trivially inside the 16.6ms budget. For phones, keep rivals casting but drop the hero map to 512² and set `renderer.shadowMap.autoUpdate=false` with a manual `needsUpdate=true` every other frame.

findings.title: The one real shadow is a 384² BasicShadowMap over a 128-unit ortho — staircased, detached from the tyres, and ~76% black
findings.evidence: src/game/ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3859-3892: `shadowMap.type = THREE.BasicShadowMap` (no PCF at all), `sun.shadow.mapSize.set(384, 384)`, ortho left/right/top/bottom = ±64, bias -0.0008, no normalBias. 128 world units / 384 texels = 0.333 units per texel; the kart is ~13 units wide, so the whole shadow is ~40 texels and each texel covers ~5 screen pixels at chase distance. Frame proof: penguin-village-p0_56 crop shows a visible pixel staircase all along the shadow boundary, the shadow floats a half kart-length toward camera with no contact under the tyres, and measured luminance inside the shadow is L=20.0 vs L=108.5 on lit road — a 76% crater.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8's kart shadow is soft-edged, correctly anchored under the contact patch, and only darkens the surface ~35-40% because the sky/bounce term survives. Here the shadow reads as a black puddle decal that has come unstuck from the kart. The 76% figure is also a bug: the road is `MeshStandardMaterial` (ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:1661-1667) while everything else is toon, so the shadow subtracts 100% of the sun instead of dropping to the toon gradient's floor band.
findings.fix: In ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3860 set `renderer.shadowMap.type = THREE.PCFSoftShadowMap`. Replace the single ±64 box with a tight hero fit: `sun.shadow.mapSize.set(1024,1024)` desktop / 512 mobile (branch on `viewport.mobile`); ortho `left=right=top=bottom=±26`, `near=60`, `far=300`; `sun.shadow.bias = -0.00015`; `sun.shadow.normalBias = 0.45`; `sun.shadow.intensity = 0.55` (three r184 supports LightShadow.intensity — this alone takes the 76% crater to ~40% and is the highest value:effort line in this audit). Texel size becomes 52/1024 = 0.051 units, a 6.5x sharpening. In the frame loop at :6336-6338, aim the shadow at a point 12 units AHEAD of the kart (`playerSample.point.clone().addScaledVector(playerSample.tangent, 12)`) so the box is not wasted behind the camera, and texel-snap the target to kill shimmer: project the target into light space, `Math.round(v / texelWorldSize) * texelWorldSize`, project back. Also add `receiveShadow = true` to the kart bodies in `attachAuthoredKartBody`/`attachTripoKartBody`/`mountDriverAvatar` (:1430, :1535, :1562) so karts darken under the CC overpass visible in comeback-city-p0_06.

findings.title: Key light is at 46° elevation while the painted sun sits on the horizon — the lighting contradicts the art direction
findings.evidence: src/game/ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:6336: `engine.sun.position.set(playerSample.point.x - 95, playerSample.point.y + 110, playerSample.point.z - 45)`. Elevation = atan(110 / sqrt(95²+45²)) = atan(110/105.1) = 46.3°. The backdrop art (comeback-city-p0_33, -p0_9) paints a huge sun disc sitting ON the horizon behind the skyline — a 0-3° sunset. penguin-village frames put the glow band along the ice shelf horizon too. So the shading says noon and the sky says dusk.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8's Sunset Wilds / Toad Harbour lock the key light to the painted sun; you get long raking shadows that stretch a full kart length across the road, a strong warm/cool split between lit and shaded faces, and rim-lit silhouettes. A 46° key light produces short shadows tucked under objects, which is exactly why every frame here reads 'flat' despite an aggressive sunset palette. This is a zero-byte, zero-perf fix that will move the pillar more than any other single change.
findings.fix: Drop the sun to the painted elevation and lock its azimuth to the backdrop's sun. In the frame loop at ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:6336, replace the hardcoded offset with a per-track palette-driven vector: add `palette.sunDir = { azimuthDeg, elevationDeg, distance }` to src/game/race/tracks/comebackCity.js and penguinVillage.js, then `const e = THREE.MathUtils.degToRad(elevationDeg), a = THREE.MathUtils.degToRad(azimuthDeg); sun.position.copy(target).add(new THREE.Vector3(Math.cos(e)*Math.sin(a), Math.sin(e), Math.cos(e)*Math.cos(a)).multiplyScalar(distance))`. Start CC at elevation 11°, azimuth aimed at the backdrop sun disc (measure it once against a ?skyLab capture), distance 190; PV at elevation 9°, azimuth toward the glowing shelf. Bump `sun.shadow.camera.far` to 420 and `near` to 40 to accommodate the shallower angle. Widen the hero ortho along the light's Y axis to ±44 (long shadows need the extra footprint) while keeping ±26 on X.

findings.title: No ambient occlusion anywhere; pmndrs SSAOEffect is already in node_modules for near-zero bytes
findings.evidence: The post chain at src/game/ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3987-4011 contains only BloomEffect, SMAAEffect, VignetteEffect and ToneMappingEffect. `grep -o 'SSAOEffect|NormalPass|DepthDownsamplingPass' node_modules/postprocessing/build/index.js` returns all three — they ship in the 6.39.2 build already listed in package.json:66, so this is tree-shaken dead weight today, not a new dependency. Frame proof: comeback-city-p0_06 — the truck's undercarriage, the awning recesses, and the hotel's balcony overhangs all have zero corner darkening; penguin-village-p0_06 — the ice-block pedestal reads as a decal on the snow with no crevice darkening at the base.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 bakes AO into every environment lightmap, so corners, wheel wells, arcade overhangs and prop bases all sit in soft occlusion. AO is what makes a stylized scene feel solid rather than papercraft. Without it, low-poly stylization reads as 'cheap low-poly' instead of 'deliberate low-poly'.
findings.fix: In ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx's postChain branch (:3965-4011), before building the EffectPass: `const normalPass = new NormalPass(scene, camera); composer.addPass(normalPass);` then `const ssao = new SSAOEffect(camera, normalPass.texture, { blendFunction: BlendFunction.MULTIPLY, samples: 9, rings: 4, distanceThreshold: 0.35, distanceFalloff: 0.12, rangeThreshold: 0.0015, rangeFalloff: 0.004, luminanceInfluence: 0.65, radius: 0.09, intensity: 1.5, bias: 0.03, resolutionScale: 0.5, worldDistanceThreshold: 60, worldDistanceFalloff: 20, worldProximityThreshold: 6, worldProximityFalloff: 2 })` and push it into the effects array FIRST (before bloom, so occluded areas do not bloom). Use `new DepthDownsamplingPass({ normalBuffer: normalPass.texture, resolutionScale: 0.5 })` and feed `depthDownsamplingPass.texture` to `ssao.depthAwareUpsampling` for the half-res path. Gate on `!viewport.mobile` and behind `?postSsao=0` like the existing effect toggles. Cost estimate: one half-res normal prepass (the scene is 480/782 draw calls) plus a 9-sample half-res AO — budget ~1.2ms GPU on desktop against a measured 0.94-1.11ms frameWorkMs (tmp/m2-b4-post-chain/capture-telemetry.json), i.e. still 14ms of headroom. Verify with an A/B capture before shipping default-on.

findings.title: Light rig is fill-dominant — hemisphere 3.3 vs sun 2.6 means nothing has a real lit/shade split
findings.evidence: src/game/ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3874-3897: `HemisphereLight(sky, ground, palette.hemi?.intensity ?? 3.3)`, `DirectionalLight(sunColor, 2.6)`, `DirectionalLight(rimColor, 2.0)`. Penguin Village explicitly ships hemi intensity 3 (src/game/race/tracks/penguinVillage.js:134). Key:fill is 2.6:3.3 = 0.79:1, and the toon gradient's darkest band is 90/255 = 0.353 (ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:906-919), so the directional term can never fall below 35% — the maximum achievable lit/shade contrast is roughly 2.3:1 before ACES compresses it further. Frame proof: the ice-cream truck's two orthogonal faces measure L=151 vs L=169.9 (12% delta); penguin-village-p0_06's ice mountains are uniformly L=215-217 with no discernible facet shading at all.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8's key:fill is closer to 3:1 with a cool sky fill and a warm key, so a cube reads three distinct values and you instantly parse form and direction. Here the hemisphere washes everything to one value and the sunset colour only survives as tint, not as light. This is also what makes the snow field in Penguin Village read as a blank white sheet rather than a lit surface.
findings.fix: Rebalance in ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3874-3897 and the two track palettes: hemisphere intensity 3.3 -> 1.5 (CC) and 3 -> 1.4 (PV, src/game/race/tracks/penguinVillage.js:134); sun intensity 2.6 -> 4.4; rim 2.0 -> 1.6. Deepen the toon gradient's floor band from 90 to 58 in `getToonGradient()` (:907-912) and insert a 5th band so the ramp is `[58, 108, 158, 212, 255]` — this widens the shade range without hardening the cel steps. Compensate the overall exposure drop with `renderer.toneMappingExposure` 1.05 -> 1.12 (:3855) or, since the pmndrs chain owns tone mapping, by nudging `ToneMappingEffect` exposure. Judge with the same 9-point aaa-visual capture and confirm the truck's orthogonal-face delta moves from 12% to 35-45%.

findings.title: Only three objects in the whole 6700-line runtime cast shadows; the shadow ortho also hard-clips at ±64 units with no cascade
findings.evidence: `grep -n 'castShadow' src/game/ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx` yields `= true` at exactly three sites: :757 (player kart body), :2351 (breakable crate), :5293 (item-box GLB). Thirty-plus other sites explicitly set it false, including the Miami buildings (:1080), marchers (:5232), crossers (:4381/:4444), coin InstancedMesh (:4136/:4137), blizzards (:4285) and rivals (:4506). Separately, `sun.shadow.camera` is ±64 (:3886-3889) centred on the player, so even if props did cast, everything beyond 64 units is outside the frustum. The castShadow flags in src/game/race/render/createTrackMesh.js and createRaceScenery.js are dead — the shipped monolith imports only createRaceRenderer/fitRaceRendererToCanvas from that directory (ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:143) and builds its own track at :1599.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 shadows the whole readable volume: karts, items, the coin field, roadside furniture and buildings all darken the ground, which is what makes the track surface look like a place rather than a ribbon. Here the shadow pass renders one kart and an item box, which is why the road plane is a uniform value in every baseline frame.
findings.fix: Two-tier plan, no CSM dependency needed. Tier A (dynamic hero, per-frame): the ±26 tight-fit map from the earlier finding, casting set = player + rivals + drivers + item boxes + breakables + coin InstancedMesh (flip :4136 to castShadow=true — one instanced depth draw covers the whole field). Tier B (static world): add a SECOND `THREE.DirectionalLight` sharing the sun's direction and colour at `intensity = 0` with `castShadow = true`, `mapSize 1536²`, ortho ±190, `shadow.autoUpdate = false`; render its map once after all GLB mounts resolve (`renderer.shadowMap.needsUpdate = true` on the frame the miamiMountStats.mounted count stops rising), then never again. A zero-intensity light still contributes its shadow term to every receiver in three r184, so the buildings/props/mountains get a permanent baked-quality shadow for the cost of ONE depth render for the whole race. Because the world is static this is genuinely free per-frame and needs no new assets. Guard Tier B behind `!viewport.mobile` initially.

findings.title: The backdrop ring tiles 5x so there are up to five suns in the sky at once
findings.evidence: src/game/ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3957: `addBackdropRing(strips.far, { height: 380, order: -20, radius: 780, repeats: 5, y: 140 })` with `texture.wrapS = THREE.MirroredRepeatWrapping; texture.repeat.x = repeats` (:3940-3941). The far backdrop art contains a painted sun disc, so it repeats five times around the horizon. Frame proof: comeback-city-p0_67 shows TWO large yellow sun discs in one 76°-FOV frame (one at x≈700, one at x≈960); comeback-city-p0_06 shows a partial disc at the left edge and a full disc at the far right; penguin-village frames show the same duplication in the glowing shelf hotspots.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 skyboxes have exactly one sun and the key light comes from it. Two suns in frame is the kind of thing a player screenshots and posts as a bug — it destroys the credibility of the entire lighting setup before you even get to shadow quality. It is also directly why the lighting reads as directionless: there is no single source to read shadows against.
findings.fix: Set `repeats: 1` for the FAR ring at ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3957 and switch that ring's `texture.wrapS` to `THREE.ClampToEdgeWrapping` (the near silhouette ring at :3958 can keep repeats: 7 — it has no sun). If the far strip's aspect does not cover 360° at repeat 1, the cheaper fix is to paint the sun OUT of the strip (re-export the existing backdrop asset, same byte budget) and add a real 3D sun: a `THREE.Sprite` with the existing `makeGlowTexture()` output, scale ~120, `fog: false`, `depthWrite: false`, renderOrder -18, positioned each frame at `camera.position + sunDirection * 1500` so it is always exactly where the key light comes from. That also makes the elevation fix self-verifying — if the shadows point wrong you can see it against the sprite.

findings.title: Blob shadow is a hard-edged, world-axis-aligned opaque disc that never yaws, never conforms to the road, and never reacts to air time
findings.evidence: src/game/ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:723-736: `new THREE.CircleGeometry(6.2 * scale, 22)` with `MeshBasicMaterial({ color: '#03060c', opacity: 0.24 })`, `shadow.scale.y = 1.35`, `shadow.rotation.x = -Math.PI/2`, `position.y = 0.07`. It is set once at construction and never touched again — `grep` for shadow-mesh writes in the frame loop returns nothing. So (a) the ellipse's long axis is locked to world Z regardless of kart heading, (b) it has a hard 22-segment polygon edge with no falloff, (c) it does not shrink/soften when the kart is airborne, and (d) it is added to the outer group at y=0.07 so it clips or floats on any banked or sloped section. Frame proof: comeback-city-p0_9 crop — the disc under the ice kart is a visible flat-grey ellipse offset to the right of the kart with a hard elliptical boundary, reading as a decal painted on the tarmac.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 blends its projected shadow with a soft-edged contact darkening that hugs the kart footprint and lifts away when the kart leaves the ground — you can read jump height off the shadow gap. Here the disc communicates nothing and actively looks like a rendering artefact on light surfaces.
findings.fix: Replace the CircleGeometry/MeshBasicMaterial with a shared 128×128 CanvasTexture radial falloff (same texture as the prop contact decals — build it once in a module-level `getContactShadowTexture()`): `new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.PlaneGeometry(1,1), new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({ map: tex, transparent: true, depthWrite: false, opacity: 0.42 }))`, scale (13, 17) in kart units. Move the mesh OUT of the kart group into `world` and drive it per-frame in the player/rival sync block: position = `sampler.pointAt(progress, lane).point` + 0.06 * surface normal; `rotation.y` = kart heading; `quaternion` aligned to the surface normal so it lies flat on banked road; `scale *= clamp(1 - airHeight/26, 0.55, 1)` and `material.opacity = 0.42 * clamp(1 - airHeight/26, 0.25, 1)`. Give the same treatment to rivals so their shadow exists even at long range where the hero shadow map does not reach. Zero new bytes; one extra transparent draw per kart.

findings.title: Road is MeshStandardMaterial while everything else is toon — shadows punch a black hole in it instead of a cel shade band
findings.evidence: src/game/ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:1661-1668: the road is `new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color:'#ffffff', map: asphaltTexture, metalness: 0.06, roughness: 0.6, side: DoubleSide })`; the ground plane at :1684 is also MeshStandard. Every kart, driver, prop and dressing mesh is MeshToonMaterial (:1295-1302, :1425, :1530, :1558). Because Standard has no gradient floor, a shadowed texel loses 100% of the sun term. Measured on penguin-village-p0_56: inside the player shadow L=20.0, lit road immediately beside it L=56.5, brighter lit road L=108.5 — a 65-76% drop, versus the ~35% floor the toon gradient would enforce.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 keeps the shaded road within about 35-40% of the lit value and tints it toward the sky colour, so shadows read as shade rather than as holes. A near-black shadow on a dark-navy asphalt also destroys the contrast the drift sparks and boost trails need to pop against.
findings.fix: Two independent levers, apply both. (1) Set `sun.shadow.intensity = 0.55` (three r184 LightShadow.intensity, ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3892 area) — this alone lifts the crater from 76% to ~42% with zero shader work. (2) Convert the road and ground to MeshToonMaterial with the shared gradient so the surface shades in the same language as the karts: `new THREE.MeshToonMaterial({ color:'#ffffff', map: asphaltTexture, gradientMap: getToonGradient() })` at :1661 and :1684, keeping `receiveShadow = true`. Toon has no metalness/roughness so the 0.06/0.6 values are dropped — verify the wet-asphalt sheen in Comeback City still reads; if it is missed, add it back as a cheap `emissiveMap`-driven sheen rather than reintroducing Standard. Also tint the shadow toward the hemisphere sky colour by raising `hemi` slightly on the road only (or accept the sky-tinted result of the light rebalance).

findings.title: No shadow LOD or mobile plan — one 384² map, autoUpdate on, for every device
findings.evidence: src/game/ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3859-3892 configures shadows once at scene creation with no reference to `viewport.mobile` (which is resolved separately in src/game/race/render/createRaceScene.js:74 and used for render scale 0.6 vs 0.85). `renderer.shadowMap.autoUpdate` is left at its default `true`, so the full shadow pass re-renders every frame even though the only caster that moves is the player. Nothing throttles or disables the pass under load, and there is no `?shadow=` diagnostic toggle to A/B it the way `?post=`, `?postBloom=` and `?trackVisuals=` exist for every other visual system.
findings.whyMk8Wins: Not a look gap — a shipping-risk gap. Every proposed improvement in this pillar (bigger map, PCF, rivals casting, world-tier map, SSAO) needs a phone story before it can ship default-on, and right now there is no scaffolding to build one and no capture harness that reports fps (tmp/aaa-visual/baseline/capture-manifest.json has `fps: null, drawCalls: null, triangles: null` for all 18 frames, so the pillar is currently unmeasurable).
findings.fix: Add a shadow quality tier resolved next to the existing flags at ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:4999-5019: `const shadowTier = params.get('shadow') ?? (viewport.mobile ? 'low' : 'high')`. high = 1024² hero + 1536² static world tier + PCFSoft + SSAO; low = 512² hero + PCF (not soft) + static world tier only + no SSAO; off = blob/contact decals only. Set `renderer.shadowMap.autoUpdate = false` and drive `renderer.shadowMap.needsUpdate = true` manually — every frame on high, every second frame on low. Fix the capture harness first: scripts/aaa-visual-capture.mjs is writing nulls for fps/drawCalls/triangles even though `rendererStatsForFrame` already publishes them into `window.__comebackCityKartTelemetry` (ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:6356-6358) — wire those through so every change in this pillar lands with a measured before/after.

findings.title: Karts never receive shadows, so the Comeback City overpass and every prop pass through does nothing to them
findings.evidence: `mountDriverAvatar` (:1425-1431), `attachTripoKartBody` (:1526-1536) and `attachAuthoredKartBody` (:1555-1563) all set `node.castShadow = castsShadow` but never touch `receiveShadow`, which defaults to false. The procedural fallback kart's traverse at :756-758 also only sets castShadow. Frame proof: comeback-city-p0_06 shows an elevated neon overpass crossing the track in the mid-distance; when a kart drives under it (and under the finish gate at :2590) its brightness is completely unchanged.
findings.whyMk8Wins: Driving into shade in MK8 visibly dims the kart, which sells the third dimension of the track and makes tunnels and underpasses feel like real spaces. It is also free once the shadow map is already being rendered.
findings.fix: Add `node.receiveShadow = true` alongside every `node.castShadow = ...` in mountDriverAvatar (:1430), attachTripoKartBody (:1535), attachAuthoredKartBody (:1562) and the procedural fallback traverse (:757). Then make the overpass, the finish gate deck and the CC bridge deck cast into the world-tier static shadow map (they are currently in the castShadow=false set). Because the hero tier's ortho is only ±26 units, the overpass shadow must come from the static world tier — which is exactly the case for building it as a separate second light.

verdictVsMk8: Blind side-by-side this loses badly, and for a structural reason: the shipped camera is not a chase camera at all. It is a spline dolly that rides the track centerline 38 arc-units behind the player's *progress value* (ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:6309-6314) and looks down the track tangent — it never reads the kart's position, heading, drift yaw, hop height, or steer. Across 18 baseline frames spanning two tracks, speeds 73-289, straights, a hard right-hander and a bridge crest, the kart sits within a few percent of the same screen point (~52% height, ~8% of frame width) with the horizon pinned at ~47% and a perfectly level roll. MK8's camera is a damped boom on the kart that swings, leads, rolls, punches FOV and shakes; here nothing the player does moves the camera, so 289 km/h reads exactly like 88. On top of that there are three outright visible bugs: rivals routinely eclipse the player kart (comeback-city-p0_78), the camera aims off the *outside* of every corner because the look target is a straight tangent line, and a hardcoded "underpass duck" fires on a progress window that matches neither track's bridge. Note for the orchestrator: src/game/race/camera/chaseCamera.js is dead code — only ArcadeRace3D.jsx imports it — so every fix below targets the monolith.

findings.title: Rival karts eclipse the player kart — the camera has no near-band occlusion handling
findings.evidence: tmp/aaa-visual/baseline/comeback-city-p0_78.png: the blue Ice Racer rival fills the bottom-left ~40% of the frame while the player (dark red kart) is a ~130px sliver at (820,480). Same failure in comeback-city-p0_67.png (rival owns the whole lower-left quadrant), comeback-city-p0_9.png and penguin-village-p0_24.png (rival directly on top of the player). Cause: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:6309-6310 places the camera at sampler.pointAt(race.progress - 38/length, race.lane*0.6), so any rival drafting 15-25 units behind the player sits only 13-23 units from the camera — 1.6-2.9x closer than the player and therefore 1.6-2.9x larger on screen. Nothing in the shipped frame loop fades or culls it.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 explicitly protects the player silhouette: karts entering the camera's near band are alpha-faded out (and the boom is short enough that a trailing rival is mostly behind the lens). You are never unable to see your own kart in MK8. Here you lose your kart for seconds at a time, which is a control failure, not just an art failure.
findings.fix: In ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx, in the rival-pose loop that calls updateVehiclePose for each rival (same block as line ~5910 player pose), after positioning each rival compute d = rival.group.position.distanceTo(engine.camera.position). Fade with a = smoothstep(10, 24, d) (0 at 10 units, 1 at 24). Apply by walking rival.group once at build time to collect its materials into rivalModel.fadeMaterials (set transparent:true, depthWrite:false once, keep the original opacity in userData.baseOpacity), then per frame set m.opacity = baseOpacity * a and rival.group.visible = a > 0.02. Guard the whole thing so it only runs on the 4-6 rivals (cost is ~6 distance checks + ~30 opacity writes/frame, negligible). Do NOT toggle transparent per-frame — that recompiles shaders.

findings.title: Hardcoded 'underpass' camera duck fires on a progress window that matches neither track's bridge
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:6296 `const underpass = race.progress > 0.15 && race.progress < 0.24;` multiplies camera height by 0.62 (line 6308). But comebackCity.js:32 puts the bridge band at progress 0.40-0.534 and penguinVillage.js:67 puts it at 0.55-0.67. So on BOTH shipped tracks the camera drops from 10.5 to 6.51 units for 9% of every lap on an ordinary straight, and does not duck at all when the kart is actually on the bridge. It is stale constants from a retired Comeback City layout. It is also an unsmoothed step: at the vertical follow rate (see the horizon-judder finding, effective tau ~40 ms) the 4-unit drop completes in ~4 frames — a hard pop of the horizon, twice per lap, on every race.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8's clearance ducks are authored per-geometry and eased in/out over ~0.5s; the horizon never steps. A camera that jumps 4 units at a fixed point of every lap for no on-screen reason reads as a bug on first play.
findings.fix: Delete line 6296. Read the band from track data instead: `const band = trackDef.course.elevation?.cameraDuckBand ?? null;` and add `cameraDuckBand: { from, to, scale }` to comebackCity.js:32 and penguinVillage.js:67 (CC has crestLaunch:true so it needs NO duck — omit it; PV's road climbs ONTO the ice bridge so it also needs none — the honest fix is likely to ship zero duck bands and delete the multiplier entirely). If a duck is wanted later, drive it through a smoothstep ramp: duck = smoothstep(from, from+0.02, p) * (1 - smoothstep(to-0.02, to, p)), height *= lerp(1, band.scale, duck).

findings.title: Look target is a straight tangent ray, so the camera aims off the OUTSIDE of every corner instead of into it
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:6320-6323: `lookAt = playerSample.point + playerSample.tangent * 30 + (0,4.5,0)`. playerSample.tangent is the tangent AT THE KART, so the look target leaves the road on any curve by roughly 30^2/(2R): on a 90-unit-radius corner that is 5 units outside the racing line, on a 45-unit hairpin it is 10 units outside — beyond the 25-29 unit road half-width, i.e. the camera is literally aimed at the scenery. Visible in tmp/aaa-visual/baseline/comeback-city-p0_9.png: a hard right-hander at speed 264 where the frame is aimed straight/left of the apex and the corner exit is squeezed against the right edge, and in penguin-village-p0_9.png where the road exit disappears behind the left of frame. There is zero curvature-based lead anywhere in the shipped block.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 aims at a point sampled ALONG the track ahead and adds an extra yaw lead proportional to upcoming curvature, so on entry you are already looking at the apex and on exit you are looking at the next straight. That look-ahead is what makes MK8 corners readable at speed; here you are reading the corner peripherally.
findings.fix: Replace the tangent-ray target with a spline sample plus a curvature lead. In the same block: `const aheadUnits = phoneWide ? 30 : 34; const aheadP = wrap01(race.progress + aheadUnits / engine.sampler.length); const aheadSample = engine.sampler.pointAt(aheadP, race.lane * 0.35);` then `lookAt = aheadSample.point.clone().add(new THREE.Vector3(0, lookUp, 0))`. Add the lead: `const curv = signedAngleDelta(atan2(aheadSample.tangent.x, aheadSample.tangent.z), atan2(playerSample.tangent.x, playerSample.tangent.z));` and push the target sideways by the road normal * clamp(curv, -0.6, 0.6) * 14 so the camera over-aims into the corner (MK8's lead). Smooth `curv` with a tau of ~0.20s (factor 1 - Math.pow(0.007, dt)) so it does not snap on spline seams. Cost: one extra sampler.pointAt per frame.

findings.title: The camera is a track dolly, not a chase boom — it never reads the kart's heading, drift yaw, or steer
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:6305-6324 is the entire shipped camera. Position = sampler.pointAt(progress - 38/len, lane*0.6) + height. Look = tangent ray. FOV = f(speed). That is all. race.steer, driftState.slideYaw (driftFeel.js:100), race.airState, race.spinTimer, and the kart's own yaw (set at line 5369-5372 as trackYaw - slideYaw + extraYaw) are never read by the camera. Consequence in frames: comeback-city-p0_06 (speed 88, straight), -p0_24 (285), -p0_45 (287), -p0_9 (264, hard right-hander) and penguin-village-p0_15/-p0_56/-p0_9 all put the kart within a few percent of the same screen coordinate with an identically level horizon. When the player spins out (spinOutYaw, line 5375) the camera keeps staring down the track and the kart pirouettes in place with no camera reaction at all.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 hangs the camera off the kart on a damped yaw spring (~0.25-0.35s), so the kart visibly rotates *inside* the frame before the camera catches up. That lag is the single largest contributor to MK8's sense of weight and of driving rather than being carried. A spline dolly cannot produce it at any parameter setting.
findings.fix: Anchor the boom to the kart. Keep a persistent `camYaw` in the frame-loop closure. Per frame: `const kartYaw = Math.atan2(playerSample.tangent.x, playerSample.tangent.z) - driftState.slideYaw + race.airState.spin;` `const targetYaw = trackYaw + (kartYaw - trackYaw) * 0.55 + race.steer * 0.10;` `camYaw += signedAngleDelta(targetYaw, camYaw) * (1 - Math.pow(0.02, dt));` (tau ~255 ms — deliberately looser than the 96 ms position follow). Then build the boom off the kart's world point rather than a spline point: `const anchor = playerSample.point.clone(); anchor.y += hop * 0.75;` `desiredCamera = anchor.clone().addScaledVector(new THREE.Vector3(Math.sin(camYaw), 0, Math.cos(camYaw)), -back).add(new THREE.Vector3(0, height + clamp(race.speed/90,0,2.2), 0));` Keep the existing sampler-based point as a fallback blend at 0.25 weight so tight hairpins cannot swing the camera into a wall (the property the current design was buying). This is the change that unlocks findings 5, 9 and 11 below.

findings.title: Framing is a distant spectator shot: kart is ~8% of frame width at 52% height, with 45% of every frame dead foreground asphalt
findings.evidence: Measured on tmp/aaa-visual/baseline/penguin-village-p0_56.png and -p0_15.png and comeback-city-p0_24.png (1600x900): the player kart spans ~130px (8.1% of width), its centre sits at y~470 (52% down), the horizon sits at y~430 (47%), and everything below y~560 — 38% of the frame area — is empty road with no gameplay information in it. Parameters: back 38 units (line 6305), height 10.5 + up to 2.2 speed lift (6308/6313), lookUp 4.5 (6323), FOV 70 + clamp(speed/228,0,1.15)*7 = 77 deg vertical at race speed (6326-6329). At 16:9 that is a 110 deg horizontal FOV — a fisheye by kart-racer standards.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8's default chase puts the kart at roughly 16-20% of frame width with its base at ~75-80% of frame height and the horizon at ~40%, on a much narrower lens. That framing does three things this one does not: the kart reads as the subject, the drift sparks and exhaust at the kart's rear are large enough to see, and the road ahead (the part you must plan for) occupies the middle band instead of being compressed into a 60px sliver near the horizon.
findings.fix: In the else-branch at ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:6305-6329 change: cameraBackUnits desktop 38 -> 26 (mobile 43 -> 30, phoneWide 33 -> 24); cameraHeight desktop 10.5 -> 7.6 (phoneWide 10 -> 7.2, mobile 12.5 -> 8.6); lookUp 4.5 -> 2.8 (mobile 5.5 -> 3.0); base FOV desktop 70 -> 57 (mobile 68 -> 58, phoneWide 63 -> 55) with the speed term 7 -> 9. Derivation for the desktop numbers: apparent kart size scales as 1/(back * tan(hFov/2)); 38*tan(54.7deg)=53.7 today vs 26*tan(31.9deg*1.778 aspect)=28.9 after, i.e. 1.86x larger kart (~15% of frame width). Vertical: pitch = atan((7.6+2.2-2.8)/(26+34)) = 6.65deg down, so the kart lands at 50% + tan(13.95deg)/tan(32deg)*50% = 70% frame height and the horizon at 40.7%. Land this together with the corner-look-ahead fix (aheadUnits 34) since the pitch derivation assumes it.

findings.title: Drift produces zero camera response — no swing-out, no lead, no roll, no pull-back
findings.evidence: driftFeel.js:100 smooths a real slideYaw and ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:5369-5371 applies it to the kart mesh plus a body roll of -(slideYaw*0.3 + steer*0.1). The camera block (6285-6334) reads none of it: the only drift-adjacent term in the entire shipped camera is `miniTurboActive ? 3.5 : 0` added to FOV (line 6329). There is no camera.rotation.z write anywhere in the file (grep for `engine.camera.` returns only position.lerp, lookAt, fov). Frame evidence: comeback-city-p0_9.png is a hard right-hander taken at speed 264 with a perfectly level horizon and a dead-centre kart.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 swings the camera to the OUTSIDE of the slide and yaws it to lead the drift direction, so a left-hand drift shows you the left-hand apex you are aiming at; it also rolls a few degrees into the slide and tightens slightly as the mini-turbo charges. The drift is the game's core verb and here it is the one action the camera completely ignores.
findings.fix: Three additive terms, all in the camera block. (1) Swing-out: `const swing = driftState.direction * clamp(driftState.tier/3, 0, 1) * (race.drift ? 1 : 0);` smoothed at tau 0.18s, then offset desiredCamera laterally along the road normal by `swing * 7` units (toward the outside of the slide). (2) Lead: fold slideYaw into camYaw at 0.55 weight (already specified in the boom finding) — this is what makes the camera look where the kart is sliding TO. (3) Roll: after camera.lookAt, `engine.camera.rotation.z += -(driftState.slideYaw * 0.22 + race.steer * 0.05) * clamp(race.speed/MAX_SPEED,0,1);` clamped to +/-0.09 rad (5.2 deg) and skipped when reducedMotion. Cap the total swing so the kart never leaves the centre 30% of frame width.

findings.title: No start-line cinematic and a near-empty finish beat
findings.evidence: race.countdown runs 2.2s (line 284, ticked at 5443) and the camera block never references it — grep for `countdown` in ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx returns lines 284, 4720, 5443-5444, 5535, 6368, 6600-6601 and nothing inside 6285-6334. So the 2.2 seconds before GO use the exact same chase framing as lap 3. The finish beat is two constants: back 30, height 13, lookAt kart+6 (lines 6305-6319) — no orbit, no push-in, no time dilation, no FOV move (FOV keeps tracking speed, so it drifts 78 -> 70 as the kart coasts, an unauthored slow zoom).
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 authors both ends: a grid fly-through / orbit that resolves to the chase on '2', a snap-behind punch on GO, and a finish-line camera that breaks from the chase to frame the winner. Those beats are most of what makes a race feel like an event rather than a loop, and they are the moments a first-time player screenshots.
findings.fix: Add an authored camera state machine keyed on race.countdown and race.finished, in the same block. START (countdown 2.2 -> 0.9): orbit — `const t = 1 - race.countdown/2.2; const orbitYaw = trackYaw + Math.PI + lerp(2.4, 0, smoothstep(0,1,t));` boom at back lerp(18, 26, t), height lerp(4.5, 7.6, t), FOV lerp(48, 57, t), lookAt = kart + (0,2.2,0). SETTLE (0.9 -> 0): blend that pose into the normal chase pose with weight smoothstep(0.9, 0.15, countdown). GO punch: on the countdown<=0 transition (line 5444) set a `race.camPunch = 0.28` timer and add `FOV += (camPunch/0.28) * 9` with a fast attack. FINISH: on race.finished start a 2.4s orbit — yaw sweeps kartYaw+Math.PI -> kartYaw+Math.PI+1.9 over 2.4s with back 30 -> 22, height 13 -> 9, FOV -> 50, lookAt kart + (0,3.5,0). All parameter-driven, no assets.

findings.title: Zero camera shake in the shipped path — impacts, boosts and landings move the camera not at all
findings.evidence: grep for `cameraShakeTimer` returns only src/game/race/raceState.js:253, raceFrameClock.js:45/53/66, raceHitRuntime.js:17, racePlayerFrame.js:296, kartPhysics.js:164/219 and the dead chaseCamera.js:328 — none of those modules feed the shipped monolith's camera, and ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx contains no shake term at all. So taking a sardine rocket, scraping a wall, hitting a boost pad or slamming down off the bridge crest (comebackCity.js:32, crestLaunch:true) all leave the camera perfectly smooth. Worth noting the dead implementation was also broken: chaseCamera.js:330-331 adds shake to `_desired` *before* the position lerp at line 351, so at 60fps only 14.5% of the 1.2-unit amplitude ever reached the camera (~0.17 units, invisible).
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 punches the camera on every impact, landing and boost-pad hit — a short directional impulse, not white noise — and that impulse is what sells the item hit as painful and the boost as violent. Without it, getting hit is a HUD event only.
findings.fix: Add a small impulse spring in ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx. State: `const camImpulse = { x:0, y:0, vx:0, vy:0 };`. Fire helper `kick(ax, ay)` -> camImpulse.vx += ax, .vy += ay. Integrate per frame with a critically-damped spring (omega 34, zeta 0.55): `camImpulse.vx += (-omega*omega*camImpulse.x - 2*zeta*omega*camImpulse.vx) * dt; camImpulse.x += camImpulse.vx * dt;` (same for y). Apply AFTER camera.position.lerp and AFTER lookAt, as a screen-space offset: `engine.camera.translateX(camImpulse.x); engine.camera.translateY(camImpulse.y);` so the lerp cannot swallow it. Call sites and magnitudes: item hit (near line 5766/5781 projectile+fishbone handlers) kick(±1.1, -0.9); wall/scrape (line 5634 lane-clamp branch) kick(±0.45, -0.2); landing from airState (transition airborne true->false near 5526) kick(0, -1.6 * clamp(speed/MAX_SPEED,0,1)); boost pad (line 5674) kick(0, +0.7). Skip entirely when reducedMotion.

findings.title: FOV speed term saturates below boost speed, so the biggest speed events produce no lens response
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:6326-6329: `targetFov = 70 + clamp(race.speed / MAX_SPEED, 0, 1.15) * 7 + (miniTurboActive ? 3.5 : 0)` with MAX_SPEED = 228 (line 173). The clamp caps at speed 262.2. The baseline manifest records boost speeds of 285, 287, 289 on comeback-city and 280-285 on penguin-village — i.e. every boost in the capture is above the clamp, so a boost pad or mushroom contributes exactly 0 additional FOV. The only distinct boost signal is the mini-turbo's +3.5 deg, and even that is smoothed at tau 145 ms (base 0.001, line 6332), so a 0.9s mini-turbo peaks at roughly +3.3 deg — under the threshold at which a viewer registers a lens change.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 punches roughly 10-14 deg on a mushroom with a very fast attack (~80ms) and a slow release (~400ms), layered with radial blur; the asymmetry is the whole trick — the punch reads as an event, the decay reads as momentum. A symmetric 3.5 deg on a 145ms filter reads as nothing.
findings.fix: Split boost off the speed curve into its own channel with asymmetric smoothing. Replace lines 6326-6333 with: `const speedFov = base + clamp(race.speed / MAX_SPEED, 0, 1.0) * 9;` (raise the clamp ceiling to 1.0 and let boost drive the punch channel instead). Add persistent `let boostFov = 0;` and per frame `const boostTarget = (race.boostTimer > 0 ? 11 : 0) + (miniTurboActive ? 4.5 + driftState.miniTurboTier * 1.5 : 0); const rate = boostTarget > boostFov ? 0.0000001 : 0.05; boostFov = lerp(boostFov, boostTarget, 1 - Math.pow(rate, dt));` — that gives attack tau ~62 ms and release tau ~334 ms. Then `targetFov = speedFov + boostFov;` and drop the `> 0.1` gate to `> 0.02` so small moves are not quantised away. Zero cost.

findings.title: Airtime and landing are entirely uncompensated — the look target sits on the ground while the kart flies
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:6320-6323 builds the look target from `playerSample.point`, which is `engine.sampler.pointAt(race.progress, race.lane)` (line 5910) — the ROAD surface. The kart's hop is applied separately, only to the mesh (line 5917: hopHeightFor(hopTimer) + airState.height + shortcut arc). airTricks.js:6-17 gives launchLift 0.105 and gravity 58, so at race speed 228 the apex is 23.9^2/(2*58) = 4.9 units with ~0.82s of hang time; the Comeback City bridge crest (comebackCity.js:32, peak 21, crestLaunch:true) is a bigger launch. At 38 units back the kart therefore climbs ~7.4 deg = ~11% of frame height and the camera does not move a pixel. Landing likewise: race.landSquashTimer squashes the mesh (line 5908) and the camera does nothing.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 lifts and pitches the boom on a launch so the kart stays framed and you can read the landing zone, then punches the camera down ~0.12s on touchdown and springs back. Here a big jump pushes the kart toward the top of the frame and hides the landing, and the landing itself has no weight.
findings.fix: Two changes. (1) Track the hop once: hoist the hop sum from line 5917 into `const hopHeight = hopHeightFor(driftState.hopTimer) + race.airState.height + (race.shortcut.active ? shortcutArcHeight(...) : 0);` and reuse it in the camera block. Add `hopHeight * 0.7` to the camera height term (line 6313) and `hopHeight * 0.45` to the lookUp term (line 6323) — partial follow, so the kart still rises in frame (that is the airtime read) but never leaves the middle band. (2) Landing punch: detect the airborne true->false transition around line 5526 and fire the shake helper from the shake finding with kick(0, -1.6 * clamp(race.speed/MAX_SPEED,0,1)) plus a 0.15s FOV dip of -4 deg on the boost channel. Also add `airState.airborne` to the FOV formula as a +3 deg widen while in flight.

findings.title: Vertical follow is 2.4x stiffer than horizontal (via a compounded double lerp), so the horizon judders on every elevation ripple
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:6314 lerps the FULL Vector3 (including y) at `1 - Math.pow(0.00003, dt)` (k = 10.41/s, tau = 96 ms), then line 6317 immediately re-lerps the ALREADY-updated y at `1 - Math.pow(0.0000005, dt)` (k = 14.51/s). The two compose to k = 24.9/s, tau = 40 ms — the vertical axis is the stiffest thing in the camera, when it should be the softest. Both tracks are elevated: comebackCity.js:32 bridgeBand peak 21 units over progress 0.40-0.534, penguinVillage.js:67 peak 17 over 0.55-0.67. Every metre of that profile, plus every spline seam, transfers to the horizon almost 1:1. The double-lerp is also a latent maintenance trap: anyone tuning the constant on 6317 will be tuning half of the real rate.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 keeps the vertical channel notably softer than the lateral one and adds a small dead zone, so crests and dips are absorbed and the horizon stays as the stable reference the player reads speed and steering against. Here the horizon is the least stable element on screen.
findings.fix: Delete line 6317 entirely and lerp the vector once, then apply a soft vertical follow separately and correctly: `const dy = desiredCamera.y - engine.camera.position.y; const dead = 0.8; const pull = Math.sign(dy) * Math.max(0, Math.abs(dy) - dead); engine.camera.position.y += pull * (1 - Math.pow(0.06, dt));` — k = 2.81/s, tau = 356 ms, with a 0.8-unit dead zone that swallows spline-seam noise. Clamp the accumulated vertical error to +/-6 units so a bridge climb cannot leave the camera underground. Keep the XZ lerp at the existing 0.00003 (96 ms) so lateral stays tighter than vertical, which is the correct ordering.

findings.title: No camera corridor for trackside props — tall scenery slices through the near plane
findings.evidence: tmp/aaa-visual/baseline/comeback-city-p0_24.png: a pink lamp post plus its white globe head occupies x~280-430 for the full frame height, roughly a fifth of the screen, at a few units from the lens. The shipped camera has no collision or occlusion avoidance at all (the dead chaseCamera.js:195-257 applyCameraCollisionAvoidance is unused); the design comment at ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:6293-6295 claims 'the camera rides the road, so corners can never put it inside walls' — true for walls, but it says nothing about props passing the near plane. The prop exclusion test is `minCenterlineDistance(sampler, x, z) < roadWidth * 0.62` (lines 1041 and 1247); with Comeback City's roadWidth 50 that admits props 31 units from the centerline against a 25-unit road half-width, and the camera itself rides up to lane*0.6 = 14 units off centre, so a tall prop can pass within ~17 units of a camera that is only 10.5-12.7 units tall.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 authors a camera corridor: nothing tall enough to fill the lens is allowed inside the boom's swept volume, and anything that does intrude is faded. You never lose a fifth of the screen to a lamp post in MK8.
findings.fix: Two-part. (1) Widen the exclusion for tall props at mount time: in addMiamiTrackside (line 1230) and addPvTributeTrackside (line 1037), compute the prop's bounding-box height and use `const clearance = boxHeight > 8 ? roadWidth * 0.95 : roadWidth * 0.62;` before the minCenterlineDistance reject. (2) Reuse the near-band fade from the rival-occlusion finding for the small set of animated trackside props already tracked in the frame loop: fade any prop whose distance to engine.camera.position is under 16 units with a = smoothstep(7, 16, d). Prefer (1) — it is a build-time reject with zero per-frame cost; only add (2) if re-placing props moves the neon dusk silhouette the owner already signed off.

verdictVsMk8: Blind side-by-side this reads clearly worse than MK8, and the reason is structural rather than cosmetic: the shipped runtime is not a vehicle simulation, it is a rail slider. The kart has a scalar `race.speed`, a scalar `race.lane` in [-0.95, 0.95], and `race.progress` that advances at `speed / trackLength` with zero dependence on lane (ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:5642, rivalRacers.js:294) — so the racing line is worth literally nothing, no mass or lateral momentum exists anywhere in the sim, and the drift is drawn at 18-29 degrees of yaw while the trajectory only crabs 5-8 degrees. Every baseline frame shows the symptom: in comeback-city-p0_24 and penguin-village-p0_33 the kart is mid-bend and bolt-upright with zero roll, and the HUD speed reads 228-289 in 16 of the 18 captured samples, meaning corners cost essentially no speed. There is real depth layered on top — three drift tiers with sensible charge times, air tricks, a v-squared corner push, rivals with braking personalities and a corner governor — but it is bolted to a substrate that cannot express the MK8 loop of pick a line, manage entry speed, feel the weight shift. Fix the substrate (lane-dependent progress, lateral inertia, a grip-limited corner speed, real off-road) and the existing drift/trick/item layer immediately reads a class higher.

findings.title: Progress is lane-independent: the racing line does not exist
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:5642 `race.progress = wrap01(race.progress + (race.speed / engine.sampler.length) * dt)` and the identical rivalRacers.js:294. Lane never enters the distance integral. rivalRacers.js:238 computes `targetLane = clamp(kappaAhead * 90, -1, 1) * 0.55` — an apex-seeking racing line that is purely cosmetic because taking it gains zero progress. Visible in comeback-city-p0_45 and penguin-village-p0_33: both bends are 5 karts wide with a clear inside line that pays nothing.
findings.whyMk8Wins: The entire skill floor of MK8 is line choice. The inside of a corner is physically shorter, so apexing pays distance and running wide costs it, and every drift is a negotiation between angle, speed and arc length. Here the outside of a hairpin covers the same lap distance as the apex, so there is no reason to aim anywhere, no reason to defend the inside, and overtaking degenerates into a speed-number comparison. It also silently invalidates the rivals' racing-line AI.
findings.fix: In ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx replace line 5642 with a lane-aware arc-length integral. Immediately before it you already have `laneRate`, `cornerPush` and `trackCurvatureAt`. Add: `const laneScale = engine.sampler.widthAt(race.progress) * 0.44;` `const kappa = trackCurvatureAt(engine.sampler, race.progress);` `const arcScale = clamp(1 + kappa * race.lane * laneScale, 0.55, 1.45);` `const latWUps = (laneRate + cornerPush) * laneScale;` `const alongWUps = Math.sqrt(Math.max(0, race.speed*race.speed - latWUps*latWUps));` `race.progress = wrap01(race.progress + (alongWUps / (engine.sampler.length * arcScale)) * dt);`. The arcScale term makes the inside line shorter (a kappa=0.02 / R=50 bend at lane -0.7 gives arcScale 0.64, i.e. ~36% more progress per second); the sqrt term makes crabbing sideways cost forward distance so line changes are no longer free. Mirror all five lines into rivalRacers.js:294 by threading `laneScale` and the existing `curvatureAt` through the ctx object (both are already in ctx except laneScale, which is already passed at ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:5832's sibling call site). Tune the clamp floor so a well-driven corner is worth 0.1-0.2s.

findings.title: Drift is drawn at 3-4x its real slip angle — the kart slides visually but travels straight
findings.evidence: driftFeel.js:18-19 authors `slideAngleBase: 0.32` (18 deg) / `slideAngleMax: 0.5` (29 deg) as a free-floating visual. The actual trajectory: driftFeel.js:111 `driftLaneRate` returns at most 1.0 lane/s, multiplied by 1.15 at ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:5629, over a lane scale of width*0.44 ≈ 26.4 wu (sampler at :390, penguinVillage.js:33-36 widths 58-64). That is 30 wu/s lateral against 228 wu/s forward = 7.5 deg of real slip. Non-drift steering is worse: 0.72 lane/s = 19 wu/s = 4.8 deg.
findings.whyMk8Wins: In MK8 the yaw you see is the yaw you have. The kart is genuinely pointed off its velocity vector, which is why the drift reads as a controlled slide with real lateral commitment and why counter-steer visibly changes the arc. Here the model rotates 18-29 degrees while the path barely bends, so the drift reads as a decal spun onto a kart that is still driving straight — the single most 'this is fake' tell in the whole game.
findings.fix: Derive the drawn yaw from the trajectory instead of authoring it. In driftFeel.js `updateDriftFeel`, accept `latWUps` and `fwdWUps` in the options object and replace the `targetYaw` block (lines 94-100) with `const trueSlip = Math.atan2(latWUps, Math.max(1, fwdWUps)); const targetYaw = drift.active ? trueSlip * DRIFT_FEEL.yawExaggeration : 0;` and add `yawExaggeration: 1.6` to DRIFT_FEEL (MK8 over-rotates the model modestly, never 4x). Then raise the real authority to meet the drawn angle: change `driftLaneRate` (driftFeel.js:111) to `drift.direction * (1.40 + 0.90 * steerInDrift)` and drop the `* 1.15` at ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:5629. That gives 2.3 lane/s = 61 wu/s = 15 deg real slip at 228, drawn at 24 deg. Raise non-drift steering at ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:5629 from `race.steer * 0.72` to `race.steer * 1.25` (7.6 deg). Ship this with the lane-cost sqrt term from the racing-line fix, which self-limits the new authority by making aggressive crabbing bleed forward speed.

findings.title: Airborne kills both corner push and all lane control — ramps make corners free and hand the player ~8% of a lap with zero input
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:5626 `if (!airState.airborne) { ...laneRate... cornerPush... }` with an `else { race.wallContact = false; }` — while airborne the kart has no steering AND the centrifugal push is switched off entirely. Flight time from airTricks.js:7-13 (gravity 58, launchLift 0.105) at 228 wu/s is v0=23.9, t=2*23.9/58=0.82s normal and ~1.07s on the crest (`big: true`, x1.3), which at 228 wu/s is 190-245 world units. Lap length is roughly 2800 wu (3 laps at ~11s and ~250 avg), so a single crest launch is ~8% of a lap with the controls dead and the corner physics disabled.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 gives you full air steering plus a trick input, and gliders/jumps never suspend the track's demands — you can still line up your landing, and a badly aimed jump puts you in the dirt. Here the correct play is to hit the crest and let go of the stick; a ramp placed on a bend converts that bend into a free straight, which a player notices immediately as a bug ('why did my kart stop responding?') and an exploiter notices as the fastest line.
findings.fix: In ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:5626 stop gating on airborne and instead scale both terms: `const airAuthority = airState.airborne ? 0.35 : 1;` and `const carriedPush = airState.airborne ? cornerPush * 0.55 : cornerPush;` (you launched with lateral momentum, so you keep most of the outward carry), then use `laneRate * airAuthority` and `carriedPush` in the existing clamp. Keep `race.wallContact = false` while airborne but re-enable it the frame you land. Add a landing cost so aim matters: on `airEvents.landed` (line 5527), when `airEvents.trickTier === 0`, apply `race.speed *= 1 - 0.14 * Math.min(1, Math.abs(race.steer))`. Shorten the dead zone: airTricks.js:7 `gravity: 58 -> 72` and `launchLift: 0.105 -> 0.085`, giving ~0.54s normal / ~0.70s crest (~125-160 wu). Mirror the same airAuthority change into rivalRacers.js:265 so rivals do not gain the same free corner.
