findings.title: Wall contact is a hard clamp with no impulse, no rebound, no yaw and no shake — and a 70-speed floor makes wall-riding a viable line
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:5632-5637: `race.lane = clamp(..., -0.95, 0.95)` then `if (race.wallContact) race.speed = Math.max(70, race.speed - 200 * dt)`. That is the entire collision response. The kart does not bounce (lane stays pinned at the clamp), does not rotate, and `race.wallContact` (published to telemetry at :4751) drives no camera, VFX or audio reaction — a grep for shake/kickback/screenShake across the 6703-line monolith returns only the FOV lerp at :6331. Because the drain floors at 70 and cornerPushFor caps at 4 lane/s (105 wu/s, 5x the 19 wu/s steering authority), the correct play through the tightest bends is to pin the wall and coast the whole corner at 70.
findings.whyMk8Wins: An MK8 wall hit is one of the loudest feel events in the game: a lateral rebound that puts you back on the road facing wrong, a yaw snap, a hard speed cut, screen shake, a scrape sound and sparks. It punishes and it communicates. Here the kart silently sticks to an invisible line and slowly bleeds to a comfortable floor — it reads as the kart being glued to a rail, which is exactly what is happening.
findings.fix: Replace the wallContact block at ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:5633-5637 with a real impulse. Compute the closing rate: `const laneScale = engine.sampler.widthAt(race.progress) * 0.44; const impactWUps = Math.abs(laneRate + cornerPush) * laneScale;`. Then `race.speed = Math.max(52, race.speed - (110 + impactWUps * 1.9) * dt);` `race.lane -= Math.sign(race.lane) * clamp(impactWUps * 0.012, 0.15, 0.9) * dt;` (bounce off instead of sticking), `race.shake = Math.min(0.4, (race.shake || 0) + impactWUps * 0.0022);` and for a genuine slam add `race.wallHitCooldown = Math.max(0, race.wallHitCooldown - dt); if (impactWUps > 48 && race.wallHitCooldown <= 0) { race.spinTimer = 0.55; race.wallHitCooldown = 1.4; }`. Consume `race.shake` in the camera block at :6310 (see the camera finding). Emit scrape sparks by reusing the existing drift-spark emitter in raceParticles.js at the outboard wheel. Mirror the impulse into rivalRacers.js:266-269 so rivals stop wall-riding too.

findings.title: No off-road surface exists at all, and the invisible wall does not line up with any drawn track edge
findings.evidence: The only lateral consequence in the shipped runtime is the lane clamp at ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:5632. surfacePhysics.js — which defines a full ice/snow/slipZone/boost multiplier set — is never imported by ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx (its only consumer is racePlayerFrame.js:19, part of the dead ArcadeRace3D pipeline), so it is dead code. Worse, the geometry is misaligned: road width is 58-64 (penguinVillage.js:33-36) so the asphalt half-width is 29-32 wu, but lane 0.95 sits at `0.95 * W * 0.44` = 24.3-26.7 wu. The invisible wall is ~5 wu inside the asphalt edge, and the drawn curb (comebackCity.js:82, width 3.2) plus shoulder (comebackCity.js:84, width 6.2; penguinVillage shoulderWidth 6-7) are decorative and physically unreachable. comeback-city-p0_24 shows the red/white curb and the green verge beyond it — a player reads that curb as the limit and is stopped before it.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8's road edge is legible and graded: asphalt, then a rumble strip you can lean on, then dirt or grass that caps you at roughly half speed with dust and a rumble, then the wall or the fall. That gradient is where nearly all of MK8's risk-reward lives. Here there is exactly one boundary, it is invisible, it is inside the painted road, and stepping over it costs a bounded speed drain — no gradient, no legibility, no risk.
findings.fix: Zero-byte fix: make the already-drawn shoulder the off-road band. Raise the clamp at ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:5632 from ±0.95 to ±1.36 (`(W/2 + shoulderWidth) / (W * 0.44)` for W=58, shoulder=6) so the hard wall sits at the outer edge of the drawn shoulder, and add a soft band just inside it. Immediately after the clamp insert: `const offroad = Math.abs(race.lane) > 1.10 && !airState.airborne;` `if (offroad) { race.speed = Math.min(race.speed, MAX_SPEED * 0.55); race.speed = Math.max(0, race.speed - 55 * dt); race.rumble = 1; }`. Add `offroadLane` and `wallLane` to each TrackDefinition (comebackCity.js, penguinVillage.js) computed from `width` and `shoulderWidth` rather than hardcoding, and pass `wallLane` through to rivalRacers ctx (it is already a ctx field at ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:5832 — currently hardcoded 0.95). Drive dust from the existing raceParticles drift-spray emitter with a brown/white tint. Then delete or clearly mark kartPhysics.js, kartTuning.js and surfacePhysics.js as legacy-only so the next engineer does not tune dead numbers.

findings.title: The player has no corner speed limit while every rival does — braking and lifting are never required
findings.evidence: rivalRacers.js:220-228 gives each rival a genuine corner governor: `cornerCap = sqrt((authority * risk) / (kappaEff^0.7 * 0.00052))` evaluated with a personality-specific `brakeLookahead` (11-26 wu). The player has no equivalent anywhere in ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:5596-5640. The player's only cornering cost is `steeringDrag = Math.abs(race.steer) * (race.drift ? -8 : -22)` (line 5607) against `accel = 118` (line 5604) — at full lock the net is still +96 wu/s², so turning at maximum lock is free speed. The manifest bears this out: 16 of 18 captured samples read 228-289 including frames taken mid-bend (comeback-city-p0_24 at 285, penguin-village-p0_33 at 229 on a boost pad entering a left-hander).
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8's whole corner rhythm is slow-in / fast-out: you shed speed on entry (lift, brake-drift, or eat the understeer), then the mini-turbo pays it back on exit. Here entry speed is irrelevant — you arrive flat out, get shoved sideways, and either hold it or scrape. The player is playing a lane-dodging game while the AI is playing a racing game, which is why the rival personalities' braking characters (Purple Lab's 11-wu late-braking lookahead vs Blue Speed's 26) are invisible to the player.
findings.fix: Give the player the same governor, but as a grip-limited bleed rather than a hard cap so it reads as tyres letting go instead of a rev limiter. In ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx immediately after the `race.speed = clamp(...)` at line 5608 insert: `const kappaAhead = Math.abs(trackCurvatureAt(engine.sampler, race.progress + 24 / engine.sampler.length));` `const kappaEff = Math.max(Math.abs(trackCurvatureAt(engine.sampler, race.progress)), kappaAhead);` `const gripAuth = (race.drift ? 1.55 : 0.95) * (playerKart.stats.traction ?? 1);` `const gripCap = kappaEff > 4e-4 ? Math.sqrt(gripAuth / (Math.pow(kappaEff, 0.7) * 0.00052)) : Infinity;` `if (race.speed > gripCap) race.speed -= Math.min(240, (race.speed - gripCap) * 3.2) * dt;`. This uses the identical constants as cornerPushFor (ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:4626) so the two models agree. Pair it with the acceleration-curve fix so the speed you lose is genuinely expensive to regain, and it produces the MK8 loop for free: brake early, drift the apex, cash the mini-turbo on exit.

findings.title: No acceleration curve and a hard top-speed clamp — the kart hits a wall at 228 and mistakes cost almost nothing
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:5604 `const accel = throttle && !spinning ? 118 * playerKart.stats.accel : ...` — a single constant, integrated linearly at :5608 and hard-clamped at `MAX_SPEED = 228` (:173). 0 to 228 is 1.93s with a C1 discontinuity at the top: full thrust right up to the cap, then instantly nothing. Recovery costs are trivial as a result: a wall scrape floors you at 70 and costs 1.34s to undo; a spin-out floors at 46 (:5610) and costs 1.54s. Coast decel is -48 plus an extra -38 at :5609.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8's acceleration is heavily curved — the last 10-15% of top speed takes as long as the first 70% — which is what makes losing speed hurt, makes slipstream and mini-turbos feel like real gifts, and makes the top-speed stat meaningful. It also means the speed needle is always moving, which feeds the camera and audio. Here the speedometer is pinned at the cap almost the entire race (16/18 captured samples), so nothing downstream of speed — FOV, engine pitch, motion lines — has any dynamic range to work with.
findings.fix: Replace the constant at ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:5604 with an asymptotic curve and delete the hard clamp's role as the primary limiter. Use `const vRatio = clamp(race.speed / maxSpeed, 0, 1.2); const accel = throttle && !spinning ? 195 * playerKart.stats.accel * Math.max(0.04, 1 - Math.pow(vRatio, 2.2)) : spinning ? -150 : -48;`. At v=0 that is 195 (punchier launch than today), at 0.8*max it is 76, at 0.95*max it is 21 — reaching ~95% of cap in ~2.5s with no corner in the curve, and the existing `clamp(..., 0, maxSpeed)` at :5608 becomes a safety net rather than the shape. Keep the boost path punchy by exempting it: when `driftState.miniTurboTimer > 0 || race.boostTimer > 0` skip the taper (use the flat 195 + the existing `miniTurboAccel = 150`) so mini-turbos still spike hard past cruise. Apply the same curve to rivalRacers.js:233 (`rival.speed + 112 * dt`) so the field's acceleration character matches.

findings.title: Steering rate is speed-independent and lateral velocity is assigned, not integrated — the kart has no mass
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:5628-5632: `laneRate = (race.drift ? driftLaneRate(...) * 1.15 : race.steer * 0.72) * steerAuthority * playerKart.stats.handling` then `race.lane = clamp(race.lane + (laneRate + cornerPush) * dt, ...)`. laneRate is a velocity written directly from input every frame, with no lateral state and no mass term — the only smoothing anywhere is on the input itself (`race.steer = lerp(race.steer, targetSteer, 1 - Math.pow(0.001, dt))` at :5474, tau ≈ 0.145s). Notably the rivals DO carry lateral state (`rival.laneVel`, rivalRacers.js:264) — the player is the only racer without it. Because the rate is constant, at speed 20 you cross the track exactly as fast as at 228.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 karts have weight you can feel: the chassis takes time to load up into a turn and time to unload out of it, heavier karts resist direction changes and shrug off bumps, and steering authority is speed-scaled so the kart is calm in the pits and precise at pace. Here the kart snaps to a lateral velocity instantly and stops instantly, which is why every frame shows a dead-flat chassis with no load — it reads as a cursor being dragged, not a vehicle.
findings.fix: Give the player the lateral state the rivals already have. In ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx add `laneVel: 0` to the race state object (near `lane: 0` at :296) and rewrite :5628-5632 as: `const steerRate = 1.45 * clamp(0.42 + 0.58 * (race.speed / MAX_SPEED), 0.42, 1);` `const targetLaneVel = (race.drift ? driftLaneRate(driftState, race.steer) : race.steer * steerRate) * steerAuthority * playerKart.stats.handling;` `const loadRate = (race.drift ? 7 : 12) / (playerKart.stats.weight ?? 1);` `race.laneVel += (targetLaneVel - race.laneVel) * (1 - Math.pow(Math.E, -loadRate * dt));` `race.lane = clamp(race.lane + (race.laneVel + cornerPush) * dt, -wallLane, wallLane);`. loadRate 12 gives ~83ms to load a turn on a light kart and ~110ms on a heavy one — enough to feel, not enough to feel laggy. Then reduce the input lerp at :5474 from `0.001` to `0.02` (tau ~0.085s) since the chassis now supplies the smoothing and doubling up makes the controls mushy. Feed `race.laneVel` into the chassis-roll fix so the body loads with the turn.

findings.title: Drifting is strictly dominant: less drag than steering, and a free tier-3 mini-turbo on any 2.2s straight
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:5607 `steeringDrag = Math.abs(race.steer) * (race.drift ? -8 : -22)` — drifting is literally 2.75x less draggy than steering, so a drifting kart is faster in a straight line than a steering one. Combined with driftFeel.js:111 `driftLaneRate`, a counter-steered drift (steerInDrift = -1) yields `0.54 - 0.46 = 0.08` lane/s x 1.15 = 2.4 wu/s lateral: over the full 2.15s tier-3 charge (driftFeel.js:20) the kart wanders 5 wu on a 50-wu-wide track. There is no speed cost, no top-speed cost, and no lane cost to banking a UMT on every straight, and driftFeel.js:83 charges purely on held-time with no steer requirement after the initial commit.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 lets you charge on straights too, but it costs you: the kart is genuinely angled off the velocity vector so you travel further and you cannot use the full width of the road for line or defence. Here the only cost is a 5-wu wander, and the drag term actively rewards the exploit. That collapses the whole drift/no-drift decision into 'always be drifting', which flattens the skill curve MK8 builds its 200cc metagame on.
findings.fix: Two changes, both one-liners. First invert the drag relationship at ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:5607: `const steeringDrag = race.drift ? -(26 + Math.abs(race.steer) * 10) : Math.abs(race.steer) * -22;` — a drift now costs a flat 26 wu/s² plus steering, so it is only worth it when the mini-turbo payback (DRIFT_FEEL.boostKick 26/40/56 plus miniTurboAccel 150 for 0.5/0.9/1.4s) exceeds the drag, which happens for tier 2 and 3 but not for tier-1 spam. Second, require the drift to actually be turning to charge: in driftFeel.js:83 replace `drift.charge = Math.min(drift.charge + dt, ...)` with `const chargeGain = 0.35 + 0.65 * Math.max(0, steer * drift.direction); drift.charge = Math.min(drift.charge + dt * chargeGain, DRIFT_FEEL.chargeTimes[2] + 0.6);` — a hard counter-steered straight-line drift now charges at 0.35x (6.1s to UMT, longer than any straight on either track) while a committed corner drift charges at full rate or better. Do NOT touch chargeTimes; they are already well matched to MK8's ~0.55/1.3/2.15s.

findings.title: Kart classes are three near-identical scalars with no weight axis — the choice cannot matter
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:212-223: seven karts spanning accel 0.96-1.04, handling 0.95-1.04, topSpeed 0.985-1.02. The comment at :203-211 explains why they were squeezed to ±2%: at ±3% kart choice alone decided the ~34s race. There is no weight, traction, mini-turbo or off-road stat, and KART_CONTACT (rivalRacers.js:84-112) applies a symmetric `bumpLanePush: 0.12` and a symmetric `spinSpeedDiff: 85` regardless of who hit whom — a heavyweight and a featherweight bump identically.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8 gets a wide, legible class fantasy out of stats that mostly do NOT touch top speed: weight decides who wins a shoulder-to-shoulder bump and who gets shoved off line, mini-turbo decides how fast you bank a UMT, traction decides how you behave on ice and grass, handling decides drift radius. That is why Bowser and Baby Peach feel like different games without either being flatly faster. Here the only differentiating axis is raw pace, which is precisely the axis that decides a short race — so the owner correctly compressed it to the point of irrelevance.
findings.fix: Add two stats to every entry in KART_OPTIONS (ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:212-223): `weight` in 0.85-1.20 and `miniTurbo` in 0.90-1.12, keeping topSpeed at ±2%. Wire them where the top-speed stat is NOT involved: (1) chassis load — use `weight` as the divisor in the `loadRate` term from the lateral-inertia fix; (2) contact — in rivalRacers.js:869-922-equivalent player bump application at ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:5836-5839, scale `playerBump.lanePush` by `rivalWeight / (playerWeight + rivalWeight) * 2` and gate the rear-hit spin on `KART_CONTACT.spinSpeedDiff * (playerWeight / rivalWeight)`; (3) drift charge — multiply the `chargeGain` term in driftFeel.js:83 by the kart's `miniTurbo`; (4) traction — feed `traction` into the `gripAuth` term of the player corner governor. Net effect: Cold Storage becomes an unshovable heavyweight with a lazy chassis and a slow UMT, Miami Cruiser a quick-charging light kart that loses every bump, and neither is flatly faster over a lap — which is exactly what makes the roster survive short races.

findings.title: 34-second, 3-lap race with ~11s laps leaves no room for a race arc
findings.evidence: comebackCity.js:24 `laps: COMEBACK_CITY_COURSE_V2.laps || 3` and penguinVillage.js:63 `laps: 3`. At the observed ~250 avg speed over ~2800 wu the lap is ~11s. RUBBER_BAND (rivalRacers.js:68-74) uses absolute-second thresholds — aheadMaxSeconds 3, behindMaxSeconds 4 — which on an 11s lap are 27% and 36% of a lap, so the band is essentially always engaged and the field is glued together by construction. The kart-stat comment at ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:203-211 documents the downstream damage: 'the race is so short' forced the stat spread down to ±2%.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8's 2-3 minute race is a structure: lap 1 establishes the pack, lap 2 is item warfare and position churn, lap 3 is the final-lap music change and the earned or stolen win. It also gives the tuning room to breathe — kart classes, rubber banding and item distribution all need enough race for variance to average out. At 34 seconds nothing can be tuned without deciding the whole race, which is why every other system here has been compressed toward flatness.
findings.fix: Immediate zero-byte step: raise `laps` to 5 on both tracks (comebackCity.js:24, penguinVillage.js:63), which with the corner governor and acceleration-curve fixes lands around 65-75s. Retune the rubber band to lap-relative rather than absolute: in rivalRacers.js:68-74 make aheadMaxSeconds/behindMaxSeconds a fraction of lap time by computing `const lapSeconds = trackLength / Math.max(60, maxSpeed);` at the top of updateRivalRacers and using `0.28 * lapSeconds` / `0.36 * lapSeconds`, which preserves today's feel at 3 laps and stays correct as tracks lengthen. Then reopen the kart spread the owner's own note at ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:209-211 flags as a V2 action (pre-rebalance values are in git at 511dc12b) — but reopen it on the weight/miniTurbo axes, not topSpeed. Longer term the real answer is a second sector per track rather than more laps, since 5 laps of an 11s loop reads repetitive; that is track-authoring work, not physics.

findings.title: Zero screen shake anywhere, a rail-mounted camera that never swings on a drift, and 7 degrees of FOV range that is pinned in practice
findings.evidence: A grep for shake/kickback/screenShake across the whole 6703-line runtime returns nothing but the FOV lerp at ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:6331 — no wall hit, no landing, no spin-out, no item hit produces any camera reaction. The camera position is sampled off the centreline, not off the kart: :6310 `engine.sampler.pointAt(cameraProgress, race.lane * 0.6)` and :6321 `lookAt(playerSample.point + tangent * 30)`, so during a drift the camera stays exactly square to the track tangent while the kart yaws in front of it. FOV at :6326-6329 is `70 + clamp(speed / MAX_SPEED, 0, 1.15) * 7 + (miniTurboActive ? 3.5 : 0)` — and since the manifest shows speed pinned at 228-289 for 16 of 18 samples, that term is a static ~77 all race.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8's camera is a feel instrument: it lags the kart into a drift and swings out so the slide is framed from the outside, it punches FOV and adds a lens kick the frame a mini-turbo fires, and it shakes on every wall, landing and shell. That is where a large share of MK8's 'weight' actually lives — the vehicle is stylized, the camera sells the physics. Here the camera is a dolly on rails that reports the track, not the kart.
findings.fix: Three changes in ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx. (1) Add `shake: 0` to the race state (near :318) and decay it each frame `race.shake = Math.max(0, race.shake - 4 * dt)`, raising it from the wall-impact term (see the wall finding), landing (`airEvents.landed` at :5527: `race.shake += airState.big ? 0.28 : 0.16`), spin start (:5670: `+= 0.3`) and mini-turbo release (:5492: `+= 0.10`). Consume it at :6311 before the lerp: `desiredCamera.x += (Math.sin(race.raceTime*61) + Math.sin(race.raceTime*97)) * race.shake * 1.4; desiredCamera.y += Math.sin(race.raceTime*83) * race.shake * 0.9;`. (2) Make the camera trail the slide: at :6310 change the lane argument to `race.lane * 0.6 + driftState.slideYaw * 0.5` and at :6321 add a lateral offset to the lookAt point of `playerSample.normal * driftState.slideYaw * 9` so the camera frames the kart from outside the drift. (3) Make FOV respond to change, not level: track `race.speedSmoothed = lerp(race.speedSmoothed, race.speed, 1 - Math.pow(0.05, dt))` and replace the :6328 term with `+ clamp((race.speed - race.speedSmoothed) * 0.9, -3, 9) + (miniTurboActive ? 6 : 0)`, which gives a visible punch on every boost and a squeeze on every scrape instead of a static 77. All three are pure math on existing state — no new draw calls, no bytes.

verdictVsMk8: Blind side-by-side this loses to MK8DX on sheer image integrity, and for a reason that is not a budget constraint — it is a hardcoded constant. At a 1600x900 CSS canvas the game hands the GPU a 1360x765 drawing buffer (I measured `canvas.width/height` live) and lets the browser bilinear-upscale it, so comeback-city-p0_45's neon curb stripes stairstep, penguin-village-p0_9's "THE ICE IS NICE" sign is illegible mush, and every silhouette edge crawls; MK8DX renders native 1080p docked and never shows that. Meanwhile the machine is idle: I measured 1.0-4.9 ms of CPU work per frame and a hard 144 Hz vsync cap at the shipped scale, and I proved native 1.0 lands at 11.1-14.1 ms against a 16.67 ms 60 fps budget. Structurally there is almost no runtime performance architecture — 541 (Comeback City) / 853 (Penguin Village) individual non-instanced meshes, 411 / 570 unique materials, exactly 3 InstancedMeshes in the whole scene (all of them particles), zero LOD, zero distance culling, and no adaptive-resolution controller — so the game cannot trade quality for frame time anywhere; it can only ship the cut permanently.

findings.title: Phones never receive the mobile render scale — the `mobile` flag is an aspect test and the race is force-landscape
findings.evidence: src/game/race/render/createRaceScene.js:74 `raceViewport.mobile = raceViewport.width / raceViewport.height < 0.74;`. That is a PORTRAIT test, not a device test. The K3 soft lock makes the race ALWAYS landscape on phones, so aspect is ~2.1, `mobile` resolves false, and line 76 picks `scaleTable.desktop` (0.85). I verified this live: a Playwright context at 844x620 CSS produced a 1434x1054 drawing buffer — dpr 1.70 (= rawDpr 2 x 0.85), not the intended 1.20 (= 2 x 0.6). That is 2.0x the pixel count the mobile budget assumes. With 6x CPU throttling the same run measured 25.2-27.2 ms frame elapsed (37-40 fps) with p95 spikes to 58.8-63.3 ms.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8DX handheld mode has one deliberate, tested resolution target and holds 60 fps at it. Here the phone path silently inherits the desktop target, so the one platform with the least GPU is asked to draw the most pixels, and the tuning constant that was supposed to protect it is dead code. A player on a phone sees sub-40 fps with 60 ms hitches — that is a bug, not a tradeoff.
findings.fix: In `src/game/race/render/createRaceScene.js` replace the aspect heuristic with a real device signal plus a runtime probe. (1) Add a `deviceClass` param to `fitRaceRendererToCanvas` sourced from the same `touchControls` boolean the monolith already computes and already passes correctly to `createRaceParticles` (ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:5049) — that is the authoritative phone signal in this codebase. (2) Keep `raceViewport.mobile` for the camera-tier fallbacks (used at :6288/6291/6305/6308/6322/6323/6327) but rename the render-scale input to `raceViewport.deviceClass` so the two concerns stop sharing one wrong boolean. (3) Set the phone base scale to 0.85 (not 0.6) and let the adaptive controller from the next finding own the rest — 0.6 was never actually validated because it never ran. (4) Add a dev assertion in the resize handler that logs `{deviceClass, renderScale, dpr, buffer}` once per race so this class of drift is caught by the capture harness.

findings.title: Fixed 0.85 render scale ships a permanently soft image, and there is no adaptive-resolution controller anywhere
findings.evidence: src/game/race/render/createRaceScene.js:14-17 hardcodes `RACE_RENDER_SCALE = {desktop: 0.85, mobile: 0.6}`; line 77 `const dpr = Math.max(0.355, rawDpr * renderScale)`. `setPixelRatio` is called exactly twice in the whole runtime (createRaceScene.js:86 and ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:5144) — both inside resize handlers. Nothing reads frame time to adjust it. My resolution sweep on the shipped build: 0.85 = 9.68/10.13 ms (CC/PV), 1.00 = 14.13/11.10 ms, 1.41 supersample = 22.95/15.09 ms, 1.00 with 4x CPU throttle = 13.58/13.66 ms. Native 1.00 therefore sits inside the 16.67 ms 60 fps budget with 2.5-5.5 ms of headroom even on a throttled CPU. Separately, the pmndrs SMAA pass runs at the 1360x765 buffer resolution, so it smooths the low-res image and the bilinear upscale then re-softens it — the worst of both.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8DX picks native and holds it; its edge treatment operates on the final pixel grid, so thin high-contrast geometry (curb stripes, kart silhouettes, sign lettering) stays crisp at speed. Here every thin element is resolved at 72% linear resolution and then stretched, which is exactly the content this art direction is made of — neon lines on dark asphalt. The frames prove it: CC p0_45's lane stripes and PV p0_9's sign are the two worst offenders.
findings.fix: Add `src/game/race/render/adaptiveResolution.js` exporting `createResolutionController({ targetMs = 16.67, ladder = [1.0, 0.9, 0.8, 0.7, 0.6, 0.5], start })`. Contract: `update(frameElapsedEmaMs) -> newScaleOrNull`. Downshift one rung when the EMA exceeds `targetMs * 1.08` (18.0 ms) for 45 consecutive frames; upshift one rung when it stays under `targetMs * 0.81` (13.5 ms) for 180 consecutive frames. The 4.5 ms hysteresis gap plus asymmetric dwell (0.75 s down / 3 s up) prevents oscillation. Hard-lock the scale during the countdown and for 90 frames after any resize/orientationchange, and allow at most one rung per 1.5 s. Feed it the EMA the frame loop already computes — `rollingAverage(frameElapsedSamples)` at ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:6357 (40-sample window, already there). On a rung change, call the EXACT existing resize path (`fitRaceRendererToCanvas` then the pmndrs branch at :5131-5141) with the new scale so `renderer.setPixelRatio` and `composer.setSize(viewport.width, viewport.height, false)` stay in lockstep — desyncing those two is how the composer targets end up at a different resolution than the canvas. Start rung: 1.0 on desktop, 0.85 on phones. Change `RACE_RENDER_SCALE` to `RACE_RENDER_SCALE_START` so no caller mistakes it for a ceiling.

findings.title: Zero scenery instancing or geometry merging: 541 / 853 individual meshes with 411 / 570 unique materials
findings.evidence: I walked the live scene graph. Comeback City: 544 renderables, 541 non-instanced, 3 InstancedMeshes totalling 96 instances, 411 unique materials, 407 unique geometries, 703k triangles. Penguin Village: 856 renderables, 853 non-instanced, the same 3 InstancedMeshes, 570 unique materials, 750 unique geometries, 502k triangles. The 3 InstancedMeshes are the particle systems (raceParticles.js:62/131/200) — the `createInstancedMesh` helper in createRaceScenery.js:89 is on the `trackVisualsEnabled` path, which defaults false (ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3839), so ZERO scenery instancing runs in the shipped config. The materials are unique because they are constructed per call, e.g. `buildCheckerRibbon` at :1741 does `new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({...})` on every invocation. Real GL draw calls after frustum culling measured 85-353 (CC) and 159-474 (PV). At 6x CPU throttle frame work was 19.6-22.0 ms — mobile is CPU-bound, not fill-bound, and 853 objects x per-frame matrix + frustum-sphere + render-list-sort with 570 distinct material states is where that CPU goes.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8DX budgets a few hundred draw calls per frame on far weaker hardware precisely because everything repeated is batched. Here nothing is. This is the finding that BUYS the budget for every other pillar: until the object and material counts collapse, adding lights, decals, reflections or denser trackside dressing directly costs frames on phones.
findings.fix: Add `src/game/race/render/staticBatcher.js` with two stages. Stage 1 (instancing): `queueStatic({ geometry, material, matrix })` keyed on `geometry.uuid + '|' + materialKey(material)` where `materialKey` hashes `{type, color.getHex(), map?.uuid, transparent, opacity, side, vertexColors, flatShading, depthWrite}`; `flush(parent)` emits an `InstancedMesh` when count > 1 and a plain `Mesh` when count === 1. Stage 2 (merging): for objects that share a MATERIAL but not a geometry (the ribbons, curbs, district facades), bake each into world space and run `mergeGeometries` — already imported at ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:5 — but chunk by centerline progress into 16 arcs so each merged mesh keeps a tight bounding sphere and stays frustum-cullable (one giant merge would defeat culling entirely). Stage 3 (material dedupe): add a module-level `materialCache = new Map()` and a `sharedMaterial(spec)` accessor keyed by the same hash; replace the per-call constructors at :1660, :1685, :1744, :2305, :2315 and inside the district/prop loops. Target: CC 541 -> 60-90 objects, PV 853 -> 90-120, unique materials -> under 40 per track, median GL draw calls -> 60-90. Validate with the same scene-graph walk (`scene.traverse` counting `isInstancedMesh` / material uuids) plus the capture harness.

findings.title: No LOD and no distance culling — 12k-23k-triangle Tripo props drawn at full density, camera.far 1800 against fog.far 820
findings.evidence: Grepping `LOD` / `distanceTo` across ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx and src/game/race/render/ returns no distance-based visibility logic at all. My scene walk's triangle ranking is dominated by imported props: `tripo_node_8032b6ec` 23,172 tris, `tripo_node_b3e08611` 22,000 tris x2, `tripo_node_7e86adca` 21,999, `tripo_node_06715a4b` 21,540 x3 (64,620 tris for one prop type), `Mesh_0` 20,920, `tripo_node_ab30d3b3` 14,868 x2. These are static background dressing at 20k+ triangles each, at full detail regardless of distance. Meanwhile ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3869 sets `fog.far = 820` and :3934 pushes `camera.far = 1800` — everything between 820 and 1800 renders as 100% solid fog colour yet still costs a full draw. Camera near is 0.25 (:3870), giving a 7200:1 near/far ratio and correspondingly poor depth precision for road decals.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8DX props are authored in the low hundreds of triangles and swap to impostors at distance; nothing is ever submitted that resolves to a flat fog colour. Here a prop that occupies 30 pixels on screen can cost 21,540 triangles and its own draw call.
findings.fix: Three changes, all zero-byte. (1) Distance cull: at scene-build time push every static object into a `cullList` of `{object, center: Vector3, radius: Number}` (from `geometry.boundingSphere` transformed to world). Per frame test `center.distanceToSquared(camera.position) > (820 + radius) ** 2` -> `object.visible = false`. That is one branch and no sqrt per object, and it short-circuits before three's own frustum-sphere test. (2) LOD: wrap each 12k+ prop in `THREE.LOD` with the full mesh at distance 0 and a 2-triangle camera-facing billboard impostor beyond 260 units; generate the impostor texture at build time by rendering the prop once to a 128x128 RenderTarget on first mount (procedural, adds no shipped bytes). For the props duplicated 2-3x, route the duplicates through the staticBatcher so they become one InstancedMesh. (3) Depth: raise `camera.near` from 0.25 to 0.6 (nothing is within 0.6 units — the kart is ~2 units long and the chase camera sits 33-43 units back, see :6305) and drop `camera.far` from 1800 to 1100 (the far backdrop ring is radius 780 at world origin plus roughly 250 units of track half-extent). That is a free ~2.4x depth-precision gain for road decals and skid marks.

findings.title: 309 / 329 objects run MeshStandardMaterial with no envMap, no normal maps and near-zero metalness — full PBR cost for a toon look
findings.evidence: Scene walk material histogram — Comeback City: MeshStandardMaterial 309, MeshBasicMaterial 128, MeshToonMaterial 35, SpriteMaterial 69. Penguin Village: MeshToonMaterial 358, MeshStandardMaterial 329, MeshBasicMaterial 107, SpriteMaterial 58. Only 7 `new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial` constructors exist (createKartModel.js:10, createTrackMesh.js:8, ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:1661/1685/1744/2305/2315) and their inputs are `metalness` 0-0.45 and `roughness` 0.22-0.92 with no `envMap` and no `normalMap` anywhere in the runtime. With no environment map the Cook-Torrance specular lobe has nothing to reflect, so the entire PBR BRDF is being evaluated per fragment to produce what a Lambert term would produce.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8DX is stylized and spends its fragment budget on things you can see — rim light, ramp shading, bloom. Spending it on a physically based BRDF with an empty environment is pure waste, and it is the single largest per-pixel cost on the mobile GPU, which is exactly the platform that cannot afford it.
findings.fix: Swap by role, not wholesale. Road and ground (createTrackMesh.js:8, ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:1685) -> `MeshLambertMaterial` keeping `map` and `color`; the diffuse result is visually identical at metalness 0-0.06. Ribbons and curbs (:1744) -> `MeshLambertMaterial` with `vertexColors: true, flatShading: true`. Kart bodies (createKartModel.js:10/33, :2305/2315) keep a specular highlight, so use `MeshPhongMaterial` with `shininess = (1 - roughness) * 100` and `specular` derived from the old metalness — that preserves the read at roughly a third of the fragment cost. Do this AFTER the staticBatcher material dedupe so you are editing ~40 shared materials rather than 570 clones. Verify no regression by re-running `node scripts/aaa-visual-capture.mjs --label mat-swap` and diffing against baseline with scripts/compare-race-visuals.mjs.

findings.title: MSAA is off and `antialias: true` is dead cost — SMAA MEDIUM is doing the job worse and on a low-res buffer
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3985 constructs `new PmndrsEffectComposer(renderer, { frameBufferType: THREE.HalfFloatType })`. postprocessing 6.39.2 defaults `multisampling = 0` (node_modules/postprocessing/build/index.js:917-927), so the composer's render target has `samples = 0` and there is no MSAA at all. Meanwhile createRaceScene.js:3-8 requests `antialias: true` on the WebGLRenderer, which allocates a multisampled DEFAULT framebuffer that the composer never renders geometry into — the final pass is a fullscreen triangle, so those samples buy nothing. SMAA MEDIUM (:4007) then runs as a post filter on the 1360x765 buffer. I A/B'd it with a temporary `multisampling` hook: at native 1.00, `MSAA4 + no SMAA` = 12.57 ms (CC) / 12.49 ms (PV) versus `SMAA only` = 14.13 ms / 11.10 ms — cost-neutral within noise, and MSAA resolves true geometric edges instead of guessing them from a blurred colour buffer.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8DX's edges on high-contrast silhouettes — kart bodywork against sky, curb stripes against asphalt — are stable under motion. SMAA on an upscaled buffer produces the crawling you can see on the skyline towers in comeback-city-p0_15 and the iceberg ridgeline in penguin-village-p0_24, because the edge it is trying to reconstruct was already destroyed by the render-scale cut.
findings.fix: Change ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3985 to `new PmndrsEffectComposer(renderer, { frameBufferType: THREE.HalfFloatType, multisampling: deviceClass === 'phone' ? 0 : 4 })`. Gate the SMAA push at :4007 on `wantSmaa && composer.multisampling === 0`, so phones (where MSAA is expensive on tilers) keep SMAA and desktop gets true 4x MSAA. Set `antialias: false` in `RACE_RENDERER_OPTIONS` (createRaceScene.js:4) — it is unreachable under the composer and only wastes a multisampled default framebuffer. Add a `?zzMsaa=` style debug override to the existing `postParams` block so the capture harness can A/B it. Expose `multisampling` to the adaptive controller as the FIRST thing it drops (4 -> 2 -> 0) before it ever touches render scale, so resolution is the last quality lever surrendered, not the first.

findings.title: A full 384x384 BasicShadowMap pass runs every frame and produces an unreadable grey blob
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3859 `renderer.shadowMap.enabled = !trackVisualsEnabled` (so ON by default, since trackVisualsEnabled defaults false at :3839), :3860 `shadowMap.type = THREE.BasicShadowMap` (no PCF), :3885 `sun.shadow.mapSize.set(384, 384)` over an ortho frustum of +/-64 units (:3886-3889). That is 128 world units across 384 texels = 0.33 units per texel, roughly one sixth of a kart length per shadow texel. You can see the result in penguin-village-p0_24 and comeback-city-p0_9: the shadow under the player kart is a vague dark ellipse with no relationship to the kart silhouette. This costs a complete extra scene traversal and depth-only draw of every castShadow object per frame.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8DX's kart shadow is a tight, soft, correctly-shaped contact shadow that sells the kart's contact with the road and reads clearly during drifts and jumps. Here the pass costs real frame time and delivers a blob that a single decal quad would render better and for free.
findings.fix: Pick one and commit. Preferred: tighten and sharpen — set `shadowMap.type = THREE.PCFSoftShadowMap`, `sun.shadow.mapSize.set(1024, 1024)`, and shrink the ortho frustum from +/-64 to +/-26 (left/right/top/bottom at :3886-3889), which the sun already supports because it rides with the player (:6333-6335). That yields 0.05 units per texel — a 6.5x sharpening — for the same one extra pass. Also set `shadow.camera.near = 40 / far = 200` (currently 20/420) to tighten depth range, and `shadow.bias = -0.0004` to match the finer texel. On phones, set `renderer.shadowMap.enabled = false` and enable the existing blob-decal path instead — a shadow pass is the wrong spend on a device already CPU-bound at 22 ms. Wire the enable/disable through the adaptive controller as quality rung 2 (after MSAA, before render scale).

findings.title: The post chain costs ~2.5-3.5 ms and 11 extra framebuffer binds, with no resolution-aware bloom
findings.evidence: I counted framebuffer binds per frame via a GL hook: the pmndrs chain (`?post=1`, shipped) issues 28 `bindFramebuffer` calls per frame versus 17 for the legacy chain. On Penguin Village the pmndrs chain measured 9.40-11.29 ms frame elapsed versus 6.95-7.99 ms for the legacy chain at the same 1360x765 buffer — a ~2.5-3.5 ms delta, which is 15-21% of the entire 60 fps budget. `BloomEffect` at ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3993-4004 is constructed with `mipmapBlur: true` but no `resolutionScale`, so the first downsample rung runs at full buffer resolution. SMAA MEDIUM adds two more passes plus two lookup textures.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8's glow is generous but it is a fixed, cheap, low-resolution effect — the budget goes into the scene. Here roughly a fifth of the frame is post, which is precisely the budget the other pillars need for lights, decals and denser dressing.
findings.fix: Three cuts in the `if (postChainEnabled)` block at ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3980-4012. (1) Add `resolutionScale: 0.5` to the `BloomEffect` options — mipmap bloom is resolution-independent by design (the existing comment at :3996-4002 says exactly that), so halving the input costs nothing visually and removes the most expensive rung. Re-check `radius: 0.7` after, it may need to come down to ~0.55. (2) Drop SMAA in favour of composer MSAA per the previous finding — that removes 2 passes and 2 texture binds. (3) `VignetteEffect` and `ToneMappingEffect` are already merged into the single `EffectPass` at :4011 — keep that, and make sure any future LUT3DEffect joins the SAME EffectPass rather than adding a pass. Expected: 28 binds -> ~19, and 1.5-2.0 ms returned. Measure with the same GL `bindFramebuffer` hook (patch `WebGL2RenderingContext.prototype` from a Playwright `addInitScript`) so the number is auditable rather than asserted.

findings.title: Production ships a 60-key telemetry object allocated every frame plus a full 856-object scene traverse every 750 ms
findings.evidence: `publishTelemetry` (ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:4685-4760) is called unconditionally from the frame loop at :6350 with no DEV or query-param gate. Every frame it builds a fresh ~60-key object literal including `rivalPositions: rivalPositionsOf(...)` (a fresh array of objects) and ~10 `Number(x.toFixed(n))` round-trips, each of which allocates a string. Separately `rendererStatsForFrame` (:5414-5420) calls `estimateSceneRenderStats` (:4576) every 750 ms, which does a full `world.traverse` over 544 / 856 objects while allocating a `Set` of geometry uuid strings. Neither is gated. My phone-class run showed dtMed 23-25 ms against p95 spikes of 58.8-63.3 ms — a hitch profile consistent with periodic GC plus the 750 ms traverse.
findings.whyMk8Wins: MK8DX has no debug instrumentation in the shipping build. Steady-state frame time matters less than the absence of hitches, and allocation-driven GC pauses are exactly the kind of hitch a player feels as a stutter mid-drift.
findings.fix: Gate both behind a single `const telemetryEnabled = import.meta.env.DEV || navigator.webdriver || new URLSearchParams(location.search).has('telemetry')` resolved once outside the frame loop — `navigator.webdriver` keeps every existing capture and proof script working unchanged. When disabled, skip `publishTelemetry` and `rendererStatsForFrame` entirely. When enabled, mutate one pre-allocated module-level object in place instead of allocating a literal, drop the `toFixed` round-trips (store raw numbers; format at the read site), and reuse a persistent array for `rivalPositions`. Throttle the whole publish to every 250 ms rather than every frame — no consumer of `window.__comebackCityKartTelemetry` polls faster than that.

findings.title: Snowfall runs a 220-flake JS loop with a full vertex-buffer re-upload every frame
findings.evidence: ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:3787 `const flakeCount = 220`; the frame loop at :6262-6283 iterates all 220 flakes doing a `Math.sin` plus four wrap comparisons each, writes back into the position array, and sets `snowPositions.needsUpdate = true` — re-uploading the entire 2640-byte position buffer to the GPU every frame. This is on Penguin Village, the track that already measured worse (frame work 3.21-4.86 ms desktop, 22.0 ms at 6x CPU throttle). It is also inconsistent with the rest of the codebase, which correctly does ambient sway on the GPU via the shared `AMBIENT_SWAY_TIME` uniform (toonRimShader.js:78/108) with matrices frozen.
findings.whyMk8Wins: Not a visual gap — the snow reads fine in penguin-village-p0_24 and p0_9. It is a budget gap: this is CPU spent on something the vertex shader does for free, on the platform that is CPU-bound.
findings.fix: Add `src/game/race/render/createSnowfall.js`. Upload `position`, plus `aSpeed` and `aPhase` as static `Float32BufferAttribute`s ONCE (the values already exist as the `speeds` and `phases` arrays at :3789-3790). Replace `PointsMaterial` with a `ShaderMaterial` whose vertex shader does the fall and the wrap: `float y = mod(position.y - uTime * aSpeed, uSpanY) + 0.4;` and `vec2 xz = uAnchor.xz + mod(position.xz - uAnchor.xz + uSpanXZ, 2.0 * uSpanXZ) - uSpanXZ;` with `x += sin(uTime * 0.9 + aPhase) * 1.6`. Set `gl_PointSize = 1.15 * uScale / -mvPosition.z` to reproduce the current `sizeAttenuation`. Uniforms per frame: `uTime` (reuse `AMBIENT_SWAY_TIME`) and `uAnchor` (the player sample point) — two uniform writes replacing 220 iterations and a VBO upload. Keep the existing `frustumCulled = false` and the `reducedMotion` visibility toggle at :6259-6260.

findings.title: Particle and coin InstancedMeshes submit their full allocated count with frustumCulled disabled
findings.evidence: raceParticles.js:77, :131, :200 and ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:4135 all set `frustumCulled = false`, and none of them adjust `mesh.count` to the number of LIVE particles — the draw is always issued at the allocated maximum (spray 48, bursts 32, lines 14 on desktop). My scene walk found the top triangle consumer on BOTH tracks is a 16-instance mesh of a 2414-triangle geometry — 38,624 triangles submitted unconditionally every frame with `frustumCulled: false`, whether or not any of it is on screen. Total instanced triangles: 38,784 of the scene's 703k / 502k.
findings.whyMk8Wins: Not a visual difference — this one is invisible. But 38.6k triangles of always-on geometry plus max-count particle draws is real vertex work on the mobile GPU, and it is free to reclaim.
findings.fix: Two changes. (1) In raceParticles.js, track a live count per pool and set `mesh.count = liveCount` at the end of `update()` before returning — three respects `InstancedMesh.count` as the instance draw count, so idle frames cost one degenerate draw instead of 48/32/14. Keep `frustumCulled = false` (correct here, since these follow the player and a static bounding sphere would wrongly cull them). (2) For the 16x2414-triangle mesh (the coin/pickup field at ComebackCityThreeKartRace.jsx:4127-4135), replace `frustumCulled = false` with a correctly maintained bounding sphere: call `mesh.computeBoundingSphere()` after the last `setMatrixAt` and leave `frustumCulled = true`. The coin field is world-static, so its bounding sphere is valid and three will cull it whenever the row is behind the camera. If the 2414-triangle coin geometry is a smooth cylinder, decimate it to a 12-sided prism (~50 triangles) — at the on-screen size in comeback-city-p0_45 and penguin-village-p0_67 the difference is not resolvable.
